Fifteen such rollouts on 2026-07-28, all `codex-tui`. The single same-day
rollout carrying `originator: "orgasmic"` has `source: "vscode"` and a cwd
inside `task-69cw6/worktree/crates/...` — an editor session opened in a
worktree, not a dispatch.

Historically the value was `"orgasmic"` (306 rollouts store-wide, back to
2026-06-12), and it appears across every codex version present (0.139.0 through
0.144.5), as does `codex-tui`. **So this is not a codex version regression, and
the mechanism that used to produce `"orgasmic"` has not been identified.** That
is the first thing to establish, not to assume.

Reproduction, still failing at the time of filing:

```
$ orgasmic run native-transcript run-20260728T153658-0de705fc34fb42e4bd717517768638fe
"reason": "no codex rollout with session_meta.cwd == .../task-z8wej-review/worktree
           starting within PT300S after run start under /Users/aspirational/.codex"
"status": "not_found"

$ head -1 ~/.codex/sessions/2026/07/28/rollout-2026-07-28T18-36-59-019fa95f-....jsonl
  payload.cwd       == /Users/.../task-z8wej-review/worktree     <- exact match
  payload.timestamp == 2026-07-28T15:36:59.192Z                  <- run start 15:36:58
  payload.originator== "codex-tui"                               <- the only mismatch
```

Note the filename encodes local time (`18-36-59`) while the record encodes UTC
(`15:36:59Z`). The finder reads the record, not the filename, so this is *not*
the cause — but it will mislead anyone eyeballing the directory, and it misled
the manager for one step.

=== Why this is worse than one missing transcript

Codex emits no `NativeRuntime` lifecycle event (TASK-F9VEZ), so
`lookup.session_id` is `None` and the high-confidence
`find_codex_rollouts_by_session_id` path is unavailable. The cwd+originator scan
is the **only** remaining route, and this gate closes it. Codex runs therefore
have no reachable transcript by any path.

This is dec_WDR5K's sequencing constraint failing in substance: TUI screen
capture was removed on the premise that harness-native JSONL finders would
locate transcripts. For codex the finder finds nothing, so those runs have no
transcript at all — the same shape TASK-VB9DQ established for acp-stdio claude,
now confirmed for codex through a different mechanism.

=== Ask

1. Establish what actually sets `originator` and why it stopped for
   rmux-launched codex. Codex reads an originator override from its
   environment; determine the real name and whether orgasmic ever set it, or
   whether the historical `"orgasmic"` values came from a different launch path
   (acp-stdio) that reviewers no longer use. Report what you found — a wrong
   guess here produces a fix that passes tests and changes nothing in
   production.
2. Set it deliberately on every codex launch path, or stop requiring it. If
   orgasmic can stamp the originator, do that and keep the gate as a strong
   correlator. If it cannot, the gate must go — an unsettable discriminator is
   not a safety property, it is an outage. Do not simply widen the match to any
   originator without saying what now prevents mis-attribution to an operator's
   own codex session in the same directory.
3. The unit tests must stop constructing the value production cannot produce.
   Whatever fixture proves this path must be reachable from a real launch.

=== Acceptance

- A codex reviewer dispatched by the normal path has its transcript resolved by
  `orgasmic run native-transcript` — demonstrated on a real dispatch, not a
  fixture.
- Prove it by injection: break whatever now supplies the correlator, watch the
  new regression fail naming the run, restore, watch it pass.
- State explicitly what prevents matching an operator's own codex session
  started in the same worktree within the window.

=== Non-goals

- Do not implement codex `NativeRuntime` emission here; that is TASK-F9VEZ.
  This task must leave the cwd path working *without* a session id, because
  that is the situation it exists for.
- Do not change the claude or cursor-agent finders.

** Description
Cursor 2.0 ships =cursor-agent acp= — JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio implementing the Agent Client Protocol (https://cursor.com/docs/cli/acp, https://agentclientprotocol.com). Our current cursor wiring (=crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/cursor.rs=, 1486 lines) uses =--print --output-format stream-json= with manual prefix-dedup parsing and *post-hoc* tool-policy filtering — TASK-QSBDB's allowlist downgrades unsafe shell calls to telemetry AFTER the native shell tool already ran.

ACP gives us: typed turn lifecycle (=initialize=/=session/new=/=session/prompt= → =StopReason=), typed tool-call events (=kind ∈ read|edit|delete|move|search|execute|think|fetch|other=, =status ∈ pending|in_progress|completed|failed=), and crucially a *pre-execution* permission gate via =session/request_permission= that lets us map orgasmic's SandboxAllowlist semantics to ={allow_once, reject_once, ...}= and BLOCK unsafe calls before they run.

Add a =CursorAcpAdapter= mirroring the existing =adapters/claude.rs= ACP adapter (~962 LOC), register the =("acp-stdio","cursor-agent")= pair in =SUPPORTED= alongside the existing =("acp-stdio","claude")= and =("acp-stdio","codex")= entries, and ship a new =implementer-composer-acp= agent template cloning =implementer-composer.org=.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/cursor_acp.rs= implements =HarnessEventAdapter= with =stdio_spawn= returning the =cursor-agent acp= subprocess (auth via =CURSOR_API_KEY= env), =stdio_session_init= building =initialize= + =session/new= envelopes per the protocol spec, =parse_event= translating =session/update= variants (=plan=, =agent_message_chunk=, =tool_call=, =tool_call_update=) to =DriverEvent=, and =try_handle_approval= responding to =session/request_permission= using existing SandboxAllowlist semantics.
- [ ] =("acp-stdio", "cursor-agent")= pair added to =SUPPORTED= in =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/lib.rs=.
- [ ] Legacy alias =cursor-acp= → resolves to the new pair (sibling of the existing =cursor-agent= → =subprocess-stream-json= alias).
- [ ] =shipped/agent-templates/implementer-composer-acp.org= clones =implementer-composer.org= with =:DEFAULT_DRIVER: acp-stdio=, =:DEFAULT_HARNESS: cursor-agent=, =:KIND: implementer=.
- [ ] =StopReason::refusal= and =StopReason::max_turn_requests= map to a sensible =DriverEvent= (likely =RunFail= with a typed reason). Document the mapping inline.
- [ ] =session/cancel= wired to driver-side cancellation (replaces SIGKILL).

Reject unsafe calls with ={outcome:"selected", optionId:"reject_once"}=.

** Notes
- *Migration cost: small-to-medium.* Closest analogue is =adapters/claude.rs= (962 LOC). The =acp-stdio= mode runtime (=crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/acp_stdio.rs=, 793 LOC) and JSON-RPC handshake + approval dispatch (=crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/jsonrpc.rs=, 343 LOC) are already generic over the adapter and battle-tested by both claude and codex. (d) StopReason::refusal/max_turn_requests have no clean RunComplete/RunFail analogue.

only released when a manager ran `manager dispatch-close`, which releases
explicitly (`release_dispatch_run`, crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:627).

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A MISSING FEATURE

The rescue-policy convention is explicit that this is the daemon's job:

  "A failed agent run (protocol-end without terminal declaration, fatal driver
  error, stall / max-duration / idle timeout) ends after the daemon writes the
  authoritative release tombstone and, for dispatches, a
  manager.dispatch_orphaned tx."

So the intended sequence for a vanished worker is: daemon detects protocol-end
or stall, writes the Release tombstone with
`reason = protocol_end_without_finalize`, emits `manager.dispatch_orphaned`, and
only then does the manager choose a rescue action via `orgasmic run recover`.
None of that happened here. There was no orphan tx, and the manager had to
close the record for the run to go away.

Deliberately NOT the fix: adding an `orgasmic run release` verb. Release is not
a manager-authorized action in this model — `run recover` is — and a manual
release verb would paper over the daemon failing to write its own tombstone.

LIKELY ALREADY FIXED, NEEDS CONFIRMING

The running daemon is 0.0.15-dev.1 and predates f80b577,
"a declared failure ends the run instead of waiting for the harness" (TASK-TJKFC),
whose message says `terminal_event_releases_transport` allowlisted
`tmux | tmux-tui | rmux`, so on every OTHER transport a terminal event set the
outcome and released nothing, leaving release to stream end. acp-stdio is
exactly such an 'other transport'. That is a strong candidate for the whole
explanation.

So the first step is confirmation, not code: re-run this scenario on a daemon
built from current main — dispatch acp-stdio/claude, let the worker exit without
finalize, and check whether a Release tombstone and `manager.dispatch_orphaned`
appear on their own within the stall window. If they do, close this against
f80b577 with the evidence. If they do not, the stall detector is not reaching
this state at all and that is the bug.

Either way the observable acceptance is the same: a worker that exits without
finalize produces a daemon-written release tombstone and an orphan tx without
any manager action.

** Redesign note ([2026-05-28 Thu 15:05])
The initial shape of this task ([2026-05-28 Thu 14:48], shipped on branch =task-100-impl= commit =f386570=, NOT merged, discarded) was "make the driver turn_timeout configurable + bump default 600s → 1800s". User flagged the architectural error: a per-turn timeout in the driver is the wrong abstraction — it punishes long-but-active work (which is exactly what claude with extended thinking does). The supervisor and babysitter are the correct layers for "is the worker stuck or runaway?" judgement, not the driver. New shape replaces the driver timer entirely with two supervisor-level mechanisms.

** Description

TASK-ENXWA architector dispatch ([2026-05-28 Thu 11:35:13]) failed with =tmux TUI turn exceeded 600s without EOT marker= (=driver_error= fatal, seq 629) even though claude was actively producing — pane redraws at ~1s cadence, 32k tokens loaded, multiple tool calls, "Thought for 7m 8s" right before the timer fired and the supervisor released the run as failed.

Root cause is a layering error. The tmux driver at =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs:670-676= enforces a per-turn wall-clock deadline. Drivers shouldn't enforce time; they should just emit events. Stall detection and runaway protection are supervisor-layer concerns.

There are *three* mechanisms that should cover "is the worker still doing useful work?" — each at the right layer:

1. *Code-side stall detector* (NEW, supervisor): Per-run timer that resets on each driver_event. Fires if no driver_event arrives within a per-worker-configurable window. Default 600s (10 min). Universal across drivers (tmux / acp-stdio / cursor-stream-json / etc.) — not tmux-specific. Catches genuine wedges fast.

2. *Code-side wall-time backstop* (NEW, supervisor): Absolute per-run wall-clock ceiling. Fires when total run time exceeds a per-worker-configurable window. Default 14400s (4h). Pure safety net for runaway workers that fool the stall detector by emitting junk events forever. Should never fire in normal operation.

3. *LLM babysitter agent* (EXISTING, unchanged): The =babysitter-stall-detector= worker template (claude-sonnet-4-6 via claude-acp). Its persona handles slow quality-judging — repeated tool calls, no state transition in 10 min, garbage output → poke/escalate/restart. Polls every 50 events or 60s, much slower than the code stall_detector. NOT a fast stall mechanism; complements the code mechanism. Currently broken in production due to claude-acp simulated:true fallback (TASK-TGGAJ deferred); not fixing here.

The driver-side per-turn timeout is REMOVED entirely.

** Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] *Remove driver per-turn timeout.* In =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs=:
  - Delete the =turn_timeout: Option<Duration>= config field (~line 80).
  - Delete the =turn_timeout(&self) -> Duration= accessor with =unwrap_or(Duration::from_secs(600))= (~lines 104-106).
  - Delete the per-turn timer check (~lines 670-676) that fires =driver_error= with =tmux TUI turn exceeded {}s without EOT marker=.
  - Remove any related field on the inner runner struct (~lines 636, 644, 655, 670).
  - Update / remove dependent tests in the same file. The session-ending-before-EOT-marker test path (~line 1390) stays; it's about session lifecycle, not turn timeout.

- [ ] *Add code-side stall_detector to supervisor.* In =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs=:
  - Per-run state: =last_driver_event_at: Instant= (initialized at acquire time, updated on each driver_event observed for the run).
  - Periodic check (per-tick or per-event): if =Instant::now().saturating_duration_since(last_driver_event_at) > stall_timeout=, release the run with =outcome: failed, reason: "stall_timeout_exceeded"= and emit a lifecycle event identifying the threshold.
  - Resolution of the threshold per-run: take from the worker template's =:STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS:= if set; otherwise fall back to the built-in default =Duration::from_secs(600)=.

- [ ] *Add code-side max_run_duration backstop to supervisor.* In the same file:
  - Per-run state: =run_started_at: Instant= (may already exist on the lifecycle.acquire record; reuse if present).
  - Periodic check: if =Instant::now().saturating_duration_since(run_started_at) > max_run_duration=, release the run with =outcome: failed, reason: "max_run_duration_exceeded"=.
  - Resolution: per-worker =:MAX_RUN_DURATION_SECS:=, fallback =Duration::from_secs(14400)= (4h).

- [ ] *Worker template schema.* In =crates/orgasmic-core/src/workers.rs=:
  - Add optional integer property =:STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS:= → field =stall_timeout_secs: Option<u32>= on the Worker struct.
  - Add optional integer property =:MAX_RUN_DURATION_SECS:= → field =max_run_duration_secs: Option<u32>= on the Worker struct.
  - Mirror parsing pattern of existing optional integer properties (=:CONTEXT_BUDGET:=, =:MAX_ITERATIONS:=).

- [ ] *Plumb-through.* In =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/content.rs= and =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs=:
  - Add =stall_timeout_secs= and =max_run_duration_secs= fields on =WorkerView= and =StageWorker= structs.
  - Pass them through the existing field-passthrough sites (look at how =context_budget= flows).
  - Make sure the supervisor's acquire path can read these and store them on the per-run state.

- [ ] *Regression tests* (at least three):
  - Stall detector fires after the configured window: simulate no driver_event for >stall_timeout, assert release with =reason: "stall_timeout_exceeded"=.
  - Stall detector resets on driver_event: simulate driver_events at intervals shorter than stall_timeout for longer than stall_timeout, assert NO release.
  - Max run duration fires after the configured window: simulate a run that emits driver_events frequently (no stall trigger) but exceeds max_run_duration, assert release with =reason: "max_run_duration_exceeded"=.
  - (Bonus) Worker template parsing: a worker template with =:STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS: 7200= and =:MAX_RUN_DURATION_SECS: 86400= parses cleanly and the values flow to WorkerView.

- [ ] *No worker template overrides ship in this commit* — built-in defaults (600 stall / 14400 max_run_duration) apply universally to architector + claude-tmux + codex-acp + all others. Per-worker overrides can be added in a follow-up if/when production behavior reveals a need.

- [ ] *Gates clean*:
  - =cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon= (the new tests live here).
  - =cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers= (existing tmux tests minus the removed turn-timeout cases stay green).
  - =cargo test -p orgasmic-core --test fixtures= (org-parser-compat with the new optional properties).
  - =cargo test --workspace=.
  - =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings=.
  - =cargo fmt --check=.
  - =git diff --check=.
  - MSRV 1.78 honoured.

** Notes
- *Why this shape*: per-turn driver timeouts conflate "the driver hasn't heard from the worker in N seconds" with "the worker has been running for N seconds". The first is genuine stall (worker process is wedged or claude crashed); the second is normal claude behavior under extended thinking. Separating them into stall_detector (resets on events) + max_run_duration (absolute wall-clock) gives the right semantics for both.
- *Why universal across drivers*: stall_detector watches driver_events at the supervisor layer. All drivers emit driver_events. So the stall mechanism applies uniformly to tmux + acp-stdio + cursor-stream-json. No per-driver duplication.
- *Why don't we ship per-worker overrides*: the built-in defaults (600s stall, 4h backstop) work for everything we run today: codex-acp dispatches usually 5-15 min, claude-tmux on architector is bound by claude's own context window, etc. The override mechanism EXISTS in the schema (=:STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS:= and =:MAX_RUN_DURATION_SECS:= are parsed); we just don't set values on shipped workers. Operators can set them per-worker if/when a real need surfaces.
- *Cross-task interaction*: blocks TASK-ENXWA retry. With the driver timeout removed and the stall_detector resetting on each pane-redraw driver_event (which claude emits ~1s during active work), TASK-ENXWA architector will no longer abort spuriously.
- *Babysitter LLM separate concern*: the existing =babysitter-stall-detector= worker (currently broken because it routes via claude-acp / simulated:true per TASK-TGGAJ) is NOT touched here. When TASK-TGGAJ is un-deferred or the babysitter is migrated to claude-tmux/codex, it'll resume its slow-quality-judging role. Until then the code stall_detector + max_run_duration ceiling cover the safety floor.
- *Schema impact*: the org-parser-compat fixtures MUST stay green after both new optional properties are added. Existing worker templates without the new properties continue to parse and use built-in defaults.
- *Worker-name note*: dispatched via =implementer-codex-acp= (post-rename of the legacy =implementer-codex-stdio=; the alias from commit =0f30ec1= keeps both names resolving).

** Description
Reviewer F-1 MEDIUM from the TASK-HCFBT review (report at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-100-reviewer-report.md=):

In =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs::release_first_timed_out_run= (~line 1174), the function picks a timeout candidate under the =self.inner= lock, then DROPS the lock before calling =self.release(...)=. Between the drop and the release, a =DriverEvent= drain can acquire the same lock and refresh =last_driver_event_at=. But the monitor still proceeds with the release using the stale snapshot — issuing =reason: "stall_timeout_exceeded"= for a run that is, by the time of release, no longer stalled.

Same shape applies to =max_run_duration_exceeded= path (although less likely to be racy because =run_started_at= is set once at acquire and not updated by events).

This weakens the "resets on driver_event" guarantee at the timeout boundary. Symptom in production: occasional spurious stall releases on busy runs that JUST resumed activity.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Under the =inner= lock immediately before =release()=, re-check =timed_out_run(run_id, rec, now)= for the same =run_id= and the same =reason=. If the run no longer exceeds the threshold (=last_driver_event_at= was just updated), abort the release; the next monitor tick will reconsider.
- [ ] (Alternative shape, possibly cleaner): make the release conditional via the same critical section that selects the candidate — a helper that performs check + remove + release decision atomically under the lock.
- [ ] Update or add a regression test that injects a driver_event after candidate selection but before release; assert no release fires.
- [ ] cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon green; clippy + fmt + diff-check clean; MSRV 1.78.

** Notes
- *Smallest viable shape*: revalidate under the lock immediately before release. ~5-10 LOC change in =release_first_timed_out_run=.
- *Cross-task interaction*: TASK-ZG01H.1 (babysitter give-up no in-daemon recovery) is also a small =supervisor.rs= change. Both touch the same file but different functions — parallel-eligible but cleaner sequentially to avoid same-file merge resolution.

** Evidence
- *Implementer*: =implementer-codex-acp= via bundled supervisor cluster brief. Codex commit =59af464= ("supervisor.rs cluster: fix TOCTOU race + babysitter recovery + virtual-time test"). Merged no-ff as =5b11b4d=.
- *Fix shape*: =release_first_timed_out_run= now revalidates the same =run_id= and same =reason= under the =inner= lock immediately before calling =release()=. If the candidate is no longer timed out (a =DriverEvent= drain refreshed =last_driver_event_at= in the gap), or if the timeout-reason changed, abort the release and let the next monitor tick reconsider.
- *Regression test*: =supervisor::tests::stall_detector_revalidates_after_driver_event_race= (visible in cargo test output as ✓ ok) injects a driver_event into the gap between candidate selection and release; asserts no spurious release fires.
- *Gates on merged main =5b11b4d=*: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon ✓ (125 pass, including the new revalidation test) | cargo test --workspace ✓ (424 pass) | clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings ✓ | fmt ✓ | diff-check ✓ | MSRV 1.78.
- *Bundled with*: TASK-ZG01H.1 (babysitter give-up recovery, LOW) and TASK-HCFBT.2 (virtual-time integration test, LOW). All three in one commit since they touch different functions in the same file.

** Description
Reviewer F-2 LOW from the TASK-HCFBT review:

The four regression tests for the new stall_detector + max_run_duration mechanisms avoid real sleeps (good), but they manually backdate timestamps via the =age_run()= helper and call =sup.release_first_timed_out_run()= directly. They do NOT use =tokio::time::pause()= / =advance()=, and they do NOT exercise the =spawn_run_timeout_monitor()= interval task.

A broken monitor (wrong tick cadence, broken spawn, dropped task handle) would pass these tests as long as the private helper still works in isolation.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add at least one virtual-time test that:
  - Calls =Supervisor::with_summarizer= (which spawns the monitor task).
  - =tokio::time::pause()= to enter virtual time.
  - Acquires a run with a short stall_timeout (e.g., 100ms).
  - =tokio::time::advance(Duration::from_millis(150))= past the threshold.
  - Observes release via the monitor task — by polling supervisor state or by checking that the run is removed.
- [ ] Optionally add a sibling test for the max_run_duration path on the same virtual-time idiom.
- [ ] Keep the existing 4 tests as fast helper-targeted unit tests; the new virtual-time test(s) are integration-level.
- [ ] cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon green; clippy + fmt + diff-check clean; MSRV 1.78.

** Notes
- *Smallest viable shape*: one new virtual-time test; existing tests stay.
- *Why not delete the existing tests*: they're still useful as fast helper checks. The new test adds end-to-end coverage of the monitor task without replacing the helper checks.
- *Cross-task interaction*: parallel-eligible with TASK-HCFBT.1 but cleaner sequentially.

Pauses tokio time, advances past the configured stall_timeout, observes release via the monitor task (not by calling the private helper directly).
- *Cargo.toml change*: added =[dev-dependencies] tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["test-util"] }= so =tokio::time::pause()= / =tokio::time::advance()= / =#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]= compile under default =cargo test=. Workspace =tokio= already had =features = ["full"]=; feature unification gives the test build both =full= and =test-util= without polluting non-test builds.
- *Existing tests kept*: the prior 4 fast helper-targeted unit tests (=stall_detector_releases_after_no_driver_events=, =stall_detector_resets_on_driver_event=, =max_run_duration_releases_even_with_driver_events=, =worker_parses_run_timeout_properties=) all still pass. New virtual-time test is additive.
- *Gates on merged main =5b11b4d=*: same as TASK-HCFBT.1 evidence (one cluster commit covers all three fix-subtasks).
- *Bundled with*: TASK-ZG01H.1 + TASK-HCFBT.1.

** Description
Live dogfood discovery [2026-05-28 Thu 17:22:49]: TASK-HCFBT v2's new stall_detector misfired on a codex-acp dispatch. Forensics on the killed run (=run-20260528T134411-...=):

- Run acquired at 13:44:11Z.
- Codex was running =cargo test --workspace= which produced stdout that codex buffered for ~23 minutes.
- ZERO driver_events arrived at the daemon during that buffer window.
- stall_detector saw =Instant::now() - last_driver_event_at > 600s= at the 10-min mark.
- Supervisor released with =stall_timeout_exceeded= → SIGKILL.
- Right before SIGKILL, codex flushed its buffered stdout in a 8-event burst (seq 677-684 ALL at 14:22:22.254Z within milliseconds).

So codex WAS alive and working the whole time. The supervisor's mechanism IS correct (no driver_events arrived). The bug is that codex-acp doesn't emit anything during long-running subprocess tool calls — it batches stdout flushes.

claude-tmux doesn't have this problem because tmux pane redraws happen continuously during ALL claude activity (every ~1s — the "↓ Nk tokens" / elapsed-time counter in the pane footer alone updates).

**Pragmatic mitigation already shipped (in the same commit that files this task)**: =shipped/workers/implementer-codex-acp.org= + =shipped/workers/reviewer-codex-acp.org= got =:STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS: 7200= overrides (2h), using TASK-HCFBT v2's per-worker plumbing. This lets codex-acp dispatches run substantive workloads without spurious stall. But 2h is a band-aid — codex SHOULD emit heartbeats.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] codex-acp adapter (=crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/codex.rs= and/or =modes/acp_stdio.rs=) emits a heartbeat-style =driver_event= every ~30s while waiting for subprocess output to flush. The heartbeat should be a no-op semantically (no chunk content, just a "still alive" signal) but it MUST update =last_driver_event_at= on the supervisor's side so the stall_detector doesn't fire.
- [ ] Heartbeats don't pollute the run record's substantive view (i.e., they're filtered out of session JSONL stream that the manager reads for evidence, OR they have a distinct =type= that the manager UI can filter).
- [ ] Regression test: a unit test that constructs the codex-acp adapter, simulates a tool call taking >120s with no intermediate output, and asserts heartbeats are emitted at the expected cadence.
- [ ] After this lands, the =:STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS: 7200= overrides on codex-acp worker templates can be REMOVED (back to the built-in 600s default that works for claude-tmux). File TASK-HCFBT.4 to do that cleanup once heartbeats are proven.
- [ ] cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers green; cargo test --workspace green; clippy + fmt + diff-check clean; MSRV 1.78.

** Notes
- *Why a heartbeat is the right shape*: codex's ACP adapter already has an awareness of "I'm in a tool call, subprocess running". Emit a tiny periodic event from that state. Doesn't change codex's batching behavior for actual stdout content; just adds a liveness signal.
- *Heartbeat cadence*: 30s is a reasonable default. Too aggressive (5s) wastes overhead; too lazy (300s) doesn't actually help unless stall_timeout is bumped. With 30s heartbeats, a default 600s stall_timeout has 20 chances to reset.
- *Cross-task interaction*: parallel-eligible with the in-flight supervisor cluster (TASK-HCFBT.1 + TASK-ZG01H.1 + TASK-HCFBT.2) since this is a different crate (orgasmic-drivers, not orgasmic-daemon). After both land, the codex-acp worker overrides can be removed (file TASK-HCFBT.4).
- *Alternative considered + rejected*: subprocess-output forwarding (real-time stdout relay). Larger scope; affects all driver/harness pairs. Heartbeats are smaller + sufficient.

** Evidence
- *Closed*: [2026-06-05 Fri] by implementer-codex-acp.
- *Design — where the heartbeat lives*: the heartbeat is a new branch of the
  =run_acp_stdio= =tokio::select!= event loop in
  =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/acp_stdio.rs=. That loop is the production
  event pump for the codex-acp path (=implementer-codex-acp= →
  =:DRIVER: acp-stdio= + =codex= harness; see =shipped/workers/=). It owns the
  session lifetime, so a =tokio::time::interval= branch inside the same select
  shares the loop task's lifetime exactly — when the loop ends (release /
  terminal event / transport EOF), the interval is dropped with everything
  else. No detached =JoinHandle=, so no leaked ticker (handle-drop pitfall
  avoided by construction: the ticker is a select arm, not a spawned task).
- *Event shape*: added =DriverEvent::Heartbeat { seq }= in
  =crates/orgasmic-core/src/session.rs=. Snake_case serde tag ⇒ =type:
  "heartbeat"=, distinct from all substantive events. It carries no content;
  its only job is to flow through the supervisor's event drain, which sets
  =rec.last_driver_event_at = Instant::now()= for *every* drained event
  (variant-agnostic, supervisor.rs ~L632) before any terminal-outcome
  inspection. So a heartbeat resets the stall detector without releasing the
  lease (=terminal_outcome_for_event(Heartbeat) == None=).
- *Start/stop + cadence semantics*: =tokio::time::interval= at 30s
  (=HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL=); first (t=0) tick consumed so the first real heartbeat
  is one interval into a quiet stretch. =MissedTickBehavior::Delay=. A
  =quiet_since_last_tick= flag is cleared whenever the loop emits a real event
  (command / stderr / transport events); a heartbeat fires only on a tick where
  no real event occurred since the previous tick — so heartbeats appear *only*
  during genuinely-silent stretches and never interleave with active output.
  Cadence is overridable per-session via an optional =heartbeat_interval_ms=
  driver-config field (positive int; defaults to 30s when absent) — a tuning
  knob and the hook the regression test uses to run at 60ms.
- *Substantive-view filtering (AC2)*: distinct =type: "heartbeat"= ⇒ naturally
  excluded from every substantive surface, which match on specific string tags
  with catch-alls (evidence distillation + run-summary in
  =orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs=, manager-readable text/tool views). Belt-and-
  suspenders: =update_babysitter_buffer= early-returns on =Heartbeat= so it
  cannot inflate the babysitter summary window/count;
  =SubprocessExitSummary::record= ignores it via its existing catch-all.
- *Tests*:
  - =crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/driver_modes.rs::acp_stdio_codex_emits_heartbeats_during_quiet_turn=
    — a real =sh= mock codex peer completes the JSON-RPC handshake, starts a
    turn, then goes silent until =turn/interrupt=. At a 60ms cadence the test
    asserts ≥3 monotonic-seq heartbeats arrive during the quiet window and
    nothing else; after =release()= it asserts NO heartbeat arrives post-close
    (only the terminal =RunComplete=) and a final settle window confirms the
    ticker stopped (no leaked timer). Covers AC3 (quiet turn → cadenced
    heartbeats) and the stop-on-session-end requirement.
  - =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs::heartbeat_is_non_terminal_so_drain_never_releases_on_it=
    and =::heartbeat_does_not_pollute_babysitter_summary_window= — supervisor-
    side contract: heartbeat is non-terminal (resets but never releases) and is
    a no-op in the babysitter summary, while a following real event records
    cleanly.
- *Gate results*:
  - =cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers= → 73 (lib) + 23 (driver_modes) + 4/5
    (cursor_agent) pass; the one failure is
    =real_cursor_agent_stream_json_bridge_emits_events_and_releases= (TASK-AJZCK.2,
    pre-existing environmental: live =cursor-agent= auth timeout on this host).
    Log =/tmp/t100_3-drivers.log= + =/tmp/t100_3-dm.log=.
  - =cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon= → 124 + 22 + 56 pass, 0 failed (incl. both
    new heartbeat unit tests). =/tmp/t100_3-daemon.log=.
  - =cargo test -p orgasmic-core= → green. =/tmp/t100_3-core.log=.
  - =cargo test --workspace= → all suites green, 0 failed (the cursor smoke
    passed in this run). =/tmp/t100_3-workspace.log=.
  - =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= → clean.
    =/tmp/t100_3-clippy.log=. MSRV-1.78-safe (no post-1.78 std methods; used
    =Value::as_u64=, =tokio::time::interval=, plain combinators).
  - =cargo fmt --check= clean; =git diff --check= clean.
- *Files touched*: =crates/orgasmic-core/src/session.rs= (new =Heartbeat=
  variant); =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/acp_stdio.rs= (heartbeat select
  arm + =heartbeat_interval= config plumbing through =AcpStdioRuntime=);
  =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs= (=update_babysitter_buffer= skip +
  2 unit tests); =crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/driver_modes.rs= (regression
  test).
- *Follow-up filed*: TASK-HCFBT.4 (P3) — remove the =:STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS: 7200=
  overrides on =implementer-codex-acp.org= + =reviewer-codex-acp.org= after a
  validated live codex-acp dispatch confirms heartbeats hold the 600s default.
  NOT done here because it needs a live-dispatch proof, not just unit tests.
- *Reviewer pass*: [2026-06-05 Fri] static review of =834038f= (diff
  =984afc7..834038f=), read-only, no rebuild (gates verified green by
  implementer). Verdict: SHIP. All five acceptance criteria met; AC4 correctly
  deferred to TASK-HCFBT.4. Verified the core contract end-to-end: heartbeat is a
  select arm of =run_acp_stdio= (shares loop lifetime, no detached handle);
  supervisor drain sets =last_driver_event_at= variant-agnostically
  (supervisor.rs:632) and =terminal_outcome_for_event(Heartbeat)=None= (resets,
  never releases); =max_run_duration= is computed from =run_started_at=
  (supervisor.rs:1934-1977) so the 4h ceiling is unaffected by heartbeats;
  child-death closes the transport pipe → =recv_json Ok(None)= → loop break →
  heartbeats stop promptly (acp_stdio.rs:484,645); substantive surfaces
  (api.rs evidence distillation L3313, run-summary terminal scan L5373,
  ManagerChatTranscript.tsx, ws.rs pass-through,
  =SubprocessExitSummary::record=) all ignore =type:"heartbeat"= — UI drops

** Description
TASK-HCFBT.3 made the codex-acp adapter (=acp-stdio= mode) emit liveness
=DriverEvent::Heartbeat= events every ~30s during quiet turns, so the
supervisor's stall detector resets on genuine activity even while codex buffers
a long subprocess (e.g. =cargo test --workspace=). That removes the need for the
band-aid =:STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS: 7200= (2h) overrides shipped on the codex-acp
worker templates.

This task removes those overrides and returns codex-acp workers to the built-in
600s default — but ONLY after a real live codex-acp dispatch has demonstrated
that heartbeats actually hold a substantive (>10min quiet) run under the 600s
default. Do not close on unit tests alone; the whole point is to validate the
end-to-end daemon→adapter→supervisor heartbeat path in production.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [X] A live codex-acp dispatch runs a workload with a >10-minute quiet
  subprocess window (e.g. =cargo test --workspace= in a worktree) WITHOUT a

  =stall_timeout_exceeded= — confirmed by the run's session JSONL showing
  interleaved =type:"heartbeat"= events during the quiet window.

  =shipped/workers/implementer-codex-acp.org= and
  =shipped/workers/reviewer-codex-acp.org=.
- [X] clippy + fmt + diff-check clean (likely no =.rs= touched).

* DONE TASK-HCFBT.5 fix-subtask: heartbeat hardening — child.try_wait() liveness arm, recovery-counter heartbeat skip, interval floor :drivers:codex:acp:reliability:heartbeat:fix:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID:               TASK-HCFBT.5
:PRIORITY:         P3
:WRITE_SCOPE:      crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/acp_stdio.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/**
:TEST_CMD:         cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers; cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon
:END:

** Description
Bundles the three non-blocking findings from the TASK-HCFBT.3 reviewer pass
(verdict SHIP, =834038f=):

1. *(F1, medium)* The heartbeat select arm in =run_acp_stdio= gates liveness on
   transport EOF only. A codex peer wedged at the OS level with its stdout fd
   still open ticks heartbeats indefinitely, degrading stall detection for
   that case from ~600s to the 4h =max_run_duration= backstop. Add a
   =child.try_wait()= select/poll arm so a dead-or-exited child stops
   heartbeats even when the pipe lingers; regression test with a peer that
   exits while a sibling holds the pipe open.
2. *(F2, low)* The recovery mechanical-summary "driver events recorded"
   counter (api.rs:4751) blanket-counts heartbeats; skip =type=="heartbeat"=
   so long quiet runs don't over-report.
3. *(F3, low)* =heartbeat_interval_ms= rejects 0 but accepts 1ms (busy-spin
   risk); clamp to a documented floor (≥100ms) in the config plumbing.

** Evidence
F1 (child liveness): =run_acp_stdio='s heartbeat select arm now carries an
=if child_alive= guard and polls =child.try_wait()= on every tick *before*
emitting. =Ok(Some(_))= (exit) and =Err(_)= (status unknowable) both flip
=child_alive=false=, stopping heartbeats; the existing EOF / terminal /
command-close paths still reap the child via =child.wait()= at loop end (no new
release path). Regression test
=acp_stdio_heartbeats_stop_when_child_exits_with_pipe_held_open=: the mock peer
backgrounds a =sleep 5= that inherits stdout (pipe never EOFs) then exits its
main shell; the test asserts heartbeats flow while alive then go silent for
>5 cadence windows. Verified it TIMES OUT/FAILS when the =try_wait= gate is
stubbed to always-=Ok(None)=, and PASSES with the real gate. Cleanup reaps the
peer process group (=kill -- -PID=, pid==pgid via the existing =setsid=
=detach_subprocess=) with null stdio — no orphan leak (TASK-AJZCK.1 shape).

F2 (recovery counter): =build_recovery_prompt= (api.rs) now =continue=s on
=type=="heartbeat"= before incrementing =driver_events=, so the
"driver events recorded" mechanical-summary line no longer over-reports on long
quiet runs. Untyped driver events still count exactly as before (count moved out
of the =if let Some(ty)= so only heartbeats are excluded).

F3 (interval floor): added =HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_FLOOR= (100ms);
=heartbeat_interval()= clamps any configured =heartbeat_interval_ms= up to the
floor (=.max(FLOOR)=). The existing quiet-turn test moved 60ms→100ms (which

** Description
TASK-HJBXF live-dogfood found: =claude= TUI takes ~2-5s to render its banner + input field after =tmux new-session= spawns it. The driver's current code calls =paste_text_into_pane= immediately after =spawn_tmux_session= returns, which races claude's startup → prompt enters the void → claude sits at empty cursor forever.

Two viable fixes:
1. *Wait-for-input-prompt heuristic*: capture-pane periodically (~250ms) after spawn; detect claude's prompt indicator (=❯ = at the start of a line, or => = for older claude versions) → only then paste. Add ~10s timeout fallback (if no prompt detected, log warning + paste anyway).
2. *Sleep-after-spawn*: simpler but less robust — =sleep 3-5s= after spawn before paste. Works for claude today but brittle if claude TUI startup gets slower or faster.

Reference HAR app (=../har/=) likely solves this — read =../har/crates/har-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs= or equivalent for the proven pattern.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Driver waits for claude's input field to be ready before pasting prompt.
- [ ] If no input field detected after timeout (~10s default), log warning + paste anyway (don't block forever).
- [ ] Inline test: mock-peer that takes >1s to render its prompt; driver still successfully pastes.
- [ ] Real-wire smoke test (gated on =which tmux && which claude=) confirms the fix.
- [ ] All gates green.

** Evidence
- *Implementer pass merged as =823be91= (codex =dae58c3=, ~18 min wall, clean codex dispatch — no rescue needed for the codex side).* +164/-1 LOC across 2 files. New helper =wait_for_input_ready(session, timeout)= polls =capture_pane= every 250ms until prompt indicator (line starting with =❯= or => = followed by whitespace) appears OR =DriverError::InputNotReady(timeout)= fires. Acquire path calls it ONLY when =spawn_plan.command == "claude"=. On timeout, logs warning + pastes anyway. Real-world detail caught by codex: claude v2.1.153 uses NBSP (U+00A0) after =❯=, not ASCII space → detection uses generic =char::is_whitespace=. Inline tests: =wait_for_input_ready_returns_ok_when_mock_pane_has_prompt= + =wait_for_input_ready_returns_input_not_ready_on_timeout= + =pane_has_input_prompt_detects_claude_indicators= + =real_claude_input_ready_smoke= (gated on which tmux + claude). Configurable knob =TmuxTuiConfig.input_ready_timeout= default 10s.
- *Manager 2-line follow-up patch (this commit) restores 800ms settle-sleep for NON-claude commands.* Codex's diff inadvertently dropped the existing =tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(800)).await= that gated the paste path for the entire acquire loop, replacing it with a claude-only =wait_for_input_ready= branch. =real_tmux_prompt_bundle_is_consumed= (which uses =cat= as a mock TUI without a =❯= prompt) became flaky → race-dependent ordering between Ready emission and TextChunk emission from cat's instant stdout echo. Fix: when =command != "claude"=, sleep 800ms before paste (mirrors pre-TASK-HJBXF.1 behavior). 57/57 driver lib tests pass post-patch.
- *Gates on merged main =823be91= + manager patch:* cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers --lib (57 passed) ✓; cargo test --workspace ✓ (1 failure pre-patch — see manager note); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings ✓; cargo fmt --check ✓; git diff --check ✓.
- *Lesson learned*: =cargo test 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "exit: $?"= captures tail's exit code, NOT cargo's. Use =set -o pipefail= or check =${PIPESTATUS[0]}= for the leftmost-pipe exit code in future gate runs. Logged for housekeeping.

** Description
Real-tmux integration tests (=real_tmux_prompt_bundle_is_consumed=, =real_tmux_session_lifecycle=, etc.) leave orphan tmux sessions named =orgasmic-run-prompt-real-<uuid>= after the test completes. The test calls =s.control.release("done")= but evidently the release path doesn't fully kill the tmux session under test isolation, OR the test ends before async cleanup completes.

Manager housekeeping during the TASK-HJBXF.2 dogfood found 3 such orphans accumulated from various test runs.

Fix: either (a) ensure =DriverSession::Drop= or explicit cleanup tears down the tmux session synchronously, or (b) use =std::process::Command::new("tmux").args(["kill-session", "-t", session_name])= as a final guard in each test's cleanup block.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Real-tmux tests don't leave orphan sessions after =cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers --lib modes::tmux= run.
- [x] Mock-peer + non-tmux tests unaffected.
- [x] All gates green.

** Evidence
- *Date*: [2026-06-05 Fri].
- *Fix shape*: added a =SessionGuard(String)= Drop-guard struct to the tmux test module that calls the existing =kill_tmux_session_sync= on drop. Each real-tmux test that spawns a session now binds =let _guard = SessionGuard(tmux_session_name(&s.identity));= (or the explicit session name for =real_claude_input_ready_smoke=) immediately after spawn — so the session is killed unconditionally on success, assert-failure unwind, or panic. Tests covered: =real_tmux_session_lifecycle=, =real_claude_input_ready_smoke=, =real_tmux_eot_marker_emits_run_complete=, =real_tmux_early_exit_before_eot_is_failure=, =real_tmux_prompt_bundle_is_consumed= (the named orphan source), =real_tmux_attach_proves_existing_session=. =real_tmux_control_drop_without_release_kills_session= left unguarded by design (it asserts the driver's own Drop cleanup). =kill-session= is a no-op when the session already exited.

* DONE TASK-HQ970 tx record accepts a multi-line --reason and bricks the append-only ledger :tx:data-integrity:defect:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-HQ970
:PRIORITY: P1
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-core
:END:

`orgasmic tx record --reason "<multi-line text>"` writes the newlines verbatim
into the org property drawer, returns success with a tx_id, and leaves the
append-only ledger unparseable. Every subsequent CLI read fails, so no verb —
including the ones you would use to repair it — can run. The only way out is a
hand-edit of the file the manager is forbidden to hand-edit.

REPRODUCED [2026-07-26], not inferred. `orgasmic tx record --type manager.action
--project orgasmic --task TASK-D0GA3 --reason "$(cat multi-line-file)"` returned

    {"tx_id": "tx-20260726-orgasmic-2973", "tx_path": ".orgasmic/tx/2026-07.org"}

and the next command failed with

    Error: parse .orgasmic/tx/2026-07.org
    Caused by: ...:29850: malformed property drawer entry: blank line inside
    property drawer

The remaining `--extra KEY=VALUE` properties were appended AFTER the injected
prose, so they landed outside the drawer too. A second, subtler failure mode:
once the blank lines were removed the parser then rejected the entry with "tx
entry has trailing content after property drawer" — tx entries are drawer-only
and carry no body at all, which is not stated anywhere in `tx record --help`.

BLAST RADIUS. The write is accepted, so a manager has no signal until the next
read. Both ledgers were hit in one session: the project ledger and, because
`tx record` is not project-scoped by default (TASK-HXSW0 instance 6),
`$ORGASMIC_HOME/state/tx/2026-07.org` as well. A daemon that cannot parse its
tx file cannot dispatch, cannot close, cannot update a task.

THREE SEPARATE DEFECTS, all in this one path:
1. No validation. A value containing a newline must be rejected at the API
   boundary with a clear error, before anything is written.
2. No atomicity or verification. The writer should re-parse what it produced
   before reporting success — a ledger that only accepts what it can read back
   cannot be bricked by its own writer.
3. No documented body support. If long prose belongs in a tx (and
   `tx-scannable-bodies` implies it does), the entry format needs a body region
   the parser accepts, or `--reason` needs to be documented as single-line and
   the convention corrected.

Acceptance:
- `tx record --reason` with an embedded newline fails with a clear message and
  writes nothing
- a tx write that would not round-trip through the parser is rejected rather
  than committed
- `tx record --help` states the single-line constraint, or a body region exists
  and is tested with multi-paragraph prose
- a regression test asserts the ledger still parses after each supported write
SIBLING FILED [2026-07-28]: TASK-ZYWZD applies this task's defect-2 principle (a writer must not commit what it cannot read back) to the node body surface, where `node body set` silently truncated TASK-ATAXN to 300 of 3959 chars. If either fix grows shared compose->re-parse->refuse machinery, use it for both.

* DONE TASK-HXSW0 Make the CLI self-documenting for agents: real help per verb and flag, no silent no-ops, a drivers listing verb :cli:agent-ergonomics:docs:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-HXSW0
:PRIORITY:    P1
:END:

Filed 2026-07-26 after a session in which the manager guessed wrong CLI verbs
four times, and one shipped convention was found instructing a hallucination.

The operator framing, which sets the constraint: fix this with better CLI help
that agents are told to consult, NOT by pasting a command cheat sheet into every
prompt. Prompt space is scarce and a stale cheat sheet is worse than none.

MEASURED FAILURES, all from one session

1. `orgasmic manager drivers` does not exist in any command group — and
   `shipped/prompt-studio/conventions/manager-dispatch.org` instructed the
   manager to run it to choose `--mode`/`--harness`. The valid pairs live only in
   `orgasmic_drivers::SUPPORTED` (crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/lib.rs:74) with no
   CLI surface at all. The convention was corrected the same day, but the
   underlying gap stands: the one fact needed on EVERY dispatch has no listing
   verb. The only discovery path is to submit a bogus pair and read the
   rejection, which does helpfully name all sixteen.
2. `orgasmic task show` — guessed repeatedly. The real verb is `task get`, and
   listing lives in a SEPARATE top-level group, `tasks list`. A singular/plural
   split where both exist and neither mentions the other is a hallucination
   generator.
3. `orgasmic run release` — a prior manager asserted it existed, corrected
   itself in the handoff, and the correction itself was then wrong. Two wrong
   records about one nonexistent verb.
4. `orgasmic worker list` — guessed, does not exist.

5. WORST CLASS — a silent no-op on a write verb.
   `orgasmic task update TASK-X --property "WRITE_SCOPE=..." --property
   "TEST_CMD=..."` returned `{"changed":{"STATE":"in_progress"}}` and dropped
   both properties without a word. The same call with lowercase `write_scope`
   and `test_cmd` worked. An unrecognised property key must be an error: a write
   verb that reports success while discarding two of three arguments is worse
   than a missing feature, because the caller has no reason to re-check.

6. Flags on the primary agent verb have NO help text. `orgasmic manager dispatch
   --help` renders `--task <TASK>`, `--kind <KIND>`, `--brief <BRIEF>`,
   `--from <FROM>`, `--model <MODEL>`, `--effort <EFFORT>`, `--worktree`,
   `--branch`, `--reason` with blank descriptions. An agent cannot learn from
   that whether `--from` is a git ref or a path, or that `--worktree-remove`
   on `dispatch-close` defaults to TRUE and force-deletes uncommitted work
   (TASK-2BPWM).

WHAT ALREADY WORKS, and should be the template

Two errors in the same session were excellent and cost zero follow-up:
- `manager dispatch` from the wrong lifecycle: "task TASK-X is in lifecycle
  stage in_progress; implementer dispatch is allowed only from BACKLOG or TODO"
  — names the rule and the allowed set.
- `node body append --section Evidence` on a node lacking it: "no section
  \"Evidence\"; sections: [] (use `set --section` to create one via add)" —
  names the fix verb.
Contrast `node body append gotchas ...` → "glossary file not found", which names
the wrong file entirely (already a recorded gotcha).

WORK

1. Give every command and every flag a one-line description that says what it
   does and what it returns. Blank `#[arg]` descriptions on agent-facing verbs
   should be treated as a bug, not a style nit.
2. State destructive defaults in the help text where the operator reads them,
   not only in the code.
3. Make unrecognised `--property` keys a hard error listing accepted keys.
   Audit for other silent-drop paths in the same shape.
4. Add a real listing verb for mode/harness pairs, sourced from
   `orgasmic_drivers::SUPPORTED` so it cannot drift.
5. Make near-miss verbs self-correcting: an unknown subcommand should suggest
   the real one (`task show` -> `task get`; `worker list` -> ?) and cross-
   reference the singular/plural split between `task` and `tasks`.
6. Audit shipped prompts and conventions for commands that do not exist. One was
   found by accident; nobody has checked the rest. A test asserting that every
   `orgasmic ...` invocation appearing in `shipped/**` parses against the real
   clap surface would make this class permanently impossible.

Item 6 is the highest-leverage item here — it converts "an agent hallucinated"
into a build failure.

Acceptance:
- an agent can discover any verb and flag it needs from `--help` alone, in at
  most three calls, without reading Rust source
- no write verb silently ignores an argument
- every command string in shipped prompts/conventions is checked against the
  real CLI surface by a test
- mode/harness pairs are listable
CONFIRMED INSTANCE, found while filing these very tasks [2026-07-26].

`orgasmic task create` has no `--priority` flag at all. Every task filed this
session used `--property "priority=P1"` on create, which was accepted silently
and discarded. ALL SEVEN tasks created today came out with priority None:
TASK-099T6, TASK-A55J7, TASK-VSWZT, TASK-S2KM0, TASK-6FNAY, TASK-2BPWM,
TASK-HXSW0. They were repaired afterwards with `task update --priority`, which
does have a real flag and works.

This sharpens item 3 beyond "unknown property keys should error". Two distinct
defects compose here:

1. The property allowlist differs between `create` and `update`. `update`
   accepts `--priority` as a first-class flag; `create` accepts neither the flag
   nor the property. The same field is settable, unsettable, or silently ignored
   depending on which verb you reach for.
2. The silent drop makes the divergence invisible. `create` returned a normal
   success object with `id` and `tx_id` and no indication that an argument had
   been thrown away.

The result is a whole session of P1 work filed as unprioritised, which is exactly
the kind of state error that later reads as "nobody triaged this" rather than
"the CLI dropped it".

Note the failure is silent in BOTH directions worth testing: an unknown key
(`WRITE_SCOPE` uppercase, dropped) and a known-but-unsupported-on-this-verb key
(`priority` on create, dropped). Fixing only the first would leave this case
intact.

TWO MORE CONFIRMED INSTANCES [2026-07-26], both found while filing a fix subtask.

4. `task create` accepts and silently discards property keys that `task update`
   accepts and persists. Reproduced on TASK-D0GA3: the same
   `--property "PARENT_TASK=TASK-2BPWM" --property "FIX_SUBTASK=t"` pair was
   dropped by `create` (drawer contained only ID, PRIORITY, TEST_CMD,
   WRITE_SCOPE) and then written verbatim by `update`, whose response echoed both
   keys under "changed". PRIORITY, TEST_CMD and WRITE_SCOPE survived `create` in
   the same invocation, so this is a per-key filter on create, not a general
   restriction. The user-visible effect is that the same command produces
   different state depending on which verb you happen to use.

5. `:PARENT_TASK:` is never read by anything. `parent_task` is derived purely
   from the id grammar — `derive_task_parent_id` (crates/orgasmic-core/src/id.rs:319)
   splits `TASK-<stem>.<digits>` and returns `TASK-<stem>`. So the property is
   accepted by `update`, stored in the drawer, echoed as changed, and ignored by
   every reader. `orgasmic task get TASK-D0GA3` still reports
   `parent_task: null` with `:PARENT_TASK: TASK-2BPWM` sitting in the file.

   This one had a downstream cost: the shipped `manager-dispatch` convention
   instructed managers to file fix subtasks with a `:PARENT_TASK:` back-edge, so
   the documented mechanism produced no edge at all. Corrected in the convention
   the same day — parentage must be minted into the id as `TASK-<parent>.N`.

The pattern across all five instances is one defect: `--property` is an untyped
passthrough with no schema, so every layer is free to accept, store, filter or
ignore a key independently, and every combination reports success. The fix is not
five special cases. It is (a) validate keys against the schema at write time and
reject unknown or miscased ones with a message naming the correct key, and
(b) make `create` and `update` accept the same set, or say why they differ.

INSTANCE 6 [2026-07-26]. `orgasmic tx record` is the only mutation verb that is
NOT project-scoped by default. Without `--project`, it writes to
$ORGASMIC_HOME/state/tx/YYYY-MM.org — the global home file — and reports success
with a differently-shaped tx id (tx-20260726192932-05e34dce) rather than the
project's tx-20260726-orgasmic-NNNN. Every sibling verb (`task update`, `node
body append`, `task create`) resolves the project from the cwd and needs no
flag. The help text for --tx-path says "defaults to $ORGASMIC_HOME/state/tx/
YYYY-MM.org", which is accurate and is the only warning you get; nothing in
`tx record --help` suggests --project is load-bearing.

Cost: one manager.action for TASK-D0GA3 was written to the home tx file and had
to be re-recorded with --project. The stray entry is still there. A manager
following the obvious invocation silently loses every tx it records off the
project ledger and cannot tell from the exit code.

Fix direction: default `tx record` to the cwd project like its siblings, and
keep --project / --tx-path as explicit overrides.

** Description
The =acp-stdio= driver mode spawns =codex app-server= as a subprocess (auto-spawn shipped in TASK-RF3J1.1 via HAR pattern) but never drives it over JSON-RPC. As a result every dispatch routed through =implementer-codex-stdio= / =reviewer-codex-stdio= idles: codex app-server reads nothing from stdin, never receives =initialize= / =thread/start= / =turn/start=, and the orgasmic daemon eventually marks the run as stuck (TASK-J95T2 early-exit classifier was added precisely because this gap kept jamming the supervisor pipeline). Workaround for the last ~3 weeks: route every dispatch through the working =implementer-cursor= / =reviewer-cursor= path (cursor-agent CLI + subprocess-stream-json driver).

Closing this gap unlocks two things:

1. *On-rail codex dispatches*: =--worker implementer-codex-stdio= becomes a usable choice in =orgasmic manager dispatch=; reviewer-codex-stdio can run reviewer passes. Removes the "cursor-agent only" footgun.
2. *UI real-time agent chat* (TASK-C7ZG5 follow-up): user direction this session — "user can via task dialog (ui) click the current agent status to open the chat with the running agent and in real time monitor the session via the same chat interface as manager uses in har app for acp driver type". The chat UX only makes sense over a real ACP wire, so this task is its enabler.

Concrete code-level diagnosis (the implementer brief expands on each):

- =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/acp_stdio.rs= today is just a compose-adapter wrapper that hands work to =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver=. It spawns the binary correctly but =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver::run_subprocess_stream_json= treats stdout as line-delimited stream-json and calls =adapter.parse_stdout_line(&line)= for each line. The =HarnessEventAdapter::parse_stdout_line= default deserialises one JSON value per line and delegates to =parse_event= — so codex notifications WOULD route through =CodexAdapter::parse_event= correctly if codex were already in a session. But nothing sends the JSON-RPC requests (=initialize=, =thread/start=, =turn/start=) that get codex into that state, and the adapter's control surface (=transition_state=, =babysitter_action=, =release=) emits =WireMessage::JsonRpc { method, params }= values that the subprocess driver also has no codepath to send.
- =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/acp_ws.rs::run_acp_ws= is the closest analog: it implements exactly this JSON-RPC client lifecycle (request_response → on_ws_thread_started → ws_turn_start_params → loop driving =parse_event= against incoming notifications + handling control wire-messages). It just happens to do so over a WebSocket. The natural refactor is either: (a) factor =request_response= / =handle_outcome= / =RpcIds= into a transport-agnostic helper that both =acp_ws.rs= and a new =acp_stdio.rs= runtime can drive, or (b) duplicate the loop in =acp_stdio.rs= and reach for the shared helper later — implementer's call based on how clean the abstraction comes out.

Note: =codex app-server= speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC on its stdio (HAR convention), not LSP-style Content-Length framing. Confirm by spawning it locally — but assume newline-delimited unless evidence otherwise.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =acp-stdio= mode drives a real JSON-RPC client lifecycle when the harness adapter's =compose_request= returns a =HarnessRequest::Subprocess= (today's path) AND the adapter's =stdio_initial_payload= surface is enough to seed the session:
  - sends an =initialize= request, waits for response,
  - sends =thread/start= with the params from the adapter's session_init shape (or a new adapter method — see "Open implementation choices" below) and routes the result through =adapter.on_ws_thread_started(endpoint, response)= so =CodexAdapter= can record the thread id and emit =Ready=,
  - sends =turn/start= with =adapter.ws_turn_start_params()= and feeds the result through =adapter.on_ws_response("turn/start", value)=,
  - loops reading notifications from stdout (one JSON-RPC value per line) and feeds each through =adapter.parse_event(value)=,
  - dispatches control =WireMessage::JsonRpc { method, params }= writes to stdin (one JSON-RPC envelope per line) when =transition_state= / =babysitter_action= / =release= produce them,
  - detects terminal events (=adapter.terminal_emitted() = true= after =turn/completed= / =thread/closed=) and shuts down cleanly.
- [ ] The "endpoint" parameter for =on_ws_thread_started= is replaced with a transport-neutral identifier (e.g., the path-or-binary the subprocess was spawned as) so the same =CodexAdapter::on_ws_thread_started= works for both acp-ws and acp-stdio without lying about the URL. If renaming the trait param crosses too many call sites, document the carry-over in the brief.
- [ ] A new fixture-style integration test in =crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/driver_modes.rs= (or a sibling) that pairs an =AcpStdioDriver= against a mocked codex peer (e.g., a child process running a tiny Rust helper or a python one-liner that reads JSON-RPC requests from stdin and writes scripted responses + notifications) and asserts the same envelope shape the existing acp-ws fixture asserts: =Ready { simulated: false, thread_id: ... }= → =TextChunk { Assistant, "hello" }= → =ToolCall { transition_state }= → =RunComplete=. Real-binary verification with =codex app-server= itself is allowed but not required (codex CLI may not be on CI). If the helper-process approach is too fiddly, an in-process =tokio::io::DuplexStream= mock that gets handed to a refactored "run_acp_stdio over arbitrary AsyncRead/AsyncWrite" function is also acceptable — implementer's call.

If codex isn't on PATH, document the constraint in the Evidence section and rely on the mock-peer fixture for correctness.

** Description
Closes 3 of 5 TASK-HY0QT reviewer findings (F-1, F-2, F-3). F-4 + F-5 reviewer-deferred (can piggyback if cheap; otherwise ship deferred).

The TASK-HY0QT implementation introduced =run_acp_stdio= as a parallel runtime to =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver=, but in doing so dropped two subprocess-lifecycle properties that TASK-J95T2 specifically went to the trouble of shipping for the cursor-agent / claude-stream-json path:

- *F-1 missing exit synthesis*: =run_acp_stdio= ends the runtime loop and calls =child.wait()= but never invokes =finalize_subprocess_exit= (or an analog). If =codex app-server= dies before emitting =turn/completed= / =thread/closed= — crash, OOM, SIGKILL, network hiccup, whatever — the supervisor sees an open run with no terminal event. This is exactly the failure mode TASK-J95T2's =cursor::distill_subprocess_exit_summary= + synthetic =RunComplete= path was built to prevent on the cursor-agent side.
- *F-2 no kill on channel drop*: When all =AcpStdioControl= senders drop (supervisor crash, early-detach, abrupt session shutdown), =commands.recv()= returns =None= and the runtime breaks WITHOUT calling =child.kill()=. The legacy =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver= treats channel-close as a release signal and kills the child before finalising. Without that, a dropped session can leave a detached =codex app-server= orphan.
- *F-3 control-plane untested*: The new fixture =acp_stdio_codex_jsonrpc_handshake_mock_peer= exercises the read-side handshake (=initialize= → =thread/start= → =Ready= → notification stream → =RunComplete=) but never calls =session.control.release(...)= / =transition_state(...)= / =babysitter_action(...)= to assert that =HarnessControlOutcome.wire_messages= (e.g., codex =turn/interrupt=, =turn/steer=) get serialised to stdin as JSON-RPC envelopes. This was one of the three stacked failures the TASK-HY0QT brief identified pre-merge (failure mode B: wire-message control plane was silent); the write path is implemented via shared =handle_outcome= but has no regression test on the stdio side.

Reviewer report at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-077-review-report.md=.

ENTRY 1 dead_pid_aborts_joins_hung_producer_then_receiver_releases — FIXED.
Root cause is not the load. Measured ALONE on an idle machine, the test took
10.08s against its own 12s assertion, a 1.19x margin: HungProducerDriver hangs
in BOTH halves of the driver stop (HungReleaseControl::release is pending(),
the producer parks 6s), so stop_and_join_driver_producer spends
DRIVER_RELEASE_TIMEOUT twice. Both hangs are load-bearing — they are the only
way to reach the abort path the test is named for — so the fix injects the
budget instead of removing the hangs: a driver_release_timeout cell on
Supervisor with a #[cfg(test)] setter, mirroring TASK-HAREX's
set_release_drain_budget, compressed to 150ms. Test cost 10.08s -> 0.44s.
Compressing it alone flipped the asserted release to `early-exit subprocess
with no work envelopes`, which exposed a second latent defect: the terminal
event both HungProducerDriver tests are named after ("racing terminal") landed
inside the join window only because that window happened to be [5s, 10s]. It is
now emitted from release(), at the moment the forced stop begins, for any
budget. The sibling timeout_aborts_joins_hung_producer_then_drains_racing_terminal
shares the fixture and got the same compression; it asserts no wall clock and
was never flaky, but it cost the suite 10s per run.

Composition with TASK-HAREX: none of this fights DrainGate. The gate arms on
begin_explicit_release and would fire at RELEASE_DRAIN_BUDGET; the channel now
closes on the real producer abort ~300ms in, so the drain still ends on stream
closure and the gate is never reached. The test's release reason
(`driver stream closed`) proves that — a gate-bounded drain would not produce it.

ENTRY 3 replacement_start_waits_out_a_shutting_down_predecessor — FIXED, two
modes. Mode A (the reported one, `waited 1.50062225s, its own whole shutdown
budget`): the replacement's ceiling is the marker's DRAIN + 2*TAIL and TAIL was
100ms, so the whole margin was the ~375ms head start against a 1200ms drain
enforced by a timer. TAIL is now 2s. That is not a tolerance bump on the term
under test: graceful_shutdown passes release_drain to wait_idle and
writer_shutdown to shutdown_within, both ceilings that return the moment their
subject is idle, and this predecessor has no release in flight and a quiet
writer — so the predecessor's real cost is unchanged and the test still runs in
1.53s while the replacement can absorb ~4.3s of overrun. Mode B surfaced only
after mode A was fixed, in this task's own post-fix runs:
`the predecessor published its departure`, lib.rs:1808, 1/12. The test read the
shutdown marker once behind a fixed 250ms sleep, but publish_shutdown_marker
runs on the daemon's shutdown task — that line asserted the host had scheduled a
task in 250ms. It now waits for the marker, with the original liveness assertion
as the loop's failure exit.

A/B, four concurrent copies at --test-threads=64, 12 runs per arm:
  entry 1        pre 10/12 red -> post 0/12
  entry 3 mode A pre  1/12 red -> post 0/12
  entry 3 mode B      1/12 red (post-A tree) -> 0/12 after mode B fix
Both also green in 12 sequential runs and 6 runs under 10 cpu hogs.

Proofs: verify/TASK-J1XCB (both wall-clock modes) and verify/TASK-J1XCB-marker

loaded runs. The captured panic is now complete, and the clause the original

home`. api.rs:24818 in the tree of the original sighting (be3408ce) resolves to

guessed — port 0 only makes the refusal certain once classification is reached.

is a fresh tempdir per iteration; nothing outside acquire_daemon_lock opens

** Description
Bundle of three daemon-dispatch-polish fixes. All surfaced live this session (TASK-M5JTN reviewer F-2 + TASK-M5JTN.1 stuck-dispatch incident + TASK-PYW86 chrome smoke side finding). Bundled rather than three separate dispatches because all overlap on the daemon dispatch/run lifecycle code paths and a single coherent change is cheaper than three sequential round-trips.

*Item 1 — cursor-agent driver synthetic run_complete on subprocess exit (was TASK-M5JTN.2 / supersedes it).* TASK-M5JTN reviewer F-2: Item 1's path (c) "system fallback after assistant accumulation" produces noisy last.txt on live implementer-cursor dispatches (composer-2.5-fast emits 500+ raw thinking deltas with =stream: system= and no terminal event). Path (a) — the cursor-agent driver synthesizes a =DriverEvent::RunComplete { summary }= on clean subprocess exit when no real terminal was emitted — is the architecturally correct fix. Reviewer confirmed feasibility: =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/cursor.rs= already has =terminal_emitted=, =emit_run_complete_once=, =translate_result=; =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/subprocess_stream_json.rs= currently emits nothing on successful exit when =!terminal_emitted()= (lines 276-286).

*Item 2 — daemon run-lifecycle classifier early-exit detection (was TASK-T3NWN candidate).* Surfaced live this session during the first TASK-M5JTN.1 dispatch attempt. When cursor-agent subprocess dies after only 2 envelopes (=lifecycle::acquire= + =driver_event::ready=) — e.g., spawned with a bad CLI invocation race — the daemon's run-lifecycle classifier leaves the run stuck "active" and refuses =/runs/.../release= with =active run= error. Required daemon restart to clear the lock. Need: detect this early-exit pattern (subprocess exited + only N envelopes with no work envelope) within a short window (~10s) and auto-release the lease so subsequent dispatches don't 409 Conflict.

*Item 3 — hung task-detail endpoint (was TASK-NGDNP candidate).* Surfaced during TASK-PYW86 chrome smoke (two turns ago): =GET /projects/:valid_project_id/tasks/:invalid_task_id= hangs (>4s timeout, no response). Compare =GET /projects/<missing>/tasks/<id>= returns 404 in ~7s. Likely the task-detail handler does a synchronous file read (or task-graph lookup) with no NotFound short-circuit on the invalid task_id path. Need: return 404 quickly for unknown task ids on valid projects.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *Item 1 (synthetic run_complete)*:
  - In =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/subprocess_stream_json.rs= (or =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/cursor.rs=, depending on architectural fit), synthesize a =DriverEvent::RunComplete { summary }= when: (i) subprocess exits with status 0, (ii) no terminal session marker (=RunComplete=, =Lifecycle::Release=) has been emitted, (iii) some content was accumulated during the run. Summary = accumulated assistant text if available, otherwise the trailing N system chunks (consistent with =dispatch_last_summary_from_session= precedence).
  - The synthetic emission MUST NOT fire when a real terminal event has already arrived. Use the existing =terminal_emitted= flag.

* DONE TASK-JGHNC Seven tmux-gated daemon tests accept the rmux shim and have been measuring rmux while reporting tmux
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-JGHNC
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

From TASK-K4G1D (2026-07-29), measured, not inferred: inside an orgasmic
worker, `tmux` on PATH is the rmux shim, and a `-L`-pinned call through the
shim creates an RMUX server (the socket lands in /private/tmp/rmux-501/, and
the real tmux cannot connect to it). The 0RCRY owned-server mechanism does not
protect against this — the isolation holds, but the multiplexer is the wrong
one.

Consequence: seven tmux-gated daemon tests gate on `tmux_on_path()`, which
accepts the shim, so IN EVERY WORKER-RUN SUITE they have been measuring rmux
while reporting tmux:

  boot_rehydration_reattaches_tmux_session,
  explicit_reattach_tmux_session_endpoint,
  pending_plan_reattach_existing_session,
  boot_reattach_respawns_when_session_gone,
  failed_terminal_with_live_tmux_session_is_not_resurrected,
  production_resume_native_fork_uses_pinned_claude_not_path_shim,
  two_recovery_chain_second_resume_uses_first_fork_session_id

(names as listed in K4G1D's report §6.2; verify against HEAD before acting).

K4G1D added the strict availability rule (`tmux_mode_availability_for` — a
shimmed tmux counts as ABSENT, loudly) but deliberately did NOT widen
`tmux_on_path()`: regating seven tests is a decision, not a fix — it would
newly fail the tmux sentinel in every worker environment, and it partly
reframes the worker-vs-manager failure comparisons recorded on TASK-STWVB.

=== Ask

1. Decide: should these seven tests demand REAL tmux (strict rule), or is
   testing-through-the-shim acceptable for some of them (in which case they
   should SAY they ran rmux)? Record the decision and its reason.
2. Apply it: either regate on the strict rule (accepting that worker-run
   suites will report tmux NOT RUN via the honesty manifest — that is the
   truth), or split tests into genuinely-mode-agnostic (rename/parameterize per
   K4G1D's pattern) vs really-tmux-specific (strict gate).
3. Re-examine any STWVB comparison that relied on "the worker ran these under
   tmux" — it ran them under rmux.

=== Acceptance

- No daemon test can report mode=tmux while executing rmux: proven by test
  (K4G1D's strict rule is the template; its verify artifact pins the
  silent-GREEN failure mode).
- The honesty manifest names whatever is gated out in a worker environment.
- Injection per TCTTD standard, self-tested before reporting.
