* DONE TASK-JHWNP worktree-per-task-chain: implementer and fix rounds share one worktree; only review gets a fresh checkout :dispatch:worktree:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-JHWNP
:PRIORITY: P2
:TEST_CMD: scripts/run-tests.sh -p orgasmic-cli --test dispatch
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/**
:FIX_SUBTASK: TASK-JHWNP.1
:END:

** Description
Today every dispatch creates a fresh worktree (~create_worktree~, manager.rs), so a task chain of implement -> review -> fix -> review pays full ecosystem setup per round. Rounds are serial in practice. Design goal: one worktree per task CHAIN for same-kind implementer rounds — round 2+ reuses round 1's worktree (warm caches, populated submodules) — while every reviewer dispatch keeps getting a fresh checkout, because a fresh checkout at the worker commit is the only thing that proves the COMMIT rather than the implementer's directory (missing ~git add~, ignored-local-state bugs).

** Mechanics to build
- ~manager dispatch~ same-task same-kind implementer reuse: when the task's previous implementer worktree still exists and its dispatch is closed, reuse it instead of ~create_worktree~. The reused tree must be CLEAN (previous round committed); a dirty or wedged tree refuses with an actionable message, never silently falls back. Explicit ~--fresh-worktree~ opts out.
- Round branches: the new round's branch is created inside the reused worktree from ~--from~; derived-branch collision handling (dispatch.md already requires explicit ~--branch~ on round 2) stays coherent.
- Close keeps a chain worktree: closing a non-final implementer round must be able to leave the worktree for the next round without the operator remembering ~--no-worktree-remove~. Final close (implementer.done with merge evidence) removes it as today.
- Between-rounds protection: a kept chain worktree is not held by any open dispatch, so ~worktree-prune~ would salvage and reclaim it mid-chain. Design a hold the prune classifier respects (and releases at final close). Do NOT weaken any RMA18 refusal to do it.
- Cross-kind reuse stays refused (TASK-096.1). Reviewer worktrees unchanged. Submodule settle/cleanup at chain end unchanged.

** Acceptance
- Test: round-2 implementer dispatch reuses round-1's worktree path and an untracked warm-cache marker file survives.
- Test: dirty leftover tree -> reuse refused, message names the tree state and the escape.
- Test: worktree-prune keeps a mid-chain worktree, reclaims it after final close.
- Test: reviewer dispatch for the same task still creates a fresh worktree.
- Existing dispatch/cleanup suites stay green; no RMA18 refusal weakened.

* DONE TASK-JJ9RD Config node write path + kind registry single-source (silent wrong-file write) :daemon:cli:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-JJ9RD
:PRIORITY: high
:END:

** Description
Worst bug of the 2026-07-06 orsl battle-test (friction report F7+F8): =project.org= (=* PROJECT=) and =config.org= (=* CONFIG=) both scaffold =:ID: {{PROJECT_ID}}=, and the daemon's =NodeLayer= enum (crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:6883) has no =Config= variant. Consequences: config.org has zero CLI write surface (violating the "no hand-edits" convention — an agent filling TEST_CMD/LINT_CMD/BUILD_CMD has no lawful path), and the natural attempt =node prop set <project> TEST_CMD ... --kind project= silently succeeds against the wrong file (project.org). Separately, the CLI =--kind= flag is a free-form =Option<String>= (crates/orgasmic-cli/src/node.rs:32) — no enum in =--help= at all; the accepted set lives only in =NodeLayer::from_kind= (api.rs:6953), which under-documents =handoff=/=goal= and cannot express =config=.

Fix:
- Add =NodeLayer::Config= with kind-scoped id resolution (kind+id → file via =org_node_path=, api.rs:7468, routing to config.org). Kind-scoping avoids migrating existing projects' files.
- Reject CONFIG-reserved keys (TEST_CMD/LINT_CMD/BUILD_CMD/PIPELINE) under =--kind project= with an error naming =--kind config=.
- Single-source the kind registry (expose from a shared location) so the CLI derives a real clap enum: =--help= lists exactly the daemon-accepted kinds, including =handoff=, =goal=, =config=.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =node prop set --kind config= / =node body set --kind config= write config.org; round-trip test.
- [ ] CONFIG-reserved key under =--kind project= → 400 naming =--kind config= (regression test for the silent wrong-file write).
- [ ] CLI =--kind= help enumeration generated from / parity-tested against the daemon registry.
- [ ] Existing projects (shared =:ID:=) work without file migration.

* DONE TASK-JK66P Stall detector kills healthy workers during long quiet tool calls — MRJRK's worker died running its final suite gate
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-JK66P
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Measured 2026-07-29 on dispatch-TASK-MRJRK-implementer-20260729T000911: pane_activity events flowed every ~30s until 00:41:22, then the worker launched scripts/run-tests.sh (output redirected to files per house rules, so the pane goes quiet), and at 00:51:22 — exactly 10 minutes of pane silence — the daemon emitted run_complete 'stall_timeout_exceeded' and released the run (finalized_by_worker: false). The worker was HEALTHY: its report.md was complete except the suite result it was killed while producing; its branch had all work committed and its verify artifact self-tested PASS. The manager salvaged by running the gate and closing manually.

THE TENSION: this is the mirror image of TASK-VZMZE (heartbeats reset the stall timer so a wedged run is immortal). Here the detector has no heartbeat to see — the harness pane is static while a child process works — so quiet-but-healthy reads as stalled. TASK-HAREX's false-positive analysis named this exact profile ('sessions routinely go silent for 10+ minutes while cargo builds') for the RELEASE path; the STALL path has no equivalent protection.

THE SIGNAL THAT EXISTS: the worker's tool subprocess (cargo/run-tests.sh) was alive the whole time — child-process liveness under the pane is observable. A pane-bytes-only stall clock conflates 'no output' with 'no work'.

=== Ask
1. Establish what the stall clock currently measures for rmux dispatches (pane bytes? harness heartbeats?) and its budget (~10min observed). Coordinate with VZMZE's analysis — one design should fix both directions: a wedged run must not be immortal, a working run must not be shot.
2. Candidate signal: process-tree activity under the worker pane (child pids alive + consuming cpu), or harness-level tool-call-in-progress state, feeding the stall clock as evidence of work.
3. Whatever ships: MRJRK's profile (10+ quiet minutes on the final suite gate) must survive, proven by test with a compressed budget; VZMZE's wedge must still die.

=== Acceptance
- A run whose pane is silent but whose tool subprocess is alive and consuming cpu is NOT stalled, proven with compressed budgets.
- A run with no live work under it still stalls out on the existing schedule.
- Injection per TCTTD standard, self-tested with orgasmic verify --artifact.

** Description
Retire hosted pull-request and main-push CI. Keep targeted implementation gates, then require one complete local certification on the clean final tree before PR readiness. Cache reusable receipts by tree, base, certifier, and toolchain fingerprints; publish an exact-commit local/release-certified GitHub status; fail closed when the status is missing or stale.

** Acceptance
- No active workflow launches hosted CI for pull requests or pushes to main.
- A clean exact tree can be certified locally and posts local/release-certified only after the full release gate passes.

   reap a wedged =rmux= or =ps= child, so repeated probes can leak processes and
   blocking-pool work.

broaden to tmux here; TASK-4CSMY owns transport generalization after this
classifier is safe." That order did not happen: TASK-4CSMY landed first (merge

to make safe. Its reviewer called that a BLOCK SHIP
(=tx-20260802-orgasmic-4055=): an at-rest tmux pane whose prompt, transcript or
tool output contains =Esc to interrupt= is classified =Working= on every expired
stall sweep and survives to the 14,400s max-run ceiling instead of dying at 600s.

the unblocking work for TASK-4CSMY as well as for TASK-JQ8AV.

* DONE TASK-JQARS Implement the documented orgasmic manager drivers command :cli:runtime:docs:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-JQARS
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Problem: `shipped/entry/router.org` tells every manager "Use `orgasmic --help` and `orgasmic manager drivers` to discover installed transport pairs (`mode` + `harness`)". That subcommand does not exist; it exits with `unrecognized subcommand 'drivers'`.

This is not cosmetic. dec_WDR5K item 1 makes the `SUPPORTED` (mode, harness) matrix in `orgasmic-drivers` "the sole authority" for transport selection, and item 9 assigns per-dispatch model and effort choice to manager judgment rather than configuration. The runtime therefore depends on a manager reading that matrix — and gives it no way to.

Observed consequence 2026-07-25: a manager needing a reviewer transport ran the documented command, got the error, fell back to grepping `pub const SUPPORTED` out of `crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/lib.rs`, and picked the first entry of the array. The dispatch was decided by source-order, not judgement. A missing discovery surface does not produce a careful manager; it produces an arbitrary one.

Work:
1. Implement `orgasmic manager drivers`: list the `SUPPORTED` (mode, harness) pairs from the drivers crate, so the documented command matches reality.
2. Include what a manager actually needs to choose between them, not just the pair list — at minimum which pairs are non-interactive versus which spawn an interactive TUI pane, since that distinction decides whether a dispatch can run unattended.
3. Surface per-harness runtime options where a protocol catalog exists (dec_WDR5K item 9 permits structured protocol adapters only; never CLI text parsing). Where no catalog exists, say so explicitly rather than omitting the harness.
4. Add a router/CLI consistency check so a command named in shipped entry text cannot silently not exist. The general defect is that shipped prose and the CLI surface drifted with nothing to catch it.

Acceptance:
- every command named in `shipped/entry/router.org` resolves
- a manager can choose a transport without reading Rust source
- the output distinguishes unattended-capable transports from interactive ones

* DONE TASK-K4G1D Run the mux-dependent daemon tests under tmux as well as rmux, so 'is rmux at fault' becomes a measurement :testing:daemon:drivers:rmux:
:PROPERTIES:
:DEPENDS_ON: TASK-RRT4T
:ID: TASK-K4G1D
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs
:END:

Filed after the operator asked whether rmux, being far less mature than tmux,
might itself be the defect behind the recurring artifact-test failures.

It cannot currently be answered, and that is the problem worth fixing.

WHAT IS KNOWN
rmux 0.9.0 (crates.io, pinned `=0.9.0` in crates/orgasmic-drivers/Cargo.toml) is
a pre-1.0 third-party tmux clone with a tmux-compatible CLI. Measured 2026-07-26
against tmux on the same machine: 15 create+kill cycles cost 12.1 ms each against
tmux's 13.1 ms, 20 pane spawns of a warm script cost 12.8 ms against tmux's
6.9 ms, neither leaves a session behind, and neither costs syspolicyd anything.
So at the level that can be measured from outside, rmux is leak-free and merely
about 2x slower per pane spawn.

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN
Every artifact-regenerate test in crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs runs only
under rmux. There is no tmux counterpart, so when one fails there is no way to
tell whether the defect is in our driver, in rmux, or in the test's deadline.
Two of the three worker rounds on TASK-STWVB attributed that failure to a
different cause and both attributions were later withdrawn.

The one confirmed rmux-adjacent defect so far was OURS, not rmux's: TASK-8W30B,
where RmuxControl::release aborted its lifecycle task before Session::kill and
poisoned the shared ordered SDK transport. Worth noting the structural asymmetry
it exposed, though — the tmux driver drives tmux through its CLI, one process per
command and no shared state, while the rmux driver holds a persistent socket with
an ordered transport shared between Session and the lifecycle watcher. The second
design has failure modes the first cannot have, and every hang and leak this week
has been on that side. That is an argument about our integration, not about rmux's
correctness, and the two keep getting conflated.

WHAT TO DO
Parameterize the artifact-regenerate tests (and any other mux-dependent daemon
test) over both rmux and tmux, running the same assertions through each mode.

- red under rmux, green under tmux -> rmux is indicted, with a reproducer we can
  file upstream or route around by defaulting to tmux
- red under both -> the defect is ours, and we stop suspecting the dependency
- green under both -> the deadline is the defect

Depends on TASK-RRT4T: a mode that is unavailable must make the test fail or
report as ignored, never silently pass. Without that this change would just
double the number of tests that can quietly do nothing.

Acceptance:
- at least post_artifact_regenerate_hot_path_reuses_live_run_id runs under both
  modes
- a failure names which mode it failed under
- the answer to "is rmux at fault" is a test result, not a judgement call

* DONE TASK-K5NDR ORGASMIC_RUN_ID leaks into test subprocesses, so the CLI suite fails inside a dispatch :tests:defect:dispatch:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-K5NDR
:PRIORITY: P1
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-cli
:END:

`ORGASMIC_RUN_ID` leaks from the operator's (or a worker's) environment into
test subprocesses, so every `dispatch finalize` test in
`crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs` resolves the AMBIENT run id instead of
the one its fixture created, and fails with `no live run ...`.

Reported by the TASK-6AYEJ implementer, and it reproduced the failure on
UNMODIFIED code before touching anything —
`dispatch_finalize_commit_flag_leaves_clean_committed_worktree` fails when run
from inside a live dispatch and passes outside one. All of that task's gates had
to be run as `env -u ORGASMIC_RUN_ID cargo test -p orgasmic-cli`.

This is the same class of defect as TASK-RRT4T (tests that silently skip when
tooling is absent) and TASK-STWVB (tests that pass alone and fail in-suite): the
suite's result depends on who is running it and from where, rather than on the
code. It is worse than either in one respect — it makes the CLI suite
UNRUNNABLE from inside a dispatch, which is exactly where every dispatched
worker runs it. A worker that does not know the incantation reports a red suite
it cannot explain, or worse, works around it.

The manager's own runs of this suite pass because a manager shell has no
ORGASMIC_RUN_ID set (verified: unset). So the manager and the worker see
different results from the same command on the same tree, and the manager's
green is the misleading one.

Fix direction: the test harness must not inherit ambient orgasmic run identity.
Clear `ORGASMIC_RUN_ID` (and audit sibling `ORGASMIC_*` variables that steer
resolution) in the fixture that builds the command, not in a wrapper the caller
has to remember. A test whose correctness depends on the operator's environment
is not a test.

Acceptance:
- `cargo test -p orgasmic-cli` passes with `ORGASMIC_RUN_ID` set to an arbitrary
  value in the environment
- the fixture, not the caller, is responsible for the isolation
- an audit of other `ORGASMIC_*` variables that can steer CLI resolution is in
  the report, with each one either cleared or explicitly justified as safe

calm host that is a real finding about the 10s daemon budget and deserves a task,
not a registry excuse.* [2026-08-08] they recurred, and the third run was on a
host =run-tests.sh= itself classified CALM. So this is filed as the handoff
instructed. *Do not register these in =flake-registry.toml= to green the gate.*

** The failure
All three are in =crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs= and all three fail the
same way — the CLI request to =/api/runs/<run_id>/release= exceeding the 10s
client budget during =manager dispatch-close=:

: Error: release recorded run before dispatch-close cleanup
: Caused by: daemon request timed out after 10s (1m load average 26.72) — the
: daemon may be healthy but the system is under load; a timed-out request can
: still land server-side, so re-read state instead of assuming it failed

- =reviewer_close_non_clean_verdict_flags_stay_in_progress=
- =reviewer_close_refuses_verdict_flag_alongside_property_verdict=
- =reviewer_close_verdict_has_issues_stays_in_progress=

** Observations, dated
- [2026-08-07] two of the three, once, at load 14, external Python at 96% CPU.
- [2026-08-08] all three, at load 26.72, during a full =-p orgasmic-cli= run.
- [2026-08-08] later, on a quieter host, ONE recurred
  (=reviewer_close_non_clean_verdict_flags_stay_in_progress=) with the suite
  reporting =host: calm=, =rate 0.0000=, load 5.38 before / 4.27 after.
- Every occurrence passes in isolation. Five =reviewer_close_*= tests ran 3/3
  green at =--test-threads=4= on the same binary.

*NOT caused by TASK-RMA18*, ruled out by mechanism rather than by argument: that
change adds filesystem work only to =admit_live_run= (acquire) and
=blocking_run_for_close= (close reservation), and neither is on the
=/api/runs/<id>/release= path these three time out on. Two of the three predate
it.

** The second finding, which may be the more useful one
=run-tests.sh= called the third run =host: calm=. Its host word is derived from
the syspolicyd CPU-seconds-per-wall-second rate (TASK-STWVB.1.1), which was
=0.0000= — correctly, because syspolicyd was idle. *The classifier is blind to
ordinary CPU load*, and ordinary CPU load is exactly what makes these three fail.
Load is deliberately =corroborating display only= per the STWVB chain, and that
was the right call for the syspolicyd question it was solving — but it means a
load-induced red is reported as a calm-host REAL failure, which is the strongest
possible verdict, on the weakest evidence the script has.

Weigh carefully before changing it: the STWVB chain spent a whole round
establishing that an ABSOLUTE load threshold was wrong. The answer is probably
not a load threshold; it may be that a client-timeout failure signature deserves
its own classification arm, since =daemon request timed out after 10s= is a
self-describing host-state error the classifier could read directly.

** Direction — decide, then implement
1. Establish whether the 10s budget is simply too tight for a
   =release=-then-cleanup sequence under parallel test load, or whether something
   on the release path is slower than it should be. Measure it; do not reason
   about it.
2. If the budget is the problem, changing it is a PRODUCTION decision, not a test
   one — the same 10s applies to an operator on a loaded machine. Whatever is
   chosen must apply to both, or be explicitly justified as test-only.
3. Consider the classification arm above, so a client timeout never again reports
   as a calm-host REAL failure.

** Acceptance
- The three tests pass under full =-p orgasmic-cli= concurrency on a calm host,
  repeatably, without being registered as flakes.
- The root cause is stated as a measurement, naming whether the budget, the
  release path, or test concurrency was at fault.
- A =daemon request timed out= failure is no longer classified identically to a
  genuine assertion failure, or the decision not to distinguish them is recorded
  with its reason.
** Occurrences
THIRD OCCURRENCE, MEASURED [2026-08-08], on the merged tree at =1cdf25b= during
the manager's TASK-RMA18.1.1 gate. =scripts/run-tests.sh -p orgasmic-cli=
returned *RED — 2 real failure(s)*:
=reviewer_close_non_clean_verdict_flags_stay_in_progress= and
=reviewer_close_refuses_verdict_flag_alongside_property_verdict=, both at
=crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs:433=, both:

: daemon request timed out after 10s (1m load average 13.64) ... url (http://127.0.0.1:51030/api/runs/<run>/release)
: daemon request timed out after 10s (1m load average 15.03) ... url (http://127.0.0.1:51129/api/runs/<run>/release)

=isolation: passed= — both green alone. The load was MANAGER-CAUSED: a
=claude= implementer dispatch (TASK-2QK4P.1) was running cargo concurrently with
the gate. That is normal operating load for this project, not an anomaly.

*A SECOND FINDING, AND THE MORE INTERESTING ONE — THE HOST VERDICT IS BLIND TO
THIS FAILURE MODE.* The same VERDICT block that reported these two failures also
reported:

: host : calm (threshold syspolicyd_rate>=1.50; load corroborating only)
: rate 0.1123

*=run-tests.sh= called the host CALM while the load average at the moment of
failure was 13.64 and 15.03.* That is not a bug in the wrapper — TASK-STWVB
round 3 deliberately derived the host word from the syspolicyd RATE and demoted
load to "corroborating only", and the round-6 review upheld that reasoning
explicitly: =HOST_DEGRADED= is measured from syspolicyd CPU CONTENTION, which is
not evidence of an unrelated failure mode.

But it means *the one word an operator reads to decide whether a red is
attributable is derived from a signal that cannot see a 10s HTTP budget
expiring under scheduler pressure.* The 08-07 handoff said these tests
recurring "on a calm host" would be a real finding rather than a registry
excuse. They recurred, the host word said calm, and the word was measuring
something else entirely. *Whatever fixes the 10s budget should also decide
whether a load-sensitive timeout deserves its own attributability signal, rather
than inheriting a syspolicyd-derived one.*

NOT REGISTERED AS A FLAKE. The registry's own guard says a green-alone failure
is REAL until OWNED, and this task owns it — but registering these two would
make the gate report green-modulo on a real product weakness that is now
three-times measured. The decision to register belongs with the fix, not ahead
of it.

* DONE TASK-KBHAN Harden comment-body #+begin_/#+end_ injection in reviews.org :artifacts:daemon:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-KBHAN
:IMPLEMENTS: arch_ARSPJ
:SEVERITY: low
:END:

TASK-Y2ZQJ hardened leading-* injection in comment bodies (escape_comment_message) but not org block markers. Because orgasmic_core OrgFile's block-mask is file-global, an unmatched #+begin_x line in a member-authored comment body can suppress heading recognition for LATER comments in the same reviews.org, silently swallowing them from the parsed comment list. Blast radius: comments hidden/dropped within one artifact's reviews.org; NOT property/flag injection into artifact.org (comments live only in reviews.org). Same injection class as ZEFEY finding #2; scoped out of the one-round Y2ZQJ fix which addressed the literal leading-* requirement.

Fix direction: extend the comment-body escaper (escape_comment_message / trim_and_unescape_comment_body in crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/artifacts.rs) to also neutralize lines beginning with #+begin_ / #+end_ (comma-prefix like the leading-* handling), or validate/reject them on write. Add a round-trip unit test with a comment body containing a #+begin_src ... #+end_src block and assert later comments in the same reviews.org still parse. Keep the escape invertible.

Severity LOW: requires a member to author a comment containing a bare org block marker, and only hides subsequent comments (no privilege/flag escalation).
** Evidence
[2026-07-06 Mon] DONE (goal-20260706-drain-the-full 4/10, manager-inline). Extended the comment-body escaper in crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/artifacts.rs: comment_line_needs_star_escape -> comment_line_needs_escape now also flags org block markers (#+begin_/#+end_), comma-prefixing them like the leading-* case so they can't drive orgasmic_core's file-global block mask and swallow LATER comments in the same reviews.org. Matches the parser's semantics exactly (org_block_line_mask lowercases + trim_start()s before matching, so uppercase #+BEGIN_ and indented '  #+begin_' are caught; a leading comma defeats both since trim_start strips whitespace not commas). Invertible: predicate depends only on the comma-stripped bare form, so escape adds one comma and trim_and_unescape_comment_body strips exactly one — existing leading-* and pre-existing-comma-star round-trip tests still pass. New teeth-test comment_body_block_marker_does_not_suppress_later_comments (unbalanced #+begin_src + uppercase #+END_SRC + indented #+begin_example in comment 1, comment 2 follows) asserts both comments parse + round-trip; TEETH-VERIFIED it FAILS (1 swallowed) with the block check neutered, passes with the fix. Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon 257 lib + all integration green; clippy -p orgasmic-daemon --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean. No reviewer dispatch (manager-inline mode per manager-implementer convention; operator accepted inline reviews 2026-07-04).

The supervisor wires babysitters into the subprocess-stream-json (cursor) path but apparently not the acp-stdio path.

** Description
Lift =ClaudeAcpDriver= from simulated mode to a real ACP (Anthropic CLI / Agent Client Protocol) bridge. Same shape as TASK-CHZTR (codex appserver) but speaks ACP against the =claude= CLI.

Target: when =config.endpoint= and =config.api_key_env= are both set, the driver spawns or connects to a =claude= process speaking ACP, forwards the prompt bundle, and translates streamed ACP messages into =DriverEvent= variants. The existing simulated-mode fallback (no endpoint configured) is preserved for CI.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Simulated-mode fallback unchanged when =config.endpoint= is empty or absent.
- [ ] When =config.endpoint= is configured, the driver opens an ACP channel against the =claude= CLI (or a configured endpoint) and forwards spawn payload (model, prompt-bundle, continuation context).
- [ ] Streamed ACP messages translated to =DriverEvent= variants: text chunks, tool calls, transitions, completion. Sequence numbers monotonic per stream.
- [ ] =transition_state= and =release= map to ACP control messages (or driver-side graceful shutdown when ACP has no equivalent).
- [ ] Worker vs babysitter tool boundary preserved.
- [ ] New test exercises the bridge against a recorded fixture or a local =claude= CLI when one is on =PATH=; skipped when not available.
- [ ] =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= clean, =cargo fmt --check= clean, =git diff --check= clean.
- [X] MSRV 1.78 preserved.

* DONE TASK-KKBTP pin the credential decision preflight admitted, and stop blocking the runtime in acquire
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-KKBTP
:PRIORITY: P0
:TAGS: drivers,claude,credentials,fix
:END:
** Description
Fix round for TASK-S0QRM (merged `e1b94b2`), which TASK-Z8WEJ's reviewer
returned **BLOCK** on. The reviewer confirmed the precedence reversal, the
explicit override, apiKeyHelper handling, key neutralisation, `--safe-mode`
isolation and the RunMeta field are each individually sound. Both blockers are
at the admission-to-launch boundary.

The manager independently confirmed the credential reversal by injection before
merging (injecting the pre-fix rule turns
`a_stale_ambient_key_no_longer_beats_a_detected_native_login` red with
`left: BareApiKey, right: NativeLogin`). That work stands. Do not undo it.

=== HIGH — preflight does not pin the credential decision it admitted

`crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/trait.rs:455-467`,
`crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/claude.rs:365-385,421-426,885-898`,
`crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/acp_stdio.rs:419-429,518-524`,
`crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/subprocess_stream_json.rs:60-66`,
`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs:970-987`.

`preflight_via_adapter` clones the adapter, observes `claude auth status`,
resolves the mode — and discards it. After the supervisor has reserved the
lease, `AcpStdioDriver::acquire` clones again and `compose_request` observes
again; for claude's subprocess arm ACP-stdio then delegates to
`SubprocessStreamJsonDriver`, which clones and composes a second time. A normal
acp-stdio claude dispatch asks `auth status` **three independent times**: once
before ownership and twice after it.

Rule 4 makes this correctness-critical. With a valid native login and a stale
ambient `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, a `Present` answer at preflight yields
`NativeLogin` and `Ready`; a timeout or malformed answer at either later
composition yields `Unknown`, which `resolve_credentials` treats as `Absent`
and flips to `BareApiKey`. **The run then launches with the stale key that
preflight never judged, after the lease is held.** The reverse transition is
equally possible. `RunMeta` records the last selection; recording is not pinning.

Reviewer's invariant probe:

```
369:        let probe = ClaudeAuthProbe::observe(&command).await;
425:            resolve_credentials(&cfg, &ClaudeAuthProbe::observe_blocking(&spawn.command))?;
FAIL: credential mode is independently observed at 2 production sites
```

Neither existing test can catch it: `the_probe_and_the_launch_resolve_the_same_credential`
uses a configured `api_key_env`, whose precedence is deliberately independent of
status, and `the_resolved_claude_credential_mode_survives_the_mode_layer` uses a
stub that always returns the same answer.

=== HIGH — acquire blocks the async runtime, and its advertised bound is incomplete

`crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/claude.rs:577-584,637-642,732-777`, plus
the two compose paths above.

`claude_available` runs a synchronous `Command::status()` for `claude --version`
with **no timeout**, called from `simulation_reason` during synchronous
`compose_request`, directly inside async `WorkerDriver::acquire`, with no
`spawn_blocking`. The blocking status probe then polls with
`std::thread::sleep`. Because ACP-stdio composes twice, acquisition pays two
unbounded `--version` calls and two blocking `auth status` calls *after* the
async preflight already completed.

Measured by the reviewer on installed claude 2.1.220, no turn submitted: three
sequential `auth status` calls `real 0.88s`, two `--version` calls `real 0.15s`
— about **1.03s of probing** on the production call graph, two thirds of it
after preflight. If `--version` hangs, acquisition has no bound at all and holds
a Tokio worker thread. The 5s `STATUS_TIMEOUT` on `blocking_native_login_evidence`
does not bound the preceding availability probe.

This is the TASK-Z3093 lesson recurring: blocking work on a runtime worker
thread.

=== Ask

1. Resolve a single immutable credential plan **before ownership** and carry
   that exact plan into acquire and composition. Do not re-probe in
   `compose_request`. The plan carries mode plus the non-secret launch facts
   (whether to neutralise the ambient key, whether to inline helper settings);
   secret values stay non-durable.
2. Remove the duplicate ACP-stdio composition for subprocess-stream-json, or
   make the first composition the request actually delegated and spawned.
3. Keep every harness probe async and wall-clock bounded. No `Command::status`,
   no `std::thread::sleep`, no pipe-draining wait on a Tokio worker.
4. Decide the `Unknown` policy explicitly and record it. Treating `Unknown` as
   `Absent` preserves key-only installs, but it lets a transient timeout change
   the credential tier between otherwise identical dispatches. Explicit
   `api_key_env` and `--credential-mode bare_api_key` already give a
   deterministic key choice; say whether an *unchosen* ambient key should also
   win on inconclusive detection, and why.

=== Acceptance

- A regression whose status stub returns `Present` at preflight and
  `timeout/Unknown` at composition, asserting the admitted mode, the spawned
  argv/env and the RunMeta entry are all identical. Prove it by injection:
  restore the re-probe, watch it fail, remove it, watch it pass — with output.
- A regression where `claude --version` hangs, proving acquisition stays bounded
  and the daemon stays responsive.
- Count the production `auth status` observations per dispatch and assert the
  number. One is the target; the test should name the number, not describe it.

=== Non-goals

- Do not revisit the precedence reversal, `--safe-mode`, key neutralisation or
  the `--credential-mode` override. All four were reviewed and confirmed sound.
- Do not fix TASK-GT91X (the codex transcript finder) here.

* DONE TASK-KKGKM A project the daemon cannot read must not prevent it from binding :daemon:boot:resilience:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-KKGKM
:PRIORITY: P0
:RELATES_TO: TASK-3R3EZ TASK-5P60H
:END:

Problem: when the daemon lacks filesystem permission for a registered project's path, it does not degrade — it dies. Reproduced 2026-07-25 after a runtime binary swap invalidated the macOS TCC grant for `~/Documents`:

- boot logged `starting pre-bind boot work`, then only `project scan timed out` warnings, then nothing
- the process sat at 0% CPU for minutes, never reaching `listening`
- `lsof` showed no project files open at all, only its own log, lock and binary — consistent with a permission-gated `open()` blocking in the kernel before a descriptor exists
- launchd `KeepAlive` kept spawning replacements, each refusing with `daemon instance lock is held, but the incumbent is not healthy`, so the machine churned without recovering
- the only operator-visible signal was a WARN line in a log file nobody was watching; `orgasmic status` simply hung

The daemon never bound, so every CLI verb, the UI, and the app were dead. A permission problem affecting a subset of projects took down the whole runtime.

The scan timeout works as designed — it logs "omitting project so daemon boot can continue" — but something after it blocks anyway. Find that, and make the whole class non-fatal.

Work:
1. Bind first, or at minimum guarantee that no per-project filesystem work can prevent binding. An operator must always be able to reach `status` and the UI to learn why the runtime is unhealthy.
2. Give a project whose files cannot be read a durable `unavailable` state with the reason, rather than retrying it into a hang. This is the same state TASK-3R3EZ introduces for missing project roots; reuse it rather than inventing a parallel one.
3. Report the condition where an operator will actually see it: `orgasmic status` and `orgasmic doctor` should name the affected projects and the exact remedy, not just emit a WARN into `daemon.out.log`.
4. Identify what blocks after the index scan completes. Boot reattach reads every session JSONL and is the leading suspect, but it was not confirmed — no fd was open at the time of sampling. Confirm before fixing.
5. Bound the launchd churn: repeated replacements refusing on the instance lock is noise that hides the real fault. Relates to TASK-5P60H's backoff work.
6. Regression: a registered project whose path is unreadable must still leave the daemon bound, reporting that project as unavailable.

Acceptance:
- an unreadable project cannot prevent the daemon from binding
- `status` and `doctor` name the affected project and the remedy
- the daemon stays useful for every other project
- a regression covers the unreadable-project case

ITEM 4 CONFIRMED (2026-07-25) — the task said confirm before fixing, so it was
reproduced rather than assumed.

Built an isolated throwaway ORGASMIC_HOME with two registered projects and
planted a FIFO where a session JSONL belongs. A FIFO with no writer blocks
inside open() before a descriptor exists, which is the same shape as the
permission-gated open in the original incident, and it is deterministic without
touching TCC.

Baseline with both projects healthy: bound in 44 ms.
With the blocking session file present:
- never reached listening; curl exit 7 (connection refused) indefinitely
- daemon.boot froze at {"phase": "reattaching runs", "seq": 7}, refreshed_at
  stuck at the boot instant while wall clock advanced 33 s
- 0% CPU, and lsof showed zero descriptors on the blocking file — exactly the
  "no fd was open when the process was sampled" observation from the incident,
  now explained: the process is blocked *inside* open(), before an fd exists
- stack sample:
    tokio::runtime::park::CachedParkThread::block_on
      orgasmic_daemon::api::reattach_live_runs_on_boot
        orgasmic_core::session::read_session_file
          std::fs::read_to_string

So the leading suspect was right, and there is a second finding the task did not
anticipate: the scan runs synchronously on the main thread inside block_on, so
it also starves the boot-progress refresh task. That is why the operator's only
liveness signal froze and `orgasmic status` simply hung — the heartbeat could
not advance even to report the phase it was stuck in.

FIX
1. Boot auto-reattach now runs after the listener is bound, in a spawned task.
   It is best-effort recovery; answering status is what an operator needs in
   order to diagnose anything at all.
2. Its file reads moved to spawn_blocking, so a wedged read costs one blocking
   thread instead of a runtime worker.
3. Session paths that are not regular files are refused by shape with a named
   warning, rather than discovered by hanging.

Verified end to end on the same isolated home: binds in ~50 ms with the
blocking file still present, /api/daemon/status answers in 1.6 ms, and the
warning names the offending path.

REGRESSION
crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/boot_resilience.rs covers both the blocking-open
case and an unreadable project directory. Both were verified to fail against the
reverted fix, not merely to pass against the current one.

The first version of that test used tokio::time::timeout and hung forever
instead of failing: a synchronous block inside a future stalls the task
mid-poll, so the timer fires but the task can never be woken to observe it. It
now boots on an owned thread and waits on a channel deadline, and a reverted fix
reports itself cleanly at 20.02 s with a message stating the invariant.

NOT DONE HERE, and why:
- Item 2 (durable `unavailable` project state) is the state model TASK-3R3EZ
  introduces. The task says to reuse it rather than invent a parallel one, and
  3R3EZ has not landed, so inventing it here would be something 3R3EZ has to
  unpick.
- Item 3 (status/doctor naming the affected project) depends on that state
  existing to report.
- Item 5 (bounding launchd churn) belongs with TASK-5P60H's backoff work.
- Boot reattach still reads whole session files. That is cost, not a hang, now
  that it is off the critical path; filed as TASK-7QM8M with the correctness
  subtlety that blocks a naive swap to the bounded scanner.

** Description
Surfaced live during the TASK-WQFPG.1 dispatch this session (cursor-agent =run-20260525T050115-...= on =task-062.1-impl=): the cursor-agent subprocess ran to clean completion + self-commit, but =/private/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-062.1-last.txt= and =/private/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-062.1-stdout.log= were NEVER populated, despite =run.created= tx recording both paths in =:LAST_PATH:= and =:STDOUT_PATH:=.

This is a regression from the TASK-RF3J1.6 era. The TASK-RF3J1 cluster narrative explicitly noted: "F-7 ships the dispatch RunComplete last.txt writer + =implementer.commit_pending= tx signal (gated by =dispatch.auto_commit_signal= config; default true), closing the manager-on-behalf-commit overhead loop AND restoring the watcher convention." So the writer SHOULD be wired — but is silently no-op for cursor-agent dispatches in the post-TASK-RF3J1.6 + post-TASK-FXXC0 daemon.

Earlier dispatches in this session DID populate these files (TASK-WQFPG implementer, TASK-G0C5R/TASK-DFEDX/TASK-CPA74 reviewer rounds at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-*-last.txt= are full of content). TASK-WQFPG.1 was the FIRST cursor-agent dispatch after the TASK-FXXC0 daemon-rebuild + restart at 01:23. So the regression entered between TASK-WQFPG's merge (=4e96cc0=) and HEAD.

Suspected causes (ordered by likelihood):
1. TASK-FXXC0's reshape of =post_task_dispatch= moved the manager.dispatch_started tx write into the daemon, but may have orphaned the supervisor-side RunComplete observer that TASK-RF3J1.6 wired to write last.txt. The new handler creates the run.created tx with =:LAST_PATH:= populated, but the supervisor-side writer may need a separate registration that the new handler doesn't perform.
2. Cursor-agent specific: the cursor-agent driver might not emit a RunComplete event the same way claude-acp / codex-appserver do; the writer expects a particular event shape and skips silently otherwise.
3. The =dispatch.auto_commit_signal= config might be defaulting to false post-TASK-FXXC0 (config defaults can drift on schema changes).

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reproduce the gap: dispatch a cursor-agent implementer (TASK-KM5K1 itself counts — dogfood the fix on the next dispatch); verify that =last.txt= and =stdout.log= are NOT populated on the current daemon.
- [ ] Root-cause the gap: identify which of the three suspected causes (supervisor-side observer missing, cursor-agent event shape, config default drift) is responsible. Trace via =tracing::debug!= adds if needed; remove the debugs before final commit.
- [ ] Fix: ensure that any cursor-agent dispatch via =POST /projects/.../tasks/.../dispatch= produces a populated =last.txt= (subprocess final stdout — the cursor-agent =result= event message) AND =stdout.log= (full subprocess stdout). The =implementer.commit_pending= tx signal should ALSO fire on RunComplete per the TASK-RF3J1.6 F-7 contract.
- [ ] Regression test in =crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/dispatch_endpoint.rs=: dispatch a simulated implementer run (using the existing mock-driver test scaffolding), assert that after RunComplete the =:LAST_PATH:= file exists with non-empty content AND =:STDOUT_PATH:= file exists with non-empty content. Test should reliably reproduce TASK-KM5K1's gap if the supervisor wiring regresses again.
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace + cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings + cargo fmt --check + git diff --check= all green. MSRV 1.78. No new deps.

** Notes
P2 because it breaks the dispatch observability contract (manager can't tail the implementer's progress in real-time; can't reconstruct what cursor-agent said in retrospect for forensics). Has a viable workaround (codex implementers populate the files correctly; manager can inspect session JSONL directly via =$ORGASMIC_HOME/sessions/dispatch-*-*.jsonl=). Not blocking — but every cursor-agent dispatch now leaves the audit gap. Fix-subtask candidate if reviewer surfaces follow-ups; otherwise straight to DONE on close.

* DONE TASK-KNENN Harden default instructions: route implementation through orgasmic workers, not raw provider CLIs :conventions:agent-dx:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-KNENN
:END:

Harden the agent-facing default instructions so the next agent dispatches implementation work through orgasmic workers, never a raw provider CLI.

Observed failure: asked to "implement all, use codex 5.5 xhigh on fast" inside this managed repo, an agent reached for the raw `codex` binary (`codex --help`, `codex exec ...`) instead of `orgasmic manager dispatch`. Shelling out to a provider CLI bypasses the daemon write authority, tx recording, worktree isolation, dispatch leases, and reattach/recovery — the entire reason work is managed here.

Fix: add an explicit rule to `conventions/orgasmic-tooling.org` (and/or `contributing.org`) stating that any request to implement/dispatch work — especially one naming a provider+model+effort like "codex 5.5 xhigh" — maps to `orgasmic manager dispatch --kind implementer --worker implementer-<harness>-<driver> --model <model> --effort <effort> --brief <path>`, resolving the worker from `orgasmic worker list` (e.g. codex 5.5 xhigh -> implementer-codex-tmux, model gpt-5.5, effort xhigh; service_tier fast comes from the codex harness config). Raw `codex`/`claude`/`cursor-agent` invocations are off-limits for doing project work. State the why (write authority, tx, leases, reattach) so it sticks.

Scope: docs/conventions only; a worded rule + a short mapping table from "provider model effort" to worker id. No code. Consider whether the daemon should also surface workers more discoverably to agents.
** Evidence
Manager-inline (docs-only, no dispatch). Added a 'Convention: dispatching implementation work' section to conventions/orgasmic-tooling.org (live .orgasmic + shipped/skills/orgasmic/scaffold copy): any implement/dispatch request routes through 'orgasmic manager dispatch --kind implementer --worker implementer-<harness>-<driver> --model --effort --brief', resolving the worker from 'orgasmic worker list'; raw codex/claude/cursor-agent invocations off-limits for project work (version --help OK). Includes the mapping table (codex 5.5 xhigh -> implementer-codex-tmux/gpt-5.5/xhigh; claude sonnet high -> implementer-claude-rmux/sonnet-5/high; claude opus xhigh -> .../opus-4-8/xhigh), the 'on fast' = harness-config note, and the WHY (write authority, tx, worktree isolation, leases, reattach/recovery). Cross-reference bullet added to contributing.org (both copies). Verified: daemon reindex parse_errors 0 after the live edits.

* DONE TASK-KPMFK A live stage loses its completion watcher across daemon restart, so no terminal tx is ever emitted :daemon:stage:boot:defect:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-KPMFK
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Found 2026-07-28 by the TASK-C0XMR reviewer (reviewer-codex-rmux,
run-20260728T103249) as finding 2. Pre-existing and outside the C0XMR diff, so it
did not block that round — but it falsifies the cross-restart guarantee that
review asked C0XMR to prove, so it belongs to the same family.

** The defect

`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:3321-3330,8973-9020`.

`post_stage` keeps `stage`, `target` and completion ownership **only** in the
spawned in-process `StageCompletion`. Boot reattach reconstructs the run but
respawns only `DispatchCompletion`, and only when both `last_path` and
`stdout_path` exist.

Stage runs carry `last_path: Some` and `stdout_path: None`
(`api.rs:3239-3267`), so they land in the partial-artifact warning branch and **no
stage watcher is recreated**.

Consequence: if the daemon restarts while `grill`, `plan` or `architect` is live,
a later worker finalize is persisted but no `<stage>.completed` or
`<stage>.failed` tx is ever emitted. The C0XMR outcome rule is never called at
all. The stage silently has no terminal record.

No restart test exercises a stage watcher, which is why this survived.

** Fix, per the reviewer

Persist stage completion metadata — `stage`, project/task, and `target` — in
recoverable lifecycle state, and have boot reconciliation respawn or directly
reconcile `StageCompletion`.

Note the partial-artifact branch is doing real work for dispatch runs; the fix is
to stop treating `stdout_path: None` as "incomplete" for a run shape that legitimately
never has one, not to weaken the branch for everybody.

** Acceptance

- A daemon-restart test for each shared stage path (`grill`, `plan`, `architect`).
- The `architect` case must cover its report-only terminal tx specifically —
  `architect` is a STAGE kind whose worker finalize emits `architector.reported`
  rather than `architector.done` (recorded near `api.rs:22475`, TASK-6AYEJ.1), so
  a watcher keyed on `.done` would pass the other two and still miss this one.
- A stage live across a restart emits its terminal tx.

** Non-goals

- Do not fold this into the C0XMR fix round (TASK-QSSQH). That round owns the
  failure-stickiness rule; this one owns watcher recovery. They touch the same
  file and must not be dispatched concurrently.

* DONE TASK-KWSTJ P0 prove and finish bounded GET /api/runs plus exact-run terminal paths :daemon:recovery:bug:
:PROPERTIES:
:DEPENDS_ON: TASK-JN5Q1
:ID: TASK-KWSTJ
:PRIORITY: P0
:END:

Build on, do not discard, the existing uncommitted TASK-JN5Q1 patch. First preserve its diff and rerun its focused gates. Reproduce against a fresh curl output path and record time-to-headers, time-to-body-complete, HTTP framing headers, response counts, and inventory stage timings. Treat the report claim that a complete stale file proves response serialization as disproven unless a packet/wire probe reproduces it.

Implementation boundary:
1. `GET /api/runs` must never await unbounded driver work. Terminal tombstones do no attach probe; genuine attach probes share one absolute deadline, have capped concurrency, and are aborted/joined on timeout.
2. Inventory construction must not parse multi-megabyte transcript bodies to answer lifecycle questions. Read a bounded lifecycle summary/catalog representation; legacy fallback may inspect a capped prefix/tail and must classify uncertainty conservatively. No per-failed-run whole-board rescan.
3. Exact recorded run ids use `/runs/:id` and `/runs/:id/release`; `dispatch-close` and explicit-id finalize never enumerate `/runs`. Legacy records without a run id retain a safe reachability fence.
4. Add stage metrics/logs for file count, bytes inspected, attach count/timeouts, classification counts, and total inventory latency without logging transcript content or local secrets.

Required regression is wire-level: seed production-shaped terminal, failed, interrupted, missing-worktree, and one permanently hanging attach record, including at least one very large transcript fixture or sparse file. Perform an authenticated HTTP request with a hard deadline; assert headers arrive, the body reaches EOF, JSON parses, classification counts are correct, and a second request does not rescan transcript bytes. Also run direct-close and explicit-finalize tests through a proxy that rejects `/api/runs`.

Acceptance target: p95 warm inventory below 250 ms on 200 records; cold legacy reconciliation is bounded and cannot exceed the CLI request budget. Verify with the real 197-file/2.239-GiB shape using a non-mutating fixture or snapshot. Run daemon, CLI dispatch, fmt, clippy, and diff-check gates. Do not delete or rewrite operator session history in this task.
** Evidence
Wire reproduction against the live pre-fix daemon (0.0.14, pid 11674, 5 projects, 198 session files totalling 2.239 GiB), fresh curl output path:
- `GET /api/runs` -> HTTP/1.1 200, `content-type: application/json`, `content-length: 120579`, `size_download: 120579`.
- `time_connect` 0.000286 s, `time_starttransfer` (headers/first byte) *35.205 s*, `time_total` (body complete) 35.207 s.
- Framing is therefore correct and the body does reach EOF; the body transfers in 1.4 ms once it starts. The "complete stale JSON file proves serialization" claim is disproven as an explanation, and the earlier "no headers, zero bytes" observation is a client deadline expiring inside the 35 s time-to-first-byte, not a serialization defect.

Source-backed cause, measured on the same real corpus (release build, read-only, non-mutating):
- Whole-transcript enumeration read 2.239 GiB / 428,992 envelopes in 3.08 s per pass, and the recovery-origin index re-read the whole board again whenever a failed tombstone existed, on top of serial driver attach probes.
- Bounded lifecycle scan reads 26.67 MiB in 95.3 ms over the same 198 files (135 truncated, 0 parse errors): 86x fewer bytes, 32x faster, and inside the 250 ms warm target.

Fix, on top of the preserved TASK-JN5Q1 patch (its focused gates rerun green before any new edit):
- `orgasmic_core::scan_session_lifecycle` reads a prefix/tail byte window (128 KiB + 64 KiB by default) and retains only lifecycle-relevant envelopes, rejecting transcript lines from their raw bytes without parsing. Budget sized from the real corpus: the furthest a lifecycle-deciding line ever sat was 56 KiB from the start and 13 KiB from the end.
- Truncation is conservative: `final_envelope_retained` gates the terminal-release decision, so a still-writing run is never tombstoned from a stale retained lifecycle line, and a missing acquire still classifies `ambiguous`.
- Inventory (`classify_session_dir`), the recovery-origin index (through the same pinned-directory, device/inode-validated fd), and `resolve_run_session_path` all use the bounded scan. Boot auto-reattach deliberately still reads whole files; that is TASK-5P60H's slow-start scope.
- `InventoryStageMetrics` (file count, on-disk bytes, bytes inspected, truncated/unreadable counts, attach probes started/timed out, origin-index files and bytes, per-classification counts, duration) is emitted as a `tracing::debug!` and returned on `GET /api/runs` as `inventory`. Counts and byte totals only: no session paths, transcript text, prompts, or credentials.

Regression added, `crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/run_inventory_wire.rs` (raw HTTP/1.1 over TCP, `Connection: close` so EOF is observable, 5 s hard deadline):
- `runs_endpoint_completes_over_the_wire_with_a_hanging_worker_and_huge_transcripts` seeds terminal (32 MiB transcript), failed, interrupted, missing-worktree, and one record whose driver attach never answers (stub `tmux` that sleeps 600 s). Asserts the status line and JSON content-type arrive, the body reaches EOF non-empty and parses, per-bucket classification is exact, the hung probe is recorded as `exceeded inventory deadline` with `attach_probes_timed_out == 1`, and inspected bytes stay at the fixed per-record ceiling. A second request inspects exactly the same byte window, proving transcript bytes are never rescanned.
- `runs_endpoint_stays_bounded_across_two_hundred_records` seeds 200 terminal records (every 40th carrying a 4 MiB transcript) and asserts 200 classified, bounded bytes, and a warm response well inside the request budget.
- Direct-close and explicit-id finalize keep passing through the `/api/runs`-rejecting proxy (`dispatch_close_with_recorded_run_id_does_not_enumerate_runs`, `stage_grill_finalize_from_orgasmic_run_id_on_main`).

Gates: `cargo fmt` clean, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean, `git diff --check` clean, `npm run typecheck` clean. orgasmic-core 132 lib + 26 fixture tests pass (plus one opt-in ignored real-corpus measurement). orgasmic-daemon lib 500 tests and every integration binary pass. orgasmic-cli dispatch 39 tests pass. Pre-existing failures unrelated to this change, verified identical on clean `main` by stashing: `orgasmic-drivers` `simulated_acquire_emits_deterministic_flow`, and the three `dispatch_endpoint` tests that need a stub `codex` on PATH. Under full-parallel load the daemon and CLI suites also show load flakes (tmux/git/daemon-connect timing) that all pass when rerun serially; the same class of flake was present before this change. One stale assertion from the TASK-JN5Q1 patch was corrected: `manager_session_after_restart_is_recovered_not_lost` now expects the `does not support runtime reattach` reason that acp-stdio records instead of a driver probe.

No operator session history was deleted or rewritten.
** Reviewer pass
Production-shape verification, 2026-07-25, against an APFS copy-on-write clone of the real 200-file / 2.404 GB session corpus in an isolated scratch `ORGASMIC_HOME` on port 4899. The clone makes the measurement non-mutating by construction: writes cannot reach the originals, and the installed runtime was never involved.

Same corpus, same endpoint, three requests each:

| build | ttfb req1 | req2 | req3 |
| installed 0.0.14 (pre-fix) | 24.695 s | 24.809 s | 24.840 s |
| source build (fix)         | 0.105 s  | 0.096 s | 0.097 s |

Roughly 255x faster, and inside the 250 ms warm p95 acceptance target with margin. The endpoint's own reported metrics for the fixed build: 200 session files, 2,404,437,937 bytes on disk, 28,016,305 bytes inspected (86x reduction), 135 truncated scans, 1 attach probe started and 0 timed out, duration_ms 95.

Correctness, which matters more than the latency: the two builds were compared run-by-run across every classification bucket.

- runs classified: old 200, new 200
- present only in old: 0
- present only in new: 0
- classification differences: 0

So the bounded prefix/tail scan produces an identical classification of the entire production corpus while reading 86x fewer bytes, including across the 135 files where the middle region was skipped. This is the evidence the reviewer brief asked for under "attack the bounded-window premise" — the premise holds on real data, not just on fixtures.

Earlier live-daemon numbers for context: the same endpoint on the running 0.0.14 daemon with all five projects registered took 35.205 s to first byte. The scratch measurement is lower (24.7 s) because it carries one project rather than five; the order of magnitude and the conclusion are unchanged.

Not established by this measurement: behaviour under concurrent load, and the boot path, which still reads whole session files and is TASK-5P60H's scope.

* DONE TASK-M47E5 Move dispatch worktrees out of TCC-guarded directories, and give them a prune :daemon:cli:macos:dispatch:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-M47E5
:MOTIVATED_BY: TASK-3X5AQ
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon/**,crates/orgasmic-cli/**,shipped/**
:END:

** Description
Implements the fix decided on TASK-3X5AQ. Read that task's two measurement
sections first — "The cdhash measurement" and "Verification and recommended
placement (2026-08-05)". Everything below is already measured; do not re-derive
it, and in particular do NOT revive the shared =CARGO_TARGET_DIR= or the
stable-slot idea. Both are disproved there, with reproductions.

*Why the move works, in one line:* a TCC grant for a linker/ad-hoc-signed binary
is pinned to its CDHASH, so no path scheme can make a grant survive a rebuild.
The only durable answer is to stop needing a grant — put the worktree where
macOS does not guard.

=== Part 1 — move the managed worktree root
Change the DEFAULT managed worktree path from
=<project>/.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/<task>/worktree= to:

: ~/.orgasmic/worktrees/<project-id>/<task-id>/

- Key on PROJECT ID, not display name — the id is what the CLI and daemon
  already use (=--project <id>=) and names can collide or change.
- MOVE ONLY THE SCRATCH. The dispatch RECORD — brief, =last.txt=, stdout log
  under =.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/<task>/= — STAYS in the project. It is small,
  durable, written by the already-granted daemon, and leaving it keeps every
  existing brief-path reference in gotchas, briefs and memories valid.
- =orgasmic manager dispatch --worktree <PATH>= already exists as the override,
  so this changes the managed default only and adds no new surface.
- UNIVERSAL, not macOS-gated. Linux has no TCC, but the repo still stops
  accumulating multi-GB build trees and =git status= stays clean. One code path
  beats a platform branch.

Verified already (TASK-3X5AQ): a worktree there resolves its =.git= back into
the Documents-hosted repo, =status=/=log=/=remove= all work, the worktree's own
=.orgasmic/project.org= keeps project resolution working, it is on the same
filesystem, and the toolchain builds and runs from it.

Rejected alternative, for the record: =~/Library/Caches/orgasmic/...= is the
idiomatic macOS location and IS unguarded (zero TCC rows for Cache services) —
but macOS may PURGE it under disk pressure and destroy a worktree mid-dispatch.

=== Part 2 — pruning, which is NOT optional here
This is a REQUIREMENT OF THE MOVE, not a follow-up. Today a stray worktree sits
inside the repo where =git status=, =git worktree list= and the operator's own
eyes find it. After the move it is invisible, so the same leak becomes silent
multi-GB accumulation in =~/.orgasmic=. Shipping Part 1 alone trades visible
garbage for invisible garbage.

What exists today, measured 2026-08-05:
- =dispatch-close --worktree-remove= (DEFAULT TRUE) salvages uncommitted work to
  =refs/orgasmic/salvage/<sha>= and then removes WITHOUT =--force=, so git's
  clean check gates it.
- =dispatch-status --orphans-only= REPORTS dispatches whose run is gone.
- =dispatch-status --cleanup-failed= writes the orphan close tx and clears
  LEASES — not worktrees.

What does NOT exist: any call to =git worktree prune=, any age-based GC, any
boot-time or periodic sweep, any disk budget.

So three leaks survive close today, and all three become invisible after Part 1:
1. *A DIRTY worktree is never removed* — removal is deliberately non-forced.
2. *An ABANDONED dispatch* (worker died, manager never closed) keeps its
   worktree forever.
3. *Stale =.git/worktrees/<name>= metadata* accrues if a directory is removed
   out of band, which the move makes MORE likely because the new root is a
   plausible thing for an operator to =rm -rf=.

And Part 1 introduces a genuinely NEW failure mode to handle: a worktree whose
REPO no longer exists. Today worktrees die with the repo; afterwards they are
orphans pointing at a missing gitdir, and =git worktree remove= cannot help
because there is no git to run it from. Detect and handle this explicitly.

*Design constraints for the prune:*
- NEVER remove a worktree with an open dispatch or a live run. Reuse the
  existing health signals rather than inventing new ones.
- Salvage before removing, reusing the existing =refs/orgasmic/salvage/<sha>=
  path — do not add a second salvage mechanism.
- REPORT WHAT IT SKIPPED AND WHY, and how many bytes it reclaimed. Silent
  truncation reads as "cleaned everything" when it did not; this project has
  been bitten by that shape repeatedly.
- Prefer extending the existing orphan surface (=dispatch-status
  --cleanup-failed= and its health checks) over building a parallel reaper.
  Adding machinery where existing machinery can be made consistent is what took
  a sibling chain five fix rounds.
- Decide deliberately whether prune runs automatically (daemon boot and/or at
  close) or only as an explicit verb, and SAY WHY. An automatic reaper that
  deletes a worker's tree is a much sharper tool than a verb.

=== Acceptance
- A dispatch's managed worktree is created under
  =~/.orgasmic/worktrees/<project-id>/<task-id>/= and nothing under
  =~/Documents= is written by the worker's build.
- The dispatch record (brief, report, logs) still lands in the project.
- =--worktree <PATH>= still overrides.
- Closing a dispatch still removes the worktree, still salvages first, and still
  refuses to force-remove a dirty tree.
- A prune surface reclaims worktrees for closed or absent dispatches, refuses to
  touch live ones, names what it skipped and why, and reports bytes reclaimed.
- A worktree whose repo is gone is detected and removable.
- =git worktree prune= is run so stale =.git/worktrees= metadata does not
  accumulate.
- Gotchas, briefs and any shipped text naming
  =.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/<task>/worktree= are updated in the same change —
  =cli_parity= resolves shipped invocations against the real binary and is the
  gate that catches a doctrine edit that lags the code.
** Evidence
Landed =ffead86= (merge) / =e5ed186= (worker HEAD, 6 commits) on main, base =103ed7e=.

Implementer: =implementer-claude-tmux= — driver tmux, harness claude, model claude-opus-5, effort high. Run =run-20260805T140235-4e4f74ec8c154ad48115bf43d5bbc97a=, started_tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4458=.

NO DAEMON CODE CHANGED. The daemon worktree handling was already location-agnostic (=validate_dispatch_path= / =validate_dispatch_worktree_dir= check absolute + non-symlink + directory and nothing about the project), so the whole change is =orgasmic-cli= + =shipped/=.

MANAGER PRODUCTION PROBE on the merged tree, with the freshly built binary (the installed =orgasmic= on PATH is older and cannot answer this):
- default: =worktree: /Users/aspirational/.orgasmic/worktrees/orgasmic/task-stwvb= — outside Documents, keyed on project id.
- the dispatch RECORD still resolves under the project =.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/=.
- =--worktree /tmp/override-probe= still wins.
- dry-run created nothing: neither =~/.orgasmic/worktrees= nor the override path existed afterwards.

Integration gates, re-run by the manager on the MERGED tree:
- =scripts/run-tests.sh -p orgasmic-cli= — GREEN, 0 failures, "environ: complete — no tool requirement was waived".
- =cargo test -p orgasmic-cli --test cli_parity= — 3 passed. This is the gate the task named, and it is what proves the shipped doctrine edit did not lag the code.

** Description
Declared by the TASK-M47E5 implementer rather than buried, and confirmed by the
manager against the code before filing.

=path_under_own_dispatch_artifacts= (=crates/orgasmic-drivers/.../cursor_acp.rs=,
~:1038) derives the dispatch attempt directory as =worktree.parent()= and then
requires THAT to sit under =<project>/.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch=. After TASK-M47E5
the managed worktree lives at =~/.orgasmic/worktrees/<project-id>/<task>/=, so
=worktree.parent()= is =~/.orgasmic/worktrees/<project-id>= — never under the
project. The condition is now ALWAYS FALSE.

** Severity: fails closed, so this is correctness-of-intent, not a hole
The grant only ever ADDED permission. Losing it denies more, never allows more.
The common case still works: a summary file inside the worktree is allowed by
=path_under_worktree=, and the brief-read grant is unaffected because
=path_under_dispatch_artifacts= keys on the PROJECT ROOT rather than on
=worktree.parent()=.

What is actually wrong is that a cursor-acp worker passing =dispatch finalize
--summary-file= a path inside the project dispatch stem directory is now refused,
and that the function is dead logic asserting a state that can no longer occur.
Dead code that describes an impossible world is how the next reader learns
something false.

** Fix
Derive the dispatch artifact directory from the PROJECT ROOT, the way the sibling
=path_under_dispatch_artifacts= already does, instead of from =worktree.parent()=.
The worktree path stopped being a reliable route to the project the moment
worktrees left the project — so any other place in the drivers crate that infers
project location from the worktree needs the same read. Grep for it rather than
fixing only this one call site.

** Acceptance
- A cursor-acp worker can pass a summary-file path under the project dispatch
  stem directory again.
- No grant widens beyond what it allowed before TASK-M47E5.
- Any other worktree-to-project inference in =crates/orgasmic-drivers/**= is
  either corrected or shown not to exist.

Landed =ff5aee2= (merge) on main. Implementer: =implementer-claude-tmux= (tmux / claude / claude-opus-5 / high), run =run-20260805T175326-b63f2fd760a94ef3a4f4c34c1d9754e2=, started_tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4491=.

DESIGN CHOICE: the "own" variant is GONE, not narrowed. The attempt stem is not identifiable from anything the driver holds — it comes from the operator-chosen brief FILENAME (=dispatch_artifact_stem=), while =DriverContext= carries run id, task id, worker id, project id and worktree but never the stem or attempt token. Nothing could narrow the predicate honestly, and a distinctly-named function with a body identical to its sibling was ruled out, so the one caller routes to =path_under_dispatch_artifacts=.

A GRANT WIDENING WAS DECLARED AGAINST AN EXPLICIT "never widen a grant" INSTRUCTION, AND THE MANAGER ACCEPTED IT after checking the argument in code rather than the summary. The grant went from "under this attempt own stem dir" to "under the project dispatch dir", so a sibling task stem dir is newly accepted for =--summary-file=. Verified: =read_args_allowed= (=cursor_acp.rs:827=) has ALWAYS allowed reading anything under =path_under_dispatch_artifacts=, so no file becomes reachable that was not already readable, and =dispatch_finalize_command_allowed= still pins =--task= and =--run-id= to this run own ctx. Bounded, and it adds no reachability. The alternative — drop the grant and require summary files inside the worktree — fails acceptance criterion 1 as written.

** Description

Fix round for the BLOCK SHIP on TASK-M47E5.1's review. The finding and its
confirmed mechanism are on that task under "Review round 1 — REJECT (confirmed;
it overturns the manager's acceptance)". Read it there; do not re-derive it.

In one line: the finalize command grant was widened from *this attempt's stem
directory* to *the whole project dispatch tree*, so a worker on TASK-A can name
another dispatch's report and have it become TASK-A's own terminal record.

** The manager was wrong, and the reason matters for the fix

The widening was DECLARED by the implementer and ACCEPTED by the manager on the
argument that =read_args_allowed= already reaches those paths, so no new surface
appears. That argument does not hold: =dispatch finalize --summary-file X= reads
X, may COMMIT the worktree, writes X's bytes verbatim as this run's =last.txt=,
and emits the terminal tx. A read grant and a finalize grant are different
authorities over the same path.

*The principle to build to: the criterion governs the command/path pair, not the
transitive closure of separately granted actions.*

** Direction: pass the authoritative stem, do not re-derive it

The daemon already knows this run's artifact directory — the CLI's own finalize
resolves =run.last_path= from the live run record (=manager.rs:1934=). So the
adapter should be TOLD its attempt's artifact directory in persisted driver
config and authorize exactly that, rather than inferring anything.

This restores the pre-move semantics precisely: the old predicate allowed
=worktree.parent()=, which WAS =last_path.parent()= before TASK-M47E5 moved
worktrees out of the project.

Rejected alternative: waiting on TASK-A1KJW (task-derived dispatch stem) and
deriving from =ctx.task_id=. A1KJW is a good change and would simplify this
later, but making a security fix wait on an unrelated refactor is the wrong
order. Note in the fix that A1KJW can supersede the plumbing.

*This crosses crates.* Unlike TASK-M47E5.1, the write scope has to include the
daemon and the driver-config type, because the daemon is where the authoritative
value lives.

** Acceptance

- A summary file inside the CURRENT attempt's artifact directory is accepted.
- A summary file inside a SIBLING project dispatch stem is REFUSED. This is the
  newly-permitted pair the merged code allows and the existing matrix never
  tested.
- Nothing that was refused before TASK-M47E5 is newly permitted. State explicitly
  what the grant allows now versus at =d4922f7=.
- The brief-read grant (=path_under_dispatch_artifacts=) keeps working unchanged.
- With no artifact directory configured, the grant REFUSES rather than falling
  back to anything broader. Fail closed, as the sibling
  =a_dispatch_artifact_grant_refuses_when_no_project_root_is_configured= already
  does for the project root.
- The injection proof's pinned red/green contract INCLUDES the sibling-stem
  refusal. The current =verify/TASK-M47E5.1/= proof is a correct red for the two
  behaviours it claims and does not cover the no-widening criterion at all; that
  gap is why a wrong decision survived to merge.

** Also in scope, both small

- Add =ORGASMIC_PROBE_SESSIONS= to the probe's documentation alongside
  =ORGASMIC_PROBE_TRANSCRIPTS=, with a runnable example. It is currently the only
  route for an out-of-project worktree and is documented nowhere.
- Decide the deleted five-level candidate deliberately: =manager.rs:3865= still
  accepts an arbitrary explicit =--worktree=, so an old-layout in-project
  override can still make that walk valid. Either restore it for that case or
  say in a comment that the custom layout is not supported.
** Landed and verified by the manager
Merged =3a825cb= (worker =9f7028b=, base =b4ca343=, +190/-39 across 6 files).
Manager re-ran every gate on the MERGED tree.

=== The fix restores the ORIGINAL shape with an authoritative input

The daemon persists =dispatch_artifact_dir= from
=req.last_path.and_then(FsPath::parent)= — the per-attempt directory it already
owns — and =path_under_own_dispatch_artifacts= returns, keyed on that configured
value instead of =worktree.parent()=.

Note it kept BOTH halves of the original predicate:
=path_is_under(artifact_dir, dispatch_root) && path_is_under(path, artifact_dir)=.
The daemon supplies the value and the adapter still re-checks it sits under the
project dispatch root. That is defence in depth the brief did not ask for and is
right to have.

=== The strongest line in the diff

One test asserts, in a single pair, that a sibling project dispatch stem is
*refused by finalize* AND *allowed by read*. That pins the DISTINCTION between
the two authorities rather than either grant separately — so a future collapse of
the predicates fails loudly, instead of passing the way the old matrix did.

The old matrix is precisely what let the widening through: it refused a sibling
managed WORKTREE, the sessions dir and an unrelated =/tmp= path, and never a
sibling project dispatch STEM. Every assertion passed while the one
newly-permitted pair went unexercised.

=== The proof, and why it is tighter than its predecessor

=injection.patch= is a ONE-LINE swap: =path_under_own_dispatch_artifacts= ->
=path_under_dispatch_artifacts=. It restores exactly the merged-but-wrong
predicate, so the red cannot arise for an incidental reason.

Red log read by the manager: 2 panics, =0 passed; 2 failed=, both pinned —
=a summary file in a sibling project dispatch stem must be refused= FIRST, then
=a finalize artifact grant with no configured artifact dir must fail closed=. The
test names are =a_=/=b_= prefixed so alphabetical ordering puts the no-widening
assertion first deliberately.

That is the criterion the PREVIOUS proof never covered at all, which is how a
wrong decision survived to merge.

Its =-p orgasmic-drivers= run failed on
=installed_harnesses_answer_their_own_readiness_probe= — the OPPOSITE victim of

** Review round 1 — REJECT (confirmed; two findings land on the manager's brief)
Reviewer =reviewer-codex-tmux= (tmux/codex/gpt-5.6-sol/high) on merge =3a825cb=
vs base =b4ca343=. Verdict REJECT, one BLOCK SHIP plus one non-blocking. Manager
confirmed the whole chain against the code.

=== The BLOCK SHIP: the predicate is right, its INPUT is widenable

=path_is_under= accepts EQUALITY — =path == root || path.starts_with(root)=
(=cursor_acp.rs:1530=). So if =dispatch_artifact_dir= is the dispatch ROOT
itself, both halves of =path_under_own_dispatch_artifacts= pass and every sibling
stem is reachable again.

That value is production-reachable, not a forged test config. Manager traced and
confirmed the full chain:

1. =dispatch_artifact_stem= (=manager.rs:6442=) does
   =file_name.strip_suffix("-brief.md")= with no emptiness check. A brief named
   =-brief.md= yields =stem == ""=; =.-brief.md= yields =".".
2. =dispatch_artifact_paths_for_attempt= (=:6631=) does
   =project_dispatch_dir(project_root).join(&stem)=, so =dir= IS the dispatch
   root.
3. =last_path.parent()= is therefore the dispatch root, and =api.rs:4764=
   persists exactly that as =dispatch_artifact_dir=.
4. Equality passes, and the widened grant is back.

*So round 3 fixed the predicate and left its input unvalidated.* The new paired
test hard-codes a well-formed child directory and the daemon test only proves an
already-supplied value is serialized — neither exercises production derivation.

Worth naming: this is the reviewer answering the exact judgement question the
brief asked ("is there a cheaper way to re-widen this without the test
noticing?"). The answer is yes, and it is not by collapsing the predicates —
which is what the test guards — but by feeding the surviving predicate a broader
input.

=== TWO OF THE CORRECTIONS ARE ON THE MANAGER'S BRIEF

*1. The brief was wrong about canonicalization.* It told the reviewer to check
whether =path_is_under= could be fooled by traversal or symlinks, "note this code
does not canonicalize". It DOES: =resolve_policy_path= (=:1513=) canonicalizes,
and recursively canonicalizes the nearest existing parent before normalizing
=.=/=..=. Traversal and symlink escape are genuinely rejected. The real gap was
the one the brief did not think of.

*2. The brief named the wrong baseline.* It asked for a comparison against
=d4922f7= as "pre-M47E5". =d4922f7= is IN the M47E5.2 lineage and already
contains the managed-worktree move, at which point the old own-artifact predicate
was already dead and the normal allowset was worktree-only. The true pre-move
point is =103ed7e=, where the intended shape was worktree plus =worktree.parent()=
when that parent sits under the dispatch root.

The implementer's report claimed "compared with pre-M47E5 commit =d4922f7=, the
grant allows the same path set". That claim was made in good faith against the
baseline the brief supplied, and the baseline was wrong.

=== The pattern, and what changes

Three rounds on this sub-chain, and a manager brief has contributed an error to
each: M47E5.1 declared a write scope excluding the =verify/= dir it demanded;
M47E5.1.1's brief asserted two facts about code the manager had not read closely.

The common cause is stating unverified specifics with the authority of verified
ones. Adopted going forward: *a brief either verifies a specific claim about code
before asserting it, or marks it explicitly as a claim to check.* Both errors here
would have been harmless if labelled.

=== P2 NON-BLOCKING, accepted

The new =ORGASMIC_PROBE_SESSIONS= example points at =$PWD/.orgasmic/tmp/sessions=,
which does not exist in a dispatch worktree — so the documented command cannot
provide the route it advertises. And the restored five-level candidate does not
reach the old default =<stem>/worktree= layout: from the manifest it expands to
=.orgasmic/tmp/tmp/sessions=, one parent short. It is existence-gated and
therefore harmless, but the comment claims more than it delivers.

=== Accepted, no action

- The =None= call sites are correct, with reasons the manager had not worked out:

** Description

Fix round for the BLOCK SHIP on TASK-M47E5.1.1's review. The finding and its
confirmed chain are on that task under "Review round 1 — REJECT (confirmed; two
findings land on the manager's brief)". Read it there; do not re-derive it.

In one line: round 3 fixed the finalize PREDICATE and left its INPUT unvalidated,
so a degenerate dispatch stem makes =dispatch_artifact_dir= equal to the dispatch
ROOT and the cross-stem grant returns.

** The chain, confirmed by the manager

1. =dispatch_artifact_stem= (=manager.rs:6442=) strips =-brief.md= with no
   emptiness check: a brief named =-brief.md= gives =stem == ""=, =.-brief.md=
   gives =".".
2. =dispatch_artifact_paths_for_attempt= (=:6631=) joins that stem to the
   dispatch dir, so =dir= IS the dispatch root.
3. =api.rs:4764= persists =last_path.parent()= — the dispatch root — as
   =dispatch_artifact_dir=.
4. =path_is_under= accepts EQUALITY (=cursor_acp.rs:1530=), so both halves of
   =path_under_own_dispatch_artifacts= pass for every sibling stem.

** The ruling: fix it at BOTH ends

*The adapter must not trust its input.* Require the artifact dir to be a STRICT,
shape-validated child of the resolved dispatch root — preferably
=resolved_artifact_dir.parent() == resolved_dispatch_root=, which matches the
real stem layout and rejects equality, =stem/..=, and deeper-shape surprises in
one condition rather than three.

*The CLI must not mint a degenerate stem.* Reject empty, =.= and =..= stems in
=dispatch_artifact_stem=. This is a real defect independently of the grant — a
dispatch whose artifact dir IS the dispatch root would also collide artifacts
across dispatches. *Scope is explicitly expanded to the CLI for this.*

Neither alone is sufficient: the adapter fix is the security boundary and must
hold against any input, while the CLI fix removes the only known route to that

test only proved serialization. Round 4 moved the =.parent()= call into the test
