=== The judgement worth carrying forward

Four rounds, four reviews, and the recurring failure is not in the production
reasoning — it is that each round's TEST proved something adjacent to the claim
rather than the claim. The widening survived because the matrix checked sibling
worktrees and not sibling stems; the input gap survived because the test
hard-coded a well-formed directory; this gap survives because the test does
production's arithmetic for it.

The remedy adopted for round 5 is a mutation-shaped acceptance criterion: the
test must FAIL if production derives the grandparent, the file itself, or =None=.
Naming the mutations a test must catch is stronger than naming the value it
should assert, and every round of this chain would have been caught by it.

** READ THIS FIRST — STATUS
=orgasmic manager worktree-prune= IS ON MAIN AND IS NOT SAFE TO RUN. Three
confirmed defects, two of them data-loss. It is harmless TODAY only because the
installed runtime predates the verb, so nothing can invoke it.

*** DO NOT REINSTALL THE RUNTIME UNTIL THIS TASK LANDS.
The reinstall is what makes =worktree-prune= reachable. That is the whole of the
protection right now. Two other merged changes (the TASK-YN5FJ review gate and the
TASK-M47E5 relocation) are also waiting on that reinstall, so the pressure to do it
is real — do this first.

** Description
Reviewer REJECT on TASK-M47E5 (merged =ffead86=) from =reviewer-codex-tmux=
(codex / gpt-5.6-sol / high), tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4474=. The RELOCATION half
of M47E5 is correct and stays. The PRUNE half cannot ship as written.

All three were verified against the code by the manager before filing — none is
taken on the reviewer word.

*** FINDING 1 (P0) — a symlinked managed root redirects =remove_dir_all= outside it
=scan_managed_worktrees= calls =std::fs::read_dir= on the project managed root
without first proving that root is a real directory. =read_dir= FOLLOWS a symlink.
Each CHILD is then checked with =symlink_metadata=, which is correct but too late:
the children enumerated are real directories inside whatever the root points at.

The direct-child fence in =remove_orphaned_worktree_dir= does not catch it, and
this is the part worth understanding rather than patching blind: =path= is built
as =<managed_root>/<child>= from =entry.path()=, so =path.parent()= is literally
=managed_root=. The comparison passes trivially — and =normalize_path=
canonicalizes BOTH sides through the same symlink, so it passes under either
reading. The final =symlink_metadata= sees a real directory, because it IS one; it
just belongs to the victim.

Net: if =~/.orgasmic/worktrees/<project-id>= is replaced by a symlink, a bare
=worktree-prune= recursively deletes real directories somewhere else. The root is
user-writable and this codebase runs AI workers with filesystem access, so
same-user replacement is not a hypothetical threat model.

*** FINDING 2 (P0) — prune bypasses the reservation this project already built
=RunSummary= deserializes =run_id= AND NOTHING ELSE, so the CLI cannot match a
live run to a worktree at all; =scan_managed_worktrees= makes the tx ledger the
sole ownership decision and uses live-run data only to decorate an
already-held record. Under the cleanup lock, prune re-reads only that ledger, then
removes.

So a live run whose open dispatch record is absent or torn classifies as
UNCLAIMED, and a recovery acquired in the classification-to-removal gap is not
fenced either. The local file lock is shared with CLI =dispatch-close=, but the
daemon acquire/recovery path does not take it.

THIS EXACT RACE IS ALREADY SOLVED, one path over. =Supervisor::reserve_dispatch_close=
(=crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs= ~:3984) installs a cleanup reservation
and decides liveness UNDER THE SAME LOCK, and =admit_live_run= (~:543) reads that
fence last so no run can be admitted into a reserved worktree. Its own doc comment
says why a CLI-side audit cannot substitute: "a concurrent POST /runs/:origin/recover
acquires in *another process*, so no audit of await points in the CLI can close
that window — the authority has to sit where the supervisor lock already is."

Prune reproduces precisely the defect TASK-1T3FZ was filed to close. Do not
re-solve it in the CLI; route through the existing authority.

*** FINDING 3 (P1) — "repo gone" fails OPEN on I/O error, into the only unsalvaged delete
=worktree_repo_gone= treats ANY =read_to_string(.git)= error as evidence the
repository is gone: the =else= branch falls through to =(!dot_git.is_dir())=,
which is false for an unreadable regular file, yielding "no .git link". A
permission, ACL or transient I/O failure therefore selects =RepoGone= — the one
disposition that deliberately SKIPS SALVAGE and calls =remove_dir_all=.
=resolved.exists()= collapses errors the same way.

Classification also happens before the multi-GB size walk and before the cleanup
lock, and the under-lock re-check looks only at open dispatches, never at whether
the gitdir became reachable again. So an unreadable-then-restored repository can
lose dirty work with no salvage attempted.

** Fix
1. Anchor the managed root with no-follow semantics BEFORE scanning or deleting —
   refuse a symlinked root (and unsafe symlinked ancestors), or traverse and remove
   relative to a directory handle so a later rename cannot redirect the target. Add
   a tempdir regression in which the managed root points at a victim directory and
   every sentinel file survives.
2. Route each reclaim through the daemon existing cleanup reservation before
   salvage or removal, hold it across the whole mutation, release after. Match live
   runs by CANONICAL WORKTREE and project, which means =RunSummary= must carry
   =worktree= and =project_id=. Add tests for a live run with no open tx, and for a
   recovery acquired in the classification-to-removal gap.
3. Make repository classification FALLIBLE. Only a =NotFound= on the =.git= link or
   the admin directory may yield =RepoGone=; permission and other I/O errors become
   an explicit kept/skipped reason with that reason printed. Re-check repository
   state immediately under the guard, right before the unsalvageable direct delete.

** Acceptance
- A symlinked managed root cannot cause anything outside the real root to be
  removed, proven by a regression whose sentinels survive.
- A live run is never reclaimed, including one with no open dispatch record and one
  acquired during the classification-to-removal gap, enforced through the daemon
  reservation rather than a second CLI-side scheme.
- An I/O error never classifies as =RepoGone=; it is kept and named.
- The relocation half is unchanged and its tests stay green.
- =scripts/run-tests.sh -p orgasmic-cli= and =-p orgasmic-daemon= green;
  =cli_parity= green.
** Evidence
Landed =b20fba5= (merge) / =f6f1ca2= (worker HEAD) on main, base =0f8e364=.

Implementer: =implementer-claude-tmux= — driver tmux, harness claude, model claude-opus-5, effort high. Run =run-20260805T150600-dfd05d136f1f4e4c984c960570bceb06=, started_tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4479=.

THE FIX IS THE RIGHT SHAPE, NOT THE CHEAP ONE. =remove_orphaned_worktree_dir= was DELETED rather than repaired: all three of its guards were statements about a PATH, and a path ancestors are re-resolved by every syscall. =AnchoredManagedRoot::open= opens the root once with =O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC= — which refuses a symlinked root outright — and the resulting DIRECTORY HANDLE, not the path, is what enumeration (=fdopendir=/=readdir=) and removal (=openat=/=unlinkat=) resolve against thereafter. A rename of the root path afterwards cannot redirect a removal because no removal consults the path again, and a test proves exactly that by renaming the real root aside mid-prune and moving a victim into its place.

FINDING 2 WAS ROUTED THROUGH THE EXISTING AUTHORITY, AND THE API DID NOT NEED EXTENDING — the implementer said so plainly instead of dressing it up as work. Reclaim goes through =POST /projects/:id/tasks/:task/dispatch/close-guard= onto =Supervisor::reserve_dispatch_close=, which is already keyed on the canonical worktree. Prune request differs from a close in two fields and both say prune is entitled to nothing: =releasing_run_id: None= and =owned_run_ids: []=, so EVERY live occupant blocks it. CLI =RunSummary= now deserializes =worktree=/=project_id=/=task_id= (the daemon side always carried them; only this mirror was blind, which is why the CLI could not match a live run to a worktree at all), each =#[serde(default)]= so an older daemon degrades to "unknown" and unknown refuses to reclaim. An unreachable daemon now FAILS CLOSED, where it previously fell back to "nothing is live".

FINDING 3: =worktree_repo_gone -> Option= became =worktree_repo_state -> {Present|Gone|Undetermined}=. Only =NotFound= may yield =Gone=; permission/ACL/stat failures become =Undetermined=, never reclaimed, reason printed, and reported as =KEPT_WORKTREE= distinctly from =HELD_WORKTREE= because "nobody could tell" is not "somebody owns it". State is re-checked under the guard immediately before the unsalvaged removal.

THE INJECTION PROOF DEMONSTRATES REAL DESTRUCTION, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH HAVING. Replayed by the manager on the merged tree: =orgasmic verify TASK-M47E5.2= PASS, and the red log shows the pre-fix code ACTUALLY DELETING =victim/task-precious/keep-me.txt= outside the root, and reclaiming an unreadable-git worktree with =BYTES=1880= of unsalvaged worker output. Exactly 2 panics, both the pinned assertions, =0 passed; 2 failed=.

ALL FOUR REQUIRED REGRESSIONS WERE CONFIRMED RED ON THE UNFIXED TREE, including the hardest one: a recovery acquired in the classification-to-removal gap, made DETERMINISTIC rather than raced via a post-guard pause file (mirroring the existing =ORGASMIC_DISPATCH_CLOSE_PAUSE_FILE=). ** READ THIS FIRST — WHAT THIS TASK IS AND IS NOT
This task does NOT fix the prune. It makes the prune UNREACHABLE, so that manager
discipline stops being the only thing standing between this machine and a delete
path that has now failed two independent reviews with data-loss findings.

The redesign is TASK-RMA18. Do not do it here.

** Why this exists — a manager ruling
=orgasmic manager worktree-prune= has been reviewed twice and rejected twice, six
BLOCK SHIP findings between them, every one on the destructive path. It is
currently harmless for exactly ONE reason: the installed runtime predates the verb.

That coupling is now actively harmful, and that is the point of this task. THE
REINSTALL IS BLOCKED BY IT — and two GOOD changes are waiting on that reinstall
(the TASK-YN5FJ review gate, the TASK-M47E5 relocation), so the pressure to
reinstall keeps rising while the thing preventing it is a sentence in a handoff.
A protection that lives in a document is not a protection.

Make the verb refuse by CONSTRUCTION. Then the reinstall can happen, the two good
changes go live, and TASK-RMA18 can take the time a delete path deserves.

** What to do
1. =orgasmic manager worktree-prune= exits with a clear refusal naming this task
   and TASK-RMA18, and reclaims NOTHING — no salvage, no removal, no
   =git worktree prune=. Including =--dry-run=: a dry run of a scanner that
   follows an ancestor symlink still walks and sizes directories it has no
   business touching.
2. The AUTOMATIC DETECTION appended to =dispatch-status= goes with it. It shares
   the same unsafe scan: =scan_managed_worktrees= follows an ancestor symlink and
   would report a victim directory as reclaimable, and =directory_bytes= would
   walk it. Detection is read-only, so this is lower risk than the verb — but it is

* DONE TASK-M5JTN daemon dispatch hardening bundle: cursor-agent stream taxonomy + watcher post-exit grace + tx writer trailing whitespace :daemon:dispatch:bug:fix:bundled:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID:               TASK-M5JTN
:PRIORITY:         P2
:WORKER:           implementer-cursor
:IMPLEMENTS:
:PRODUCES:         crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs
:WRITE_SCOPE:      crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/dispatch_endpoint.rs
:TEST_CMD:         cargo test --workspace
:DEPENDS_ON:       TASK-KM5K1.1
:END:

** Description
Bundle of three small daemon-dispatch-hardening fixes surfaced live during the TASK-KM5K1.1 dispatch (=run-20260525T063458=). All three concern the live cursor-agent dispatch loop and overlap on =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs= — bundling them as one cluster avoids three back-to-back single-file dispatches contending for the same write region.

*Item 1 — cursor-agent stream taxonomy gap.* The TASK-KM5K1.1 dispatch emitted 530+ =text_chunk= events ALL with =stream: system= (cursor-agent "thinking deltas"); zero events with =stream: assistant=. TASK-KM5K1.1's =dispatch_last_summary_from_session= precedence fix is correct, but on the live cursor-agent path it still produces empty last.txt summaries because no assistant chunks ever arrive. Either the cursor-agent driver needs to emit a synthetic =run_complete= event when the subprocess exits (preferred — keeps the daemon extractor honest), OR the driver re-classifies its terminal text chunk as =stream: assistant=, OR =dispatch_last_summary_from_session= grows a system-thinking fallback (least preferred — pollutes the summary with raw thinking).

*Item 2 — completion watcher no-terminal-event timeout.* =spawn_dispatch_completion_watcher= currently polls indefinitely after the subprocess exits if no terminal session marker (=Lifecycle::Release= / =run_complete= / failure outcome) was emitted in the session. Falls back only on the 86,400s safety cap, which means a clean-exit-no-terminal cursor-agent run can leave the daemon-side watcher spinning for 24h before artifacts get written. Need: short post-exit grace period (e.g., 30s — long enough to let in-flight session writes flush) after the supervisor classifies the run as ended, then proceed with artifact write from whatever envelopes are present, even if no terminal event arrived.

*Item 3 — tx writer trailing whitespace on empty :REASON: values.* When =record_dispatch_started= (or any tx writer) is called with an empty =:REASON:= string, the serializer emits =:REASON:       \n= (trailing spaces). Pre-existing: =.orgasmic/tx/2026-05.org= lines 5450, 5496, 5604, 5669 all show the pattern. Breaks =git diff --check= on every cluster-close commit; manager hand-strips before commit. Cosmetic but discipline-affecting. Fix: when serializing tx property values, trim trailing whitespace OR skip the property line entirely if the value is empty.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *Item 1 (cursor-agent stream taxonomy)*: pick ONE of the three approaches above (synthetic run_complete preferred). After the fix, a real cursor-agent dispatch (verify by running this very dispatch's brief through =orgasmic manager dispatch=) produces a non-empty =:LAST_PATH:= file. Add a focused dispatch_endpoint test that emulates the cursor-agent "all system thinking deltas, no terminal" shape and asserts the chosen fix produces non-empty last.txt content.
- [ ] *Item 2 (watcher post-exit grace)*: =spawn_dispatch_completion_watcher= must short-circuit within N seconds (recommend 30s) of supervisor-observed subprocess exit when no terminal event has arrived. Add a regression test that drives the watcher to a no-terminal-event clean exit and asserts the watcher returns within the grace window (NOT 86,400s).
- [ ] *Item 3 (tx writer trailing whitespace)*: after dispatch with =--reason ""= (or with no =--reason= flag), the resulting tx entry must not have trailing whitespace on the :REASON: line (either omit the line, emit =:REASON: \n= with no trailing space, or emit just =:REASON:\n=). Add a focused unit test that constructs a tx entry with empty :REASON: and asserts no trailing whitespace via =assert!(!line.ends_with(' '))=. Verify =git diff --check= clean after a fresh dispatch.
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace + clippy + fmt + diff= all green. MSRV 1.78.
- [ ] Tests cover all three items; net test count grows by at least 3.

** Notes
Bundled rather than three separate dispatches because all three touch =api.rs= in overlapping regions; parallelism would require careful brief partitioning and risk merge conflicts. Single bundled brief is cheaper. NOT a :FIX_SUBTASK: (these are not reviewer findings on a prior dispatch); will go through full IMPLEMENT → REVIEW → DONE lifecycle. Reviewer pass after merge per persona rule 2.

** Description
TASK-XQ89W reviewer left one LOW deferred follow-up: idempotency-branch-coverage test for the release-babysitter-first ordering path in =Supervisor::release=.

TASK-XQ89W shipped the cascade-release logic with idempotency via RunNotFound swallowing — i.e., if the babysitter run was already released (e.g., user manually released it, or it auto-released after its parent), the cascade-release call sees =SupervisorError::RunNotFound= and swallows it. The existing TASK-XQ89W regression test =implementer_release_cascades_to_auto_spawned_babysitter= asserts the happy path (both runs released after one implementer.release call). It does NOT assert the idempotency branch: what happens when the babysitter was released BEFORE the implementer? Or the implementer.release is called twice?

This is a pure test-coverage win to lock in the idempotency invariant — small, no production code changes.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *AC-1 babysitter-already-released branch*: write a new test (=babysitter_release_then_implementer_release_is_idempotent= or similar) that (a) spawns implementer + auto-babysitter, (b) calls =Supervisor::release= on the BABYSITTER first, (c) then calls release on the implementer, (d) asserts the implementer.release does NOT error (RunNotFound on the babysitter cascade-call is swallowed), (e) asserts both runs end up released. This locks in the F-2 idempotency contract from TASK-XQ89W's brief.
- [ ] *AC-2 double-release of implementer*: write a new test (=implementer_release_twice_is_idempotent_for_cascade= or similar) that (a) spawns implementer + auto-babysitter, (b) calls release on implementer (cascades to babysitter — happy path, both released), (c) calls release on implementer AGAIN, (d) asserts the second call either no-ops cleanly or returns RunNotFound (whichever is the existing contract — check =Supervisor::release= implementation; the new test should assert whichever behavior the code already exhibits, not force a contract change). Idempotency means same end state regardless of repetition.
- [ ] *AC-3 (optional, only if trivial) cascade-ordering invariant*: if it's easy to inspect, also assert via a log/event side-channel that the implementer release HAPPENS BEFORE the babysitter cascade-release (the "implementer first, then babysitter" ordering documented in TASK-XQ89W's brief). * DONE TASK-MFJZ7 the billed harness test is guarded only by a flag people must remember, and it already fired
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-MFJZ7
:PRIORITY: P1
:TAGS: drivers,tests,cost,safety
:END:
** Description
`legacy_drivers_and_explicit_pairs_emit_equivalent_start_events`
(`crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/driver_modes.rs:1662`) spawns the real `claude`
binary and can submit a real, billed turn. It is declared as a plain
`#[tokio::test]` with **no `#[ignore]` and no environment gate**, so a bare
`cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers` runs it.

The only thing standing between a contributor and a charge is remembering to
pass `-- --skip legacy_drivers_and_explicit_pairs_emit_equivalent_start_events`
on every invocation. That is prose in briefs and one entry in `gotchas.org`
("Asking a harness to prove it can work costs real money"), enforced by nothing.

=== It already fired

2026-07-28, the TASK-QRB8S worker. Its brief carried the constraint in bold and
it still ran `cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers` without the skip, twice — once on
its branch and once on a stashed baseline to classify the failure. It reported
the result honestly, which is how this was caught.

Cost was probably nil that time: the run failed with the real binary answering
`Error: Session ID … is already in use`, which is a pre-turn rejection. **That is
luck, not a control.** A clean session id would have submitted the turn.

This is the same shape as the defects this project keeps finding: a guarantee
that lives in a document rather than in the code. A worker who is told the rule
and breaks it anyway is evidence the rule needs a mechanism, not a louder brief.

=== Ask

1. Gate the test so the **default is safe**. `#[ignore]` plus an explicit
   opt-in env (e.g. `ORGASMIC_ALLOW_BILLED_TESTS=1`) is the obvious shape: a
   bare `cargo test` then skips it and says so, and `--include-ignored` alone is
   not enough to run it.
2. Make the skip unnecessary rather than mandatory. Once gated, briefs and
   `gotchas.org` should stop telling people to pass `--skip`; update both, and
   say what the new instruction is.
3. Audit for any other test that can spend money or quota — any test that
   spawns a real harness and submits a turn. Report the full list and gate each,
   or state why it cannot bill. `real_claude_stream_json_bridge_reports_auth_error`
   and the `live_rmux_*` family are the obvious places to start; several are
   already availability-gated but availability is not the same as billing.
4. Make the sentinel account for it. The `required_test_tooling_is_present`
   contract counts gated tests; a billed test that is skipped by default must not
   silently change that count in a way that hides it.

=== Acceptance

- `cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers` with no extra flags does not run the billed
  test, and prints something that names why it was skipped.
- Prove it by injection: remove the gate, show the test being collected and
  attempted, restore it, show it skipped — with output. Do **not** let the
  injected run actually submit a turn; assert on collection, not on execution.
- The opt-in path works: with the env set, the test runs.
- `gotchas.org` and every brief template no longer instruct `--skip`, and the
  audit list from ask 3 is recorded on this task.

=== Non-goals

- Do not delete the test. It is the parity check between legacy drivers and
  explicit pairs and it has real value when someone deliberately opts in.
- Do not change what the test asserts.

* DONE TASK-MRJRK A registered project can be missing from the index, and the 404 blames the wrong thing :P1:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-MRJRK
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Problem: a project can be registered on the board, listed by `orgasmic project
list`, and still be absent from the index snapshot, at which point every route
that addresses it by id fails with a 404 that names the project as though it
were unregistered. The operator's only signal is an error that points at the
wrong thing, and the only known remedy is `orgasmic reindex` - which nobody
tries, because nothing suggests the index is the problem.

Two things need fixing, and they are separable.

1. The diagnosis. `select_project` (api.rs) reports a missed lookup as
   `not_found("project {id}")`. That message is indistinguishable from a genuinely
   unknown project, so it sends the reader to check registration - the one thing
   that is definitely fine, since `project list` just showed it. The message
   should distinguish "no such project on this board" from "registered but not
   in the current index snapshot", and the latter should name the remedy
   (`orgasmic reindex`). This is cheap and is most of the operator-visible value.

2. The underlying gap. A project that is registered but missing from the
   snapshot is a state the daemon can sit in indefinitely: nothing retries, and
   nothing reports it. Whatever the cause, the daemon should either converge on
   its own or say plainly that it has not. A `status` field naming registered-
   but-unindexed projects would make the condition self-reporting rather than
   something an operator stumbles into through an unrelated 404.

Do not start by assuming a cause. What is actually established is thin, and one
plausible-sounding explanation has already been checked and ruled out.

EVIDENCE, 2026-07-25, live on the operator's daemon
Found incidentally while trying to record gotchas during TASK-TJKFC.

- Daemon booted 17:53:31Z (pid 10647, boot_id a6fdd006). It had restarted on its
  own during the session; the previous instance was pid 71878 from 16:49.
- At ~18:03Z - ten minutes after that boot, so this is NOT a boot race -
  `orgasmic node body append <anything> --project orgasmic` returned
  `404 {"error":"project orgasmic"}`. Same for ddd.
- The same command with `--project orsl`, `--project lynx-auth` and
  `--project rare` got PAST project resolution (they failed later, on the node
  id or the glossary file). So exactly two of five were missing.
- `orgasmic project list` showed all five with clean ids at that moment. Ids
  were checked through `cat -v` for hidden characters: clean.
- `orgasmic reindex` at ~18:04Z fixed it immediately. The retry of the same
  command then failed at the *next* stage instead, which is how we know project
  resolution had started succeeding.
- Corroborated in ~/.orgasmic/logs/daemon.out.log: the first `glossary file not
  found` warnings for ddd appear at 18:04:23Z - i.e. only after the reindex,
  because before it the request never got far enough to touch a file.

RULED OUT, so nobody re-runs it
- Not a boot race. Ten minutes elapsed, and the boot log shows a completed
  reattach pass at 17:53:35 with no scan-timeout or partial-load warnings.
- Not "`status` reads a different source". `status.projects` is
  `snap.projects.len()` (api.rs:5753) - the same map the lookup missed. So
  `status` should have reported 3, not 5, during the window. It was simply never
  run at that moment, which is the one piece of evidence this report is missing
  and the first thing to capture if it recurs.

STILL OPEN
Whether the two projects were dropped after a successful load, never loaded at
all, or present under a different key. Note `load_project` inserts under
`board_entry.id`, and the two affected projects are the two with the largest and
most actively written `.orgasmic/` trees - both were being written continuously
by this session while the others were idle. That is a correlation, not a cause.

REPRODUCTION NOTE
If this recurs, capture in this order before reindexing, because reindex
destroys the evidence: `orgasmic status` (the projects count is the decisive
missing datum), `orgasmic project list`, and the failing node call for each of
the five project ids.

ACCEPTANCE
- A lookup miss for an id that IS registered on the board reports that
  distinctly from an unknown id, and names `orgasmic reindex` as the remedy.
- The condition is visible without provoking it: an operator can see that a
  registered project is not in the current snapshot without first hitting an
  unrelated 404.
- A test drives a snapshot that is missing a registered project and asserts the
  error text distinguishes the two cases. The test must construct the state
  directly rather than wait for whatever produced it here, since the cause is
  not yet known - fixing the diagnosis must not be blocked on finding it.

* DONE TASK-NYF7Z rmux TUI workers are not MCP-isolated the way acp-stdio workers are :drivers:isolation:rmux:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-NYF7Z
:PRIORITY: P1
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers
:END:

The acp-stdio claude adapter isolates its worker from the operator's MCP
servers. The rmux TUI path does not. Same harness, same worker personas, two
different blast radii — and rmux is now the standing default for every dispatch
(manager-dispatch, standing worker matrix, 2026-07-26).

MEASURED ON A LIVE WORKER, not read from code alone. TASK-6AYEJ dispatched as
implementer-claude-rmux (rmux / claude / claude-opus-5 / high), pid 37956:

    claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --model claude-opus-5 --effort high
           --session-id a3c31a76-... -- <compiled prompt>

No --strict-mcp-config. Compare adapters/claude.rs:361-365, where the acp path
pushes it deliberately, with the comment "without it this machine loaded nine
MCP servers into a worker that wants none". `claude mcp list` on this machine
today returns exactly nine: Figma, Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion,
plugin:svelte, syncntn, ray-exomem-dev, ray-exomem. Six connect.

The rmux argv is built at modes/rmux.rs:550-575 and pushes only
--dangerously-skip-permissions, --model, --effort, --session-id.

DO NOT REACH FOR --bare. It skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync, auto-memory and
CLAUDE.md discovery, but it also makes Anthropic auth strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
or apiKeyHelper — OAuth and keychain are never read. Our workers run on
subscription auth, so --bare would break them. That is precisely why the acp
adapter branches on ClaudeCredentialMode and, for NativeLogin, rebuilds "what
--bare would have given us, minus its credential policy" from
--strict-mcp-config alone. rmux is NativeLogin. Use the same narrow flag.

SIZE THE WIN HONESTLY — it is an isolation win, not a context win. Measured with
two `claude --print` runs in this repo, identical but for the flag: prefix
tokens 26528 without, 26284 with. A 244-token difference. Nine servers' worth of
tool schemas would cost far more than that if they were loaded eagerly, so the
harness appears to defer MCP tool schemas and charge only for names. Anyone
justifying this task on token savings is quoting a number that no longer holds.

The real argument is blast radius. A dispatched implementer working on a Rust
CLI has no business holding live, authenticated handles to the operator's Gmail,
Google Drive, Google Calendar and Notion. Nothing in the worker persona forbids
calling them, the run is --dangerously-skip-permissions, and the operator is not
watching every pane. TASK-6AYEJ's worker invoked no MCP tool, which is luck
rather than a control.

Scope:
- push --strict-mcp-config in the rmux claude path, guarded exactly as the
  existing pushes are (skip if operator-supplied harness_args already name it,
  so an operator can still opt a pane back in)
- check the equivalent for the reviewer stage: rmux/codex gets only --model
  today. Codex reads MCP from ~/.codex/config.toml. Determine whether it has a
  comparable flag and either use it or record plainly that it does not exist.
- one test per harness asserting the flag is present by default and absent when
  the operator supplied it

Out of scope: changing --dangerously-skip-permissions, touching the acp path,
and any CLAUDE.md / plugin / hook suppression. Those are separate arguments and
at least one of them (CLAUDE.md discovery) we actively want.

Acceptance:
- a live rmux/claude dispatch shows --strict-mcp-config in its argv
- an operator-supplied harness_args override still wins
- the codex question is answered in the report with evidence either way

* DONE TASK-NZ3C9 F9N5F fix: disable stall for persistent artifactor + reset idle on driver activity :artifacts:daemon:runtime:fix:
:PROPERTIES:

:PRIORITY: high

Fix the three findings from the TASK-F9N5F reviewer pass (reviewer-claude-rmux opus-4-8 xhigh, VERDICT ship-with-fixes). The merged idle-timeout feature (supervisor.rs a05cefc) is inert as shipped because the 600s stall timeout pre-empts the 900s idle window. Two manager rulings resolve the reviewer's open questions — implement to these rulings, do not re-litigate.

** Findings
- HIGH-1: the persistent artifactor still carries its 600s stall timeout, but idle is 900s. Stall fires first, so (a) the 15-min idle window is dead code and (b) a hot session waiting on operator think-time still dies at 600s — the feature does not achieve arch_045Q0.2 session-lifetime intent.
- MEDIUM-1 (regression): idle resets ONLY on accepted send_input, not on driver output. A single artifactor generation that streams continuously for >900s with no user input is treated as idle and killed mid-generation. Real risk — artifactor runs of 56m are on record.
- LOW-1 (test gap): no production-shaped test that ages last_input_at AND last_driver_event_at together and asserts the release reason; the stall-vs-idle interaction is unexercised.

** Manager rulings (authoritative — build to these)
- RULING 1 (fixes HIGH-1): DISABLE stall for the persistent artifactor. At the Artifactor && rmux gate in api.rs (the same site that sets idle_timeout_secs and mirrors persistent:true), also set stall_timeout_secs: Some(0) so idle becomes the SOLE inactivity gate. Mirror the manager-launch pattern (api.rs ~2113). No other worker kind changes.
- RULING 2 (fixes MEDIUM-1): the idle reference is max(last_input_at, last_driver_event_at) in timed_out_run. This DELIBERATELY broadens the task's original "reset on send_input only" wording: with stall disabled, idle must mean "no accepted input AND no driver output for the idle window" = genuinely abandoned, which survives operator think-time and never aborts a live streaming turn. This ruling supersedes the strict reset-on-input-only semantics from the original F9N5F brief.
- Keep everything the reviewer verified correct: min-deadline fold, last_input_at seeding at run_started_at, the lock discipline, and the Artifactor && rmux gating (the only site idle should be ON). Do not touch those.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Artifactor && rmux runs get stall_timeout_secs: Some(0) (stall disabled); all other kinds unchanged. Test proves a persistent artifactor is NOT released at the old 600s stall point.
- [ ] Idle release fires only when BOTH last_input_at and last_driver_event_at are older than the idle window; a run streaming driver events within the window is never idle-released. Teeth test: aging only the input clock (fresh driver events) must NOT release; aging both must release with reason idle_timeout_exceeded.
- [ ] Production-shaped test ages both clocks together and asserts the release reason + lease freed (LOW-1).
- [ ] Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon green (redirect to file, do not pipe); clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; fmt --all --check clean. MSRV 1.87.

* DONE TASK-P9T4N Multi-tx writer transaction so dispatch-close is one commit; reconciliation becomes backstop
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-P9T4N
:PRIORITY: P2
:END:

From TASK-EP3H1 (2026-07-29): `WriterHandle::transaction(rewrites, tx)` takes
exactly ONE tx, which is the only reason `dispatch-close` cannot be a single
commit — a close needs two ledger entries (the terminal `implementer.done` and
the `task.state_transitioned` from `write_task_lifecycle_and_record`), so the
CLI issues N+1 requests and the pair can tear.

EP3H1 shipped the backstop: close txs record LIFECYCLE_FROM/TO and
`reconcile_torn_closes` finishes a torn close on the next manager command, and
labelled idempotency (`already_applied` vs `already_in_state`) makes replays
safe. What remains is making the tear impossible rather than repairable.

=== Ask

Add a multi-tx writer transaction — `transaction_multi(rewrites, Vec<TxAppend>)`
or equivalent — so the close tx and `task.state_transitioned` land under one
flock, then route dispatch-close through it. Reconciliation stays as the
backstop for pre-existing ledgers and for client-side response loss (which no
server-side atomicity can fix — EP3H1's measured loss was a client timeout on a
request that SUCCEEDED server-side).

=== Acceptance

- A close is one commit: an injected crash between the two legs can no longer
  produce a ledger with the close tx but not the transition.
- Reconciler still passes its torn-close tests against old-format ledgers.
- The writer core change is proven with its own tests (concurrent writers, one
  flock, ordering) — this is the risky layer; EP3H1 deliberately did not touch
  it.
- Injection per TCTTD standard.

* DONE TASK-PT2DC Reconsider task lifecycle vs worker-dependent run sub-states :schema:state-machine:run-substate:design:griller:
:PROPERTIES:

:WORKER:           griller

:END:

** Description
Grill the relationship between the human-facing task lifecycle (=BACKLOG, EXPLORE, PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, SHIP, DONE, BLOCKED, CANCELLED=) and the per-worker-kind run sub-state vocabularies in =shipped/schema/state-machine.org= (=RUN-SUBSTATE implementer/reviewer/planner/analyzer/babysitter/manager=). The current model has accumulated concrete incoherences worth resolving before they harden into the MVP. Griller-only: do NOT edit the schema or write code — produce Facts / Assumptions / Questions-with-recommended-answers / Accepted Decisions (record in =.orgasmic/decisions.org=) / Glossary updates. A downstream IMPLEMENT task will apply whatever is decided.

Concrete branches to grill (verify each against the code before asking):
1. *Missing griller vocabulary.* =config.org= maps =STAGE_WORKER_EXPLORE: griller=, yet there is NO =RUN-SUBSTATE griller= block. What sub-states does an EXPLORE/griller run report?
2. *Stale manager verb.* =RUN-SUBSTATE manager= still lists =agent.ticking= (verbs: idle, ticking, acting, paused) but =/manager/tick= was removed in dec_WTM5Y/TASK-KMWZ6 (replaced by =/manager/launch=). What should the manager vocabulary be now (e.g. launching/idle/acting/paused)?
3. *Manager runs as implementer.* =/manager/launch= acquires the manager with =RunKind::Implementer=, so a manager run emits IMPLEMENTER sub-states, never the =manager= vocabulary. Reconcile: does the manager need its own =RunKind=, or should the =manager= sub-state block be deleted?
4. *Stage/vocabulary asymmetry.* =analyzer=, =babysitter=, =manager= have sub-state vocabularies but no =STAGE_WORKER_*= mapping; =griller= has a stage but no vocabulary. Is the keying axis worker-KIND, lifecycle-STAGE, or both — and is that intentional?
5. *Overlap / shared base.* Every vocabulary starts =ready, claimed= and ends =blocked, cancelled=. Should there be a shared base sub-state set with per-kind deltas (mirroring =base_worker= EXTENDS for prompts) instead of fully-duplicated lists?
6. *Actor namespacing.* The =agent.= / =human.= / =ci.= prefix split — is it applied consistently, and what decides which actor owns a given verb (e.g. =human.review= vs =agent.reviewing=)?

** Acceptance Criteria
- [X] Each of the six branches is either resolved (recommended answer accepted) or explicitly deferred with a reason.
- [X] Meaningful accepted decisions recorded as =* dec_NNN <title> :<topic>:= records in =.orgasmic/decisions.org= (Context/Decision/Consequences; no =:STATUS:=).
- [X] Any new/renamed terms (e.g. a settled name for the manager's post-tick verb) captured in =.orgasmic/glossary.org=.
- [X] Output names the follow-up IMPLEMENT scope (which =RUN-SUBSTATE= blocks + code in =supervisor.rs=/=session.rs= a later task must change) without drafting it.

** Evidence
Grilled live with the operator [2026-06-10 Wed] (manager-implementer mode, dec_ZKRQW). Code verification surfaced a deeper fact than the six branches: the entire RUN-SUBSTATE system is dead schema — =RunRecord.sub_state= is never assigned anywhere (=supervisor.rs= init sites 712/923/1200; =TransitionState= only formats a display headline at 2101), and =RunSubState::new= (=session.rs:81=) validates namespace shape only, never the vocabularies. =RunKind= has just two variants (Implementer, Babysitter — =trait.rs:37=); its real job is babysitter tool-gating, so five of six vocabularies were unreachable regardless.

Branch outcomes (all six resolved, none deferred):
1. Missing griller vocabulary — dissolved: vocabularies become base+delta keyed on performer; griller needs no own block (it already borrowed analyzer verbs via =:APPLICABLE_STATES:=). dec_P7EY8.
2. Stale manager verb — manager block deleted; manager's active verb is =manager.working= under the shared base. dec_P7EY8.
3. Manager runs as implementer — accepted as correct: no =RunKind::Manager=; RunKind stays the tool-policy axis; manager identity stays the =manager.*= namespace (TASK-KC92G UI already keys on it). dec_P7EY8.
4. Stage/vocabulary asymmetry — axis declared: vocabularies key on worker KIND (performer); lifecycle is task-side. Operator went further: lifecycle itself shrinks to Backlog/Todo/In Progress/In Review/Done/Cancelled (EXPLORE/PLAN/IMPLEMENT collapse into In Progress; SHIP dropped, Done = merged+reviewer-passed; BLOCKED becomes badge = sub-state + =:BLOCKED_BY:=). =STAGE_WORKER_*= replaced by an ordered worker pipeline. dec_WV1ZH + dec_DEH2T.
5. Overlap/shared base — shared minimal base {working, done, blocked, cancelled} + verdict deltas (reviewer/human: approved, requested_changes); no ready/claimed ("ready" rejected by operator; Todo column covers readiness, acquisition covers claiming). dec_P7EY8.
6. Actor namespacing — performer-owns-verb rule; namespace generalizes from agent/human/ci to <worker-kind>/human/ci; =human.escalating= → performer-owned; =ci.= kept reserved. dec_P7EY8.

Recorded: dec_WV1ZH/068/069 in =.orgasmic/decisions.org=; glossary terms =run-substate= + =worker-pipeline=. Follow-up IMPLEMENT scope (named, not drafted): =shipped/schema/state-machine.org= v3 rewrite (new keywords + transitions, base+delta sub-state section, delete all six per-kind blocks); =shipped/skills/orgasmic/scaffold/config.org= =STAGE_WORKER_*= → pipeline; heading-keyword migration across =.orgasmic/tasks/sprint.org= + parsers (=orgasmic-core= schema.rs/projects.rs/org.rs, daemon index.rs/watcher.rs/api.rs, cli manager.rs) + kanban UI; =session.rs= performer-namespace validation; =supervisor.rs= wire =TransitionState= → =rec.sub_state= (first real consumer); =shipped/workers/*.org= =:APPLICABLE_STATES:= alignment.

** Description
Seven reviewer findings from TASK-PYW86 bundled as one fix-implementer round per one-round-of-fixes discipline. No critical/high; bulk is test-strength gaps + one medium content-loader classification bug. Report at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-051-review-report.md=.

*F-1 (MEDIUM test) — Path-free assertions miss the actual leaked path.* =tests/integration.rs:115-134= rejects only =/tmp=, =/private/=, =os error=. Fixture root from =tempfile::tempdir()= can be elsewhere (=/var/folders/...=, custom =TMPDIR=). A leak of =ctx.project_root= without those tokens still passes.

*F-2 (MEDIUM test) — Loader-backed GET endpoint families have no failing-path coverage.* Commit changes =/agent-templates=, =/prompts=, =/skills= handlers (=api.rs:917-978=) hitting reads in =content.rs:407-504=, but the only integration coverage is the success-only smoke at =tests/integration.rs:1750-1778=.

*F-3 (MEDIUM bug) — Content loaders classify NotFound by string matching.* =content_load_error= decides 404 only when =error.to_string()= contains =not found through loader rule= (=api.rs:351-361=). If the file disappears between =resolve_loader= and =read_to_string=, the underlying =io::ErrorKind::NotFound= becomes a generic 500.

*F-4 (MEDIUM design) — Loader-backed errors lose structured =path= field.* Helpers log only =error = %error= (=api.rs:346-361=); the path is embedded in the =anyhow= context from =content.rs:407-504=. Sanitized body, but server diagnostics lose consistent =path= field.

*F-5 (MEDIUM test) — Decisions/Architecture/Glossary/ADR tests all hit =/org/file=.* (=tests/integration.rs:479-508=) only proves =get_org_file= / =read_artifact= (=api.rs:3542-3552=). They do not exercise the route families registered at =api.rs:112-132=.

*F-6 (LOW test) — Tests don't assert JSON envelope shape.* =assert_path_free_error= checks raw text contains, not =error= field of =\{"error": ...\}=.

*F-7 (LOW design) — Raw org-file errors not artifact-aware.* =get_org_file= passes generic =org file= to =read_artifact= (=api.rs:3542-3552=). All raw-file misses say =org file not found= regardless of which file.

- [ ] *F-2*: Add failing-path tests for at least one list route AND one load route per family =/agent-templates=, =/prompts=, =/skills=. e.g., a =.org= directory where a file is expected, or unreadable user content. Assert status + path-free invariant (extended per F-1).
- [ ] *F-3*: Replace string-based content-loader error classification. Either propagate a typed content load error carrying =kind=, =path=, =source=, OR inspect the =anyhow= chain for =std::io::Error= and map =ErrorKind::NotFound= → =ApiError::not_found= and everything else → =ApiError::internal=. Add a regression test: file present at resolve-time, race-deleted before read (use a deterministic shim or =tempfile= manipulation).
- [ ] *F-4*: Content loader errors log =path = %p.display(), error = %e= structured fields consistent with =file_read_error=. Either via the typed-error route (F-3) or by re-extracting path from anyhow context.

For genuine index-only routes that never hit filesystem errors (=/contradictions=, =/tasks/:id/activity=), assert their not-found/empty-state response is path-free + properly typed.
- [ ] *F-6*: Tests parse response as JSON and assert =error= field is present + non-empty. Use endpoint-specific predicates (=contains("not found") && !contains("read ")= or =starts_with("failed to")=). Preserves copy-edit flex without losing envelope contract.

* DONE TASK-PYZ9W tx appender must survive inode swap under the file path (git is a sanctioned concurrent writer) :daemon:tx:reliability:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-PYZ9W
:PRIORITY: P2
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/ crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/
:WORKER:      implementer-codex-acp
:END:

Incident 2026-06-13 (recovered, see tx-0323..0328 :RECOVERED: notes): a manager git stash/pop replaced .orgasmic/tx/2026-06.org with a new inode while the daemon held its C2PQ3 group-commit append handle. The daemon kept acking and fsyncing tx appends — into the orphaned inode. Six records (tx-0323..0328) were invisible on disk until manually reconstructed; dispatch-status showed a phantom open dispatch. Evidence: lsof fd 14w inode 433635903 vs path inode 434035963; file mtime frozen at the stash-pop instant; in-memory tx_count kept advancing.

Root cause: the tx appender caches the open handle for group-commit batching and never detects that the directory entry now points elsewhere. Git operations and human edits are sanctioned concurrent writers (concurrent-writer convention), so silent divergence is a data-loss bug, not operator error.

Fix direction: before each append batch, stat-compare the handle inode (fstat) against the path (stat); on mismatch reopen the path and invalidate the ProjectTxSeqCache entry. Alternative: reopen per batch (measure — C2PQ3 added the cache for group-commit throughput). Audit other long-lived append handles (session jsonl writers are per-run, lower risk).
** Evidence
implementer-codex-acp (gpt-5.5 medium), combined round with TASK-38GGG, worker commit =bde3202=, merged into main, close tx-0409. writer.rs: TxWriter handles now wrapped in CachedTxWriter capturing dev/ino (FileIdentity) at open; process_tx_batch + append_tx_inner + transaction_inner re-stat the path before each append and, on identity mismatch, drop the handle (forces reopen) and clear ProjectTxSeqCache. Regression test tx_append_reopens_after_path_inode_swap_and_rescans_sequence reproduces the exact incident: append 0013, rename a replacement file (0040) over the path, append again -> 0041 lands in the file AT THE PATH, 0013 absent. Session JSONL writers left unchanged (per-run, lower risk, scoped out). Manager gates: workspace 0 failures, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, fmt clean; daemon rebuilt+restarted pid 20193 parse-errors 0. Closes the data-loss bug from the 2026-06-13 stash/pop incident.

* DONE TASK-QGWK7 dispatch-close destroys the worker report, and the reported tx carries no body — a closed dispatch has no durable record of what the worker said :dispatch:evidence:manager:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-QGWK7
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/**,shipped/**
:END:

** Description
=orgasmic manager dispatch-close= DELETES the worker's =last.txt= and
=stdout.log=, leaving only the brief — and the =implementer.reported= /
=reviewer.reported= tx entries carry NO BODY, only metadata (=TX_ID=, =RUN_ID=,
=WORKTREE=). Nor is there a copy in git: =.orgasmic/.gitignore= line 1 is =tmp/=,
and =git log -- .orgasmic/tmp= returns ZERO commits, so the dispatch record tree
has never been committed. After a close, the only surviving record of what a
worker said is the prose the manager pasted into the close tx's =REASON=.

Observed live 2026-08-06: all four dispatch record dirs for the TASK-G64ZH chain
contain their =-brief.md= and nothing else. Three reviews (22.8KB, 24.7KB,
23.4KB) and four implementer reports, gone. Two review findings had to be filed
from their TITLES alone — see TASK-3RTM0's status block.

** Why this matters more than it looks
- The BRIEF survives and the REPORT does not, which is backwards: the brief is
  reconstructible from the task and the convention, the report is not.
- It silently punishes the correct workflow. The exit checklist forbids leaving
  orphan pre-flight tx and the default-branch gate forces the reviewer close
  before the implementer close, so every review reaches the deletion. A manager
  who closes promptly destroys the evidence; one who leaves dispatches open keeps
  it.
- THE TRANSCRIPTION IS NOT THE DEFECT — being the ONLY copy is. What a manager
  writes into =REASON= and the fix-round body is CURATED: which findings survived
  checking against the code, which is worth more than the raw report. The problem
  is that an error in the curation is then unfalsifiable. Demonstrated the same
  session: a merge sha was written as =40f3ec1= into the handoff AND the task
  Evidence, and only =dispatch-close= refusing it revealed the real =f74256b=.
  You want the curated claim AND the source it came from.
- It interacts badly with =:FIX_SUBTASK:=: the fix task's body quotes the
  findings, so that quote becomes the only copy of them.

** Direction — decide, then implement
The shape is settled by two measurements, so do not re-litigate them:

*Why the report must NOT go verbatim into the task node.* =done.org= is already
26,106 lines and the daemon reparses it whole on every reindex; this one chain's
three reviews would have added ~70KB and ~1000 lines. And a review body is
markdown with =#= headings and code fences — verbatim worker output in an org
node is a file-corruption surface, which is why =node body set= refuses column-0
=* = headings and why TASK-KBHAN had to escape review comment bodies already.

*Why =last.txt= must still exist during the run.* It is a streaming sink for
unbounded untrusted bytes from a worker that may die mid-write. That is a file's
job, not a parsed indexed node's.

So:
1. At close, MOVE the record out of =tmp/= into a TRACKED path rather than
   deleting it. Key it by the GENERATION (=started_tx=), not the task: this chain
   had six dispatches across three tasks, and a task node has no natural slot for
   six reports.
2. Add a =REPORT_PATH= property to the =*.reported= tx (and/or the close tx) so
   =reviewer.reported= stops being body-less and becomes resolvable.
3. Leave the node carrying the CURATED Evidence plus a pointer. Do not replace
   curation with the raw dump — both have jobs.
4. Decide retention deliberately and say it in the convention. If old records
   should age out, that is a policy with a number, not a silent delete at close.

The =manager-dispatch= convention's Integrate step must then say plainly where a
report can be read AFTER a close, because today the honest answer is "nowhere".

** Acceptance
- After =dispatch-close --worktree-remove --branch-delete=, the worker's report is
  still readable, from a path the tx names.
- The path is tracked in git, so a fresh clone or another machine can read it.
- Reports are keyed per dispatch generation, so a task with six dispatches keeps
  six distinct reports.
- =done.org= and the other state files do not grow by the size of the reports.
- The convention names where a closed dispatch's report lives, and the retention
  policy if there is one.
** Until this lands
EXTRACT EVERY FINDING BEFORE CLOSING, and write a close =REASON= detailed enough
to file tasks from — with =file:line= anchors, not just prose. The reasons written
on 2026-08-06 are the only thing that kept F-1 through F-5 recoverable at all.
** Evidence
*Implementer* =implementer-cursor-agent-tmux= — tmux / cursor-agent /
cursor-grok-4.5-high-fast. Run
=run-20260806T151244-7572bac5ee574bd6956fcf560376cf4f=, started_tx
=tx-20260806-orgasmic-4939=, merged =da88c19=.

*THE SHAPE.* Close promotes =last.txt= + =stdout.log= out of gitignored
=.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/= into TRACKED
=.orgasmic/dispatch-records/<started_tx>/=, keyed by the dispatch GENERATION so a
chain of six dispatches keeps six records. The close tx and the worker's
=*.reported= tx carry =:REPORT_PATH:=. Not =.org=, so the indexer ignores it —
confirmed, and =parse_errors= stayed 0.

*THE SAFETY PROPERTIES, checked by the manager rather than taken from the report.*
Promotion is fd-anchored: =copy_validated_artifact_to= reads via =read_at= off the
already-validated =File=, never re-resolving a pathname, and
=unlink_validated_attempt_pair= runs ONLY after BOTH copies succeed — so a partial
failure DUPLICATES rather than loses. On promote failure the close records
=CLEANUP_ERROR= and does NOT fall back to deleting; the files stay in =tmp=.
=started_tx: None= (failed-dispatch rollback) still prunes, deliberately. The
worktree salvage path — the one the brief forbade touching, because TASK-2BPWM
and TASK-D0GA3 exist from it destroying worker output twice — is untouched.

*Gates, replayed by the manager on the MERGED tree:* fmt clean; 12 core =paths=
tests; 64 cli =dispatch= tests (9 ignored); 4 shipped-convention tests; 8
=dispatch_close= units; clippy =-D warnings= clean.

*Proof.* =verify/TASK-QGWK7/= replays green, red log carries EXACTLY ONE panic,
and it is the pinned claim: "after close the report must still be readable from

*INERT UNTIL THE RUNTIME IS REBUILT, and that is not academic here.* The CLI that
runs =dispatch-close= is the INSTALLED one, so this dispatch's own report — and
its reviewer's — will still be deleted at close. The implementer's report was
copied out to the session scratchpad before integration for exactly that reason.
The change cannot protect its own dispatch.

session, but it is transport-dependent and COMMITTED BYTES ARE PERMANENT in a way

TASK-ZBYH3 -> TASK-G64ZH spent three rounds removing from =daemon.err.log=. The
implementer's stated reason for including =stdout.log= is good — it can FALSIFY a

(2) Durability still depends on a MANUAL step: the convention says "commit the
promoted directory", and nothing enforces it. The fix trades "the manager must

than interpretive, and a missed commit leaves the file rather than destroying it
— but still a manual link in a durability chain, in a task that exists BECAUSE
durability depended on a manual step.

** F-1 — HIGH — nothing stages the promoted directory, so criterion 2 is unmet
=shipped/prompt-studio/conventions/manager-dispatch.org:312-323= says "Commit the
promoted directory with the rest of the change so a fresh clone can read it."
NOTHING IN =crates/= RUNS =git add=. The promoted files land UNTRACKED, and the
durability guarantee is a sentence in a convention.

*Ruling (the reviewer's, and the manager concurs): close should STAGE the
directory itself* — =git add -- <dest_dir>= after a successful promote, in
=remove_worktree_required_with_hook= (=manager.rs:5163=) and
=promote_dispatch_artifacts_in_place= (=manager.rs:5462=). STAGING, NOT
COMMITTING: a path in the index is in git, so every subsequent state chore
carries it automatically — including =git add -u= and =git commit -a= — while
WHEN to commit stays with the manager, which is the part needing judgement. A
staging failure is reportable through the =CLEANUP_ERROR= channel that already
exists.

*CORRECTION TO THE REVIEW'S EVIDENCE, verified by the manager — do not carry the
original claim forward.* The review argued from five sampled commits that no
manager habit would ever sweep the directory in, concluding "zero precedent in
468 opportunities". THOSE COMMITS CANNOT DISCRIMINATE: =dispatch-records/= did
not exist yet, so there was nothing untracked to sweep, and they look identical
under =git add -A= and =git add -u=. Tested directly with =git add -n=:
=git add -A .orgasmic= (this session's actual command) DOES stage it;
=git add -u .orgasmic= does NOT. Proof it works: the two reports committed at
=54a82bd= got there precisely that way.

THE FINDING AND THE RULING BOTH STAND ANYWAY, and for a sharper reason than the
one given: the guarantee currently rests on an UNSTATED detail of which =add=
form a manager happens to use. A durability property that depends on an
undocumented habit is worse than one that depends on a documented step, not
better.
** F-2 — MEDIUM — =stdout.log= promoted unconditionally into PERMANENT git history
=crates/orgasmic-core/src/paths.rs:234=; retention at
=manager-dispatch.org:319=. The arithmetic is the finding, so do not re-derive
it — it is measured, not estimated:
- Volume: =manager.dispatch_started= tx — 202 (Jun), 556 (Jul), 191 (Aug 1-6) =
  949 in ~67 days = *14.2/day*, annualizing to *5,200-6,500 generations/year*.
- Size: =last.txt= mean 4,580B (max 15,562B); =stdout.log= max *478,920B*, and
  47 of 51 measured are 0 bytes because tmux never persists pane content — the
  4 non-zero ones are stdio/ws and average *157,703B*.
- Year one: =last.txt= *24-30MB/yr* — fine, keep it. =stdout.log= at the stdio
  mean is *820MB-1.03GB/yr uncompressed*, against a repo whose ENTIRE packed
  history is *8.71MiB*. That is 10-25x the whole repo packed, ~100x raw. And
  unlike =daemon.err.log= you CANNOT rotate it: pruning git history rewrites
  every downstream clone.

The implementer's reason for including =stdout.log= is GOOD and is the strongest
argument in the change — it can FALSIFY a curated close reason, and an
unfalsifiable curated =REASON= is exactly what the parent exists to fix. So weigh
it, do not dismiss it. *Ruling: =last.txt= yes, =stdout.log= not as-is.* Pick one
and say why:
1. BOUNDED TAIL (preferred): promote the last 64KB and RECORD THE ORIGINAL BYTE
   COUNT beside it. Caps the year at ~400MB worst case and ~0 typical, keeps
   falsifiability, and makes truncation VISIBLE rather than silent.
2. Promote only on non-success (=--status aborted=, or a =blocked= finalize) —
   when the transcript is worth more than the summary.
3. At minimum, skip a 0-byte =stdout.log= entirely, whichever of the above lands.

Also: the retention policy states "keep forever" with NO number and no age-out.
The parent's own text says a policy needs a number. "Keep forever" is defensible
for =last.txt= at 24-30MB/yr — it was chosen WITHOUT the =stdout.log= arithmetic.

=manager.rs:5401-5413= -> =:5462-5479=. Every other artifact-touching path takes
=acquire_dispatch_cleanup_lock= (=manager.rs:5107=, =api.rs:5766=) and, for a
destructive close, a daemon-owned close guard.
=promote_dispatch_artifacts_in_place= takes NEITHER — and it IS destructive now,
because =promote_validated_dispatch_attempt= UNLINKS both tmp artifacts
(=paths.rs:235=). Before this change =--no-worktree-remove= touched no files, so

The hole is named in the code's own comment at =manager.rs:1147-1152=: a 404 from

fails to rule out — a recovery replacement whose origin->replacement association

CONCRETE FAILURE: a recovery replacement is streaming into =last.txt=; the close
copies a PARTIAL report, unlinks the inode, and every subsequent worker write

=manager.rs:5401-5413=, =:5438-5440=; =paths.rs:302=.

** Acceptance
- A promoted record is IN THE GIT INDEX after a close, without the manager
  choosing a particular =git add= form. Pinned by a test.
- =stdout.log= promotion is bounded by a stated number, truncation is VISIBLE,
  and a 0-byte file is not promoted at all. State the year-one growth for

- The =--no-worktree-remove= promote takes the same cleanup lock and close guard

- A close that promotes successfully against an already-reclaimed worktree
  reports =CLEANUP_STATUS=ok=.
- =REPORT_PATH= is always project-relative.
- A half-succeeded promote still names what it did promote, and leaves no
  =.promoting= files behind.
- The promote copy streams; it does not buffer a whole artifact.

** M-1 — MEDIUM — a =git add= failure mis-reports the close AND silently keeps the branch
=crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:5423=, branch chain at =:5460-5481=.
MANAGER-VERIFIED IN SOURCE, not taken on report.

=promote_and_stage_dispatch_record= folds a staging error — and now also a
stdout-tail error, which returns =Ok= + error rather than =Err= — into
=WorktreeRemovalOutcome.error=. =cleanup_dispatch= then sets
=worktree_failed = true= for ANY such error *even when =outcome.removed= is
true*. Two consequences:

1. The close reports =CLEANUP_STATUS=worktree_failed= when the worktree WAS
   removed and the report WAS promoted, staged and named.
2. Every =branch_delete= arm requires =!worktree_failed=. Traced with
   =worktree_failed=true=, =worktree_removed=true=, =remove_worktree=true=: arm 1
   fails on =!remove_worktree=, arms 2 and 3 fail on =!worktree_failed=. *So NO
   arm fires — the branch is silently retained, =branch_failed= stays =false=,
   and no error names it.*

Concrete trigger: a concurrent state chore holding =.git/index.lock= makes
=git add= exit 128. This CONTRADICTS the design this round shipped under — the
brief's invariant was "a staging failure never fails the close"; it does not fail
it, it MIS-CLASSIFIES it, which is worse because the mis-classification is
silent and costs a branch.

*Fix (the reviewer's, and the manager concurs):* push promote/stage errors into
=errors= WITHOUT setting =worktree_failed=, exactly as the =--no-worktree-remove=
arm already does at =:5452=. Note the two arms currently DISAGREE about the same
class of failure (=worktree_failed= vs =partial=) — pick one and make them agree.

** M-0 — HIGH — staging the promoted record breaks git merge after a close
*Filed 2026-08-07, AFTER the review, found by the TASK-STWVB.1.1 gate on its
first honest workspace run. This is a REGRESSION from =955c8d6=, not a review
finding — and it is the most important item on this task.*

=crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs:274=, test
=reviewer_dispatches_before_reported_implementer_close_and_unlocks_main_merge=.

#+begin_example
git ["merge", "--no-ff", "-m", "merge reviewed worker", "task-dispatch-test-impl"] failed
stderr=error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
  .orgasmic/dispatch-records/tx-20260806-orgasmic-0006/last.txt
Merge with strategy ort failed.
#+end_example

MANAGER-VERIFIED: it fails ALONE as well (5.49s, exit 101), so it is a genuine
REAL and not load-sensitivity — the new classifier called it correctly.
=955c8d6= touched =manager.rs= and =paths.rs= but NOT =tests/dispatch.rs=, and
the last change to that test file was =0df25d0= (the TASK-QGWK7 parent). The
test's flow is: reviewer =dispatch-close= (which now promotes AND STAGES its
record) -> =git merge --no-ff= -> implementer =dispatch-close=. The staged
=dispatch-records/= path is what the merge refuses to overwrite.

*Why this matters beyond one test.* That test encodes the CLOSE-THEN-MERGE flow
the review gate itself prescribes: its refusal message tells the manager to
dispatch a reviewer and close it with =--verdict=, and only then does the
default-branch merge unlock. A manager following that instruction literally
closes first and merges second — and now the merge fails. This session's manager
did not hit it only because it merged BEFORE closing, which the gate permits but
does not prescribe.

*It also sharpens the review's claim 1.* The reviewer asked what could UNSTAGE
the record between =git add= and the commit. The answer that matters turned out
to be the opposite direction: staging does not get undone, it BLOCKS a merge that
wants to touch the same path.

*Fix direction — decide, do not patch reflexively.* The options are not equal and
the choice is part of this task:
1. Stage only when the index is otherwise clean for that path, and report through
   =CLEANUP_ERROR= when it is not. Preserves the guarantee in the common case.
2. Commit the record instead of staging — rejected once already, because WHEN to
   commit needs manager judgement; do not re-open without a reason.
3. Keep staging and make the manager's documented flow merge-before-close.
   Cheapest, but it moves the guarantee back into habit, which is exactly what
   F-1 existed to remove.
4. Stage with a mechanism that does not participate in merge conflict detection.
   Investigate whether one exists before assuming it does.

Whichever lands, *the failing test must go green with the durability property
intact* — do not fix it by dropping the assertion or by un-staging in the test.
=== MANAGER RULING 2026-08-07 on the salvaged attempt (=0273e9f=) ===
The first (dead) worker invented a FIFTH option for M-0, not on the list above:
build a temporary index from HEAD (=GIT_INDEX_FILE=), =git add= the record into
THAT index, verify every expected entry landed (a genuine M-2 fix), then
=write-tree= -> =commit-tree -p HEAD= -> =update-ref
refs/orgasmic/dispatch-records/<started_tx>=. The working index is never
touched, so it cannot block a merge.

*RULING: REJECTED, and the reason is measured, not argued.* The record becomes
reachable only from a custom ref that =git clone= does not fetch, and it is not
in the working tree either.

MANAGER-MEASURED with a scratch repo — created the ref exactly as the salvaged
code does, then cloned:
#+begin_example
$ ls clone1/rec            -> No such file or directory
$ git -C clone1 for-each-ref 'refs/**'
refs/heads/main
refs/remotes/origin/HEAD
refs/remotes/origin/main
#+end_example
The default refspec is =+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*=; =refs/orgasmic/*=
is neither fetched nor pushed.

So the approach *fails the parent's acceptance criterion 2* —
=manager-dispatch.org:312-323= says "Commit the promoted directory with the rest
of the change so a fresh clone can read it", and TASK-QGWK7.1's own acceptance
says "A promoted record is IN THE GIT INDEX after a close". It buys
merge-compatibility by giving up the durability property the whole QGWK7 chain
exists for. Consistently, it also REWROTE the F-1 test
(=dispatch_close_stages_promoted_record_in_git_index=) and the parent's verify
artifact to match — which is the "bent proof" shape, even though it follows
honestly from the design change.

*DO NOT ADOPT IT. Salvage the M-2 verification loop from it* (=ls-files
--error-unmatch= per expected entry) — that part is correct and independent of
the rejected design.

=== WHAT THE M-0 FIX MUST RECKON WITH ===
A fact the review did not have, and it reframes the options: *the manager never
hit M-0 all session because it COMMITS =.orgasmic= state immediately after every
close, before the next merge.* The test hits it because it closes and then merges
with the record still staged and uncommitted. So the failure is not "staging is
incompatible with merging" — it is "staging is incompatible with merging BEFORE
the state is committed".

That leaves two honest candidates, and choosing between them IS the task:
1. *The close COMMITS the record* (option 2, previously rejected on the grounds
   that WHEN to commit needs manager judgement). Reconsider it: a dedicated
   record commit is not the manager's change, and a committed file merges
   normally. If it is rejected again, say why in terms of what breaks, not
   precedent.
2. *Staging stays and the documented flow becomes close -> commit state ->
   merge*, with =manager-dispatch.org= saying so explicitly and the test
   committing state between its close and its merge. This keeps criterion 2
   intact and matches what the manager already does in practice — but it makes
   the guarantee depend on a documented STEP rather than on construction, which
   is what F-1 set out to remove. Weigh that honestly.

Whichever lands, the acceptance is unchanged: *a promoted record must be readable
by a fresh clone*, and =reviewer_dispatches_before_reported_implementer_close_
and_unlocks_main_merge= must pass without the test dodging the case.

Follow-up round for the TASK-QGWK7.1.1 review (merged =5b734a1=, verdict

that COMMITS the promoted record through a throwaway index — is CORRECT and its

*THE REVIEW IS THE MOST VALUABLE ARTIFACT HERE. READ IT FIRST:*
=.orgasmic/dispatch-records/tx-20260807-orgasmic-5129/last.txt=. It carries 14
scratch-repo git probes with verbatim output; nothing below should be re-derived.

*SETTLED — DO NOT RE-MEASURE:* the real-index =git add= is load-bearing (without
it the manager's next =git commit= DELETES the record from history); =update-ref
HEAD <new> <old>= really is a compare-and-swap on the branch through the symref;
a fully-ignored record dir cannot report false success; =partial= costs nothing

** F-1 — MEDIUM — a failed record persist is UNRECOVERABLE, and re-running the close refuses
=crates/orgasmic-core/src/paths.rs:317= (tmp unlink) ->
=crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:5636=. MANAGER-VERIFIED IN SOURCE.

=promote_validated_dispatch_attempt= unlinks the tmp artifacts as soon as the
COPIES succeed — before =commit_promoted_dispatch_record= is ever called. So a
failed commit leaves: record on disk untracked, tmp gone, =CLEANUP_ERROR= set,
status =partial=. There is then no way back into git:
=promote_dispatch_artifacts_in_place= bails on =last_path missing= (tmp is gone);
re-running =dispatch-close= hits =CloseTarget::AlreadyClosed= and returns a no-op
by design (=manager.rs:960-983=, verified); and there is no =--repersist= verb.

*The one path where the guarantee fails is the one path with no repair*, and its
only signal is a =warning:= line. That is the regression back to "manager habit"
that F-1 of the parent existed to remove, narrowed to the error path.

Worse, the rollback is unguarded: =manager.rs:5689= runs =git restore --staged=
behind =let _ =, so if the index lock is held at THAT moment the restore fails
silently and the record is left STAGED — which is M-0's symptom back verbatim.

*Fix:* make persistence idempotent and re-entrant. =commit_promoted_dispatch_record=
already works from =dest_dir= alone; only its CALLER is gated on tmp. Route the
already-closed no-op into it when the recorded =CLEANUP_STATUS= was non-ok.
Minimum viable: stop discarding the =git restore= result.

** F-2 — MEDIUM — the =update-ref= CAS can pass on the WRONG BRANCH
=crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:5800-5812=.

The CAS compares OIDs, not ref identity. Reviewer measured: with a sibling
branch at the same OID, =git branch other && git checkout other= between the
=rev-parse= and the =update-ref= makes the check PASS and the record commit land
on =other=. Millisecond window, requires a concurrent checkout.

*Fix:* resolve =git symbolic-ref -q HEAD= alongside the OID and CAS that specific
ref instead of =HEAD=, falling back to =HEAD= when detached — which also gives
F-5 a place to refuse.

** F-3 — MEDIUM (PRE-EXISTING, not a regression) — a close inside a conflicted rebase is discarded by =rebase --abort=
Measured in four scratch repos. Conflicted merge -> close -> resolve -> commit is
SAFE (=MERGE_HEAD= survives, both parents intact). =rebase --continue= is SAFE.
=cherry-pick --abort= is SAFE and the record survives on disk. Only
=rebase --abort= destroys the record — and *the staged-only baseline loses it
identically*, which is why this is classified pre-existing from TASK-QGWK7.1 and
was NOT the BLOCK SHIP the brief pre-authorised.

*Fix:* refuse persistence (or skip it and say so through =CLEANUP_ERROR=) when
=.git/rebase-merge=, =.git/rebase-apply=, =.git/MERGE_HEAD=,
=.git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD= or =.git/BISECT_LOG= exists. Four =exists()= calls close
the whole class.

** F-4 — LOW — =commit-tree= ignores =commit.gpgsign=, and one stated residual is FALSE
Measured: with =commit.gpgsign=true= and a garbage =user.signingkey=,
=git commit-tree= exits 0 and produces an UNSIGNED commit — so a repo enforcing
signatures gets unpushable history silently. Correctly named by the implementer.

But the implementer's residual "if =user.name=/=user.email= are unset the commit
fails" is WRONG: =commit-tree= succeeds using git's derived =user@host= ident.
Harmless in effect; remove it rather than carry a false failure mode.

** F-5 — LOW — detached HEAD persists the record to no branch
Measured: on a detached HEAD, =update-ref HEAD= moves only the detached HEAD;
=refs/heads/*= is untouched, so the record commit is on NO branch and the
manager's next =git checkout= orphans it. The close still reports =ok=.

Unborn HEAD is SAFE by contrast — =rev-parse --verify HEAD^{commit}= fails before
the real =git add=, so nothing is staged. The two unusual shapes are not
symmetric; only one is guarded.

** F-6 — LOW — M-5's refusal was inserted AHEAD of the torn-close recovery
=crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:951= vs =:957=. MANAGER-VERIFIED IN SOURCE.

=normalize_report_path_property= now runs above =reconcile_torn_closes_best_effort=,
whose own comment says it must run "before anything else, including the
already-closed no-op below". So re-running a torn close with a command line
carrying an absolute =REPORT_PATH= bails BEFORE the stranded transition is
reconciled. Refusing is still right; the ORDERING silently demoted a path that
was explicitly ordered first. *Fix:* move the call below the reconcile.

** F-7 — LOW (docs) — the sidecar now has two meanings and the convention documents one
=crates/orgasmic-core/src/paths.rs:394-460=, convention at
=manager-dispatch.org:334-340=. A =stdout.log.bytes= with NO =stdout.log= means
either "the harness printed nothing" (value =0=) or "the promote failed partway"
(value non-zero) — distinguishable only by reading the value, and the prose
documents only the first. Also: the promoted excerpt is =64 KiB + ~180= bytes
(the banners ride on top of the cap) while the convention still says "64 KB".

Fold in the two other doc gaps: record commits are UNSIGNED (F-4), and
*promote-only =--no-worktree-remove= closes advance the branch too* — the
convention says "a close moves the branch you are on by one commit" without
saying it applies to those as well.

** Acceptance
- A failed record persist is RECOVERABLE without hand-repair, or the failure is
  loud enough that a manager cannot miss it — and the =git restore= result is
  reported rather than discarded. Pinned by a test that fails the commit and then
  recovers the record into history.
- The record commit cannot land on a branch the close did not resolve (F-2),
  pinned by a test that repoints HEAD to a same-OID sibling.
- A close during any sequencer operation cannot lose the record (F-3).
- Detached HEAD either persists to something durable or refuses and says so (F-5).
- =normalize_report_path_property= runs BELOW =reconcile_torn_closes_best_effort=,
  pinned by a torn-close re-run carrying an absolute =REPORT_PATH= (F-6).
- The convention states: what a non-zero =stdout.log.bytes= with no =stdout.log=
  means, that record commits are unsigned, that promote-only closes advance the
  branch, and the real excerpt size (F-7, F-4).
- The false residual about unset =user.name= is removed, not carried forward.
- =verify/TASK-QGWK7.1.1/= and =verify/TASK-QGWK7.1/= still PASS unchanged.

A dispatch worktree checkout does NOT contain .orgasmic/ whenever the project's .orgasmic is uncommitted (every greenfield project between 'orgasmic project init' and its first commit — the exact DHYXQ bootstrap window). The walk then ESCAPES the worktree (nested at <repo>/.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/<task>/worktree) and resolves the MANAGER'S live repo root. Observed consequence in the smoke: finalize --commit ran 'git add -A && git commit' in the manager repo (sweeping the unrelated uncommitted .orgasmic scaffold + AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md onto the manager's HEAD), stamped THAT sha into the implementer.done tx as SHA/MERGE_SHA, wrote last.txt claiming success — while scripts/greet.sh sat UNCOMMITTED on the dispatch branch (task-05cy5-impl still at base). Silent wrong-target write + fabricated durable-work claim: worst class. Production orgasmic is unaffected only because its .orgasmic/ IS committed (worktrees carry project.org).

Fix direction: the COMMIT boundary must be the git worktree toplevel, not the project-marker walk — use 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' from cwd (stops at the worktree boundary: .git file) for commit_worktree/current_git_branch/WORKTREE tx extra; keep find_project_root only for reading project id (or read it from the daemon's run record instead). Additionally cross-check: refuse --commit when the resolved commit root differs from the run's dispatched WORKTREE (daemon knows it; expose on RunSummary/LiveRunInfo if needed) — fail loudly, never commit a root that isn't the dispatched worktree. Regression test: dispatch-finalize fixture where the project .orgasmic is NOT committed (worktree lacks project.org) → finalize --commit commits ONLY the worktree, never the manager root.
