ten seconds, so any defect that needs uptime to express passes every gate.
That is not hypothetical: TASK-Q07Y5 shipped fully green and killed the
operator's daemon 10.00s after every boot. TASK-R74E8 fixed it and added
`daemon_serves_far_beyond_its_connection_drain_budget` — one test, watching one
instance of the class (drain-budget misapplication, 8x budget ~ seconds). The
CLASS — anything that expresses only with minutes of uptime: timers, budgets,
watchers, leaks, heartbeat/stall interactions (see TASK-VZMZE), fd/session
accumulation — still has nothing watching it.

=== Mechanism

A scheduled soak gate, not a per-merge one (minutes of wall clock do not belong
in the merge path):

1. A self-contained script (suggested `scripts/soak.sh` or a subcommand) that:
   boots a REAL daemon from the tree under test with an isolated
   `ORGASMIC_HOME` and random port (the isolated smoke-daemon recipe in
   gotchas/memory — never `daemon start`, never the LaunchAgent, never the
   installed runtime), runs it for a configurable duration (default >= 5
   minutes; >= 10x any derived budget), under light periodic traffic (status
   probes, a task read, a tx list — hit real surfaces), then SIGTERMs it.
2. Asserts across the whole window: one pid and one boot_id throughout; zero
   parse errors; memory/fd growth bounded (record; alert on gross growth, do
   not tune thresholds finely); clean exit within
   `ShutdownBudgets::default().total()` + margin (derived, not a literal —
   the R74E8/ATAXN/QRB8S standard); marker/lock files retracted after exit.
3. Wire it into a schedule: the repo already has `nightly-macos` /
   `nightly-runtime` workflows — add it there, and/or a local launchd schedule
   for the operator machine. Decide and record which; a soak that exists but
   never runs is the same blindspot with extra steps.

=== Acceptance

- The soak runs green on current HEAD for the full default duration, output
  showing the single pid/boot_id assertion sampled across the window.
- Injection proof: reintroduce the Q07Y5-class defect (apply the drain budget
  to the server's whole life instead of the drain phase) and show the soak
  catches it — daemon dies mid-window, soak exits nonzero with a message
  naming when it died. Restore, green. This proves the gate watches the class,
  not the code path R74E8 already guards.
- A second, different uptime defect class is demonstrated caught (suggested: a
  short-interval timer/watcher misbehavior injected artificially) — one
  exemplar beyond Q07Y5's, to show the gate is not overfit.
- The soak NEVER touches the installed runtime, the real LaunchAgent, or
  `$ORGASMIC_HOME` proper — asserted in the script itself, not just documented.

=== Non-goals

- Not the PR test lane (TASK-S2KM0); this is the scheduled long-run complement.
- No multi-hour endurance matrix; one honest daily soak at minutes-scale first.
- Do not run harness/provider turns in the soak — zero billed cost by
  construction.

Related: TASK-S2KM0 (CI), TASK-VZMZE (a defect exactly this gate would
express), memory "orgasmic daemon uptime blindspot".

* DONE TASK-WFW1N Worker-driven dispatch finalize verb (orgasmic dispatch finalize) :daemon:cli:dispatch:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-WFW1N
:MOTIVATED_BY: dec_3M7M0
:PRIORITY: high
:END:

Implements dec_3M7M0. Replace inferred TUI-driver finalization (guess done + scrape scrollback + unconfirmed commit) with a worker-declared completion call over the existing worker->daemon write channel.

** Scope
1. CLI verb `orgasmic dispatch finalize` (worker-side counterpart to `manager dispatch-close`):
   - flags: --run <run-id> (or --task), --status done|failed, --commit (stage+commit the worktree), --summary-file <path> (authoritative report text; also accept stdin), --worker-commit passthrough.
   - Behavior via a daemon endpoint: record the terminal event; write last.txt from --summary-file (NOT scraped); if --commit, commit the worktree; emit implementer.done / reviewer.done (by run kind); release the lease. One daemon call, atomic finalize.
2. Prompt-spec contract: add "your contract ends by calling `orgasmic dispatch finalize --run $RUN_ID --status done --commit --summary-file <report>`" to the implementer + reviewer worker personas (shipped/prompt-studio/prompt-specs or the worker templates), so it is universal, not per-brief. Thread $RUN_ID into the worker env/prompt so the worker knows its run id.
3. Demote the scrape/stall path to FALLBACK: if a finalize event arrived for a run, the release path must NOT overwrite last.txt from scrollback; stall-detection only fires "no finalize within timeout -> mark orphan / rescue-needed", not "assume done + scrape".
4. (Optional, belt-and-suspenders) a harness stop-hook that calls finalize if the worker did not.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `orgasmic dispatch finalize` writes last.txt verbatim from --summary-file (test: content matches input exactly, no scrollback contamination).
- [ ] --commit produces the worktree commit as part of finalize; a finalize with uncommitted changes + --commit leaves a clean committed worktree (commit-stall impossible).
- [ ] finalize emits the correct terminal tx (implementer.done/reviewer.done) and releases the lease; manager dispatch-status shows the run closed.
- [ ] When finalize arrived, the driver release path does NOT scrape/overwrite the report (regression test).
- [ ] When finalize did NOT arrive within the stall window, the run is flagged orphan (not silently marked done) — verified by a test simulating a worker that never finalizes.
- [ ] Worker prompt specs carry the finalize contract; a dispatched worker calls it (verify on a live rmux smoke).
- [ ] gates: daemon + cli green, clippy -D, fmt.

** Notes
Does not fix host-kill-before-finalize (dec_3M7M0 residual): that path yields no finalize event + uncommitted worktree = detectable + rescuable, which is the intended bound. ACP drivers already have protocol finalize; this brings TUI drivers (rmux/tmux) to parity. Reuses manager dispatch-close plumbing where possible (same terminal-tx + lease-release, different caller/authority).

* DONE TASK-WGXKD a worker finalize can lose its terminal tx because releasing the lease kills the process that writes it :dispatch:cli:defect:race:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-WGXKD
:PRIORITY: P0
:BLOCKED_BY: TASK-R74E8
:END:

MEASURED 2026-07-27 on run run-20260727T131952-9138610466c24c469819ac27e3f6c504 (TASK-RWCRN, implementer-claude-acp-stdio, rebuilt runtime 4d1369a). A worker called `orgasmic dispatch finalize --summary-file ... --commit` and it half-applied: the commit landed (2a69f66 at 13:51:57Z), last.txt was written (16566 bytes), the lease release succeeded and the daemon emitted run_complete with summary "worker finalize for TASK-RWCRN" (session seq 984) — but NO terminal tx was ever written, to either the project or the home ledger. dispatch-status reported [pid-gone] [run-live] [unreported]. The very next session event, seq 985, is a fatal driver_error: "claude exited with status signal: 9 (SIGKILL)".

THE MECHANISM. cmd_dispatch_finalize (crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:1213-1218) deliberately orders the terminal tx LAST, after commit, last.txt and lease release, and the comment states the intent: "If any earlier step fails or the process dies, no completion tx is on record — the run stalls and is flagged orphan (rescuable), never a done claim with no report + a held lease." The ordering is sound in isolation but is self-cancelling in production: step 2 (release_dispatch_run_with_reason, manager.rs:1246) tears down the driver, which SIGKILLs the harness process — and the `orgasmic dispatch finalize` CLI is a descendant of that same harness shell. Release kills the process that still has to perform step 3. The wider the gap between release and the tx POST, the more likely the loss.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC. The stated fallback did not occur either: the run was not flagged orphan, and the daemon log has no "release without worker finalize, flagging orphan" line for this run — because from the daemon side the release WAS a worker finalize. So the run lands in a fourth state the design did not anticipate: work durable, report durable, lease released, no terminal tx, no orphan flag. It is invisible to both the success path and the rescue path. The manager only noticed because dispatch-status printed [unreported], which exists solely because of TASK-6AYEJ.

NOT a TASK-6AYEJ regression: 6AYEJ changed WHICH tx type finalize emits (implementer.reported instead of implementer.done), not when it is emitted. The ordering predates it. 6AYEJ is what made the failure visible rather than silent.

FREQUENCY. Timing-dependent, not deterministic. The daemon log shows many successful "worker finalized via orgasmic dispatch finalize, skipping scrape" lines on 07-26, so the tx usually wins the race.

CANDIDATE FIXES, to be argued rather than assumed:
1. Move the terminal tx BEFORE the release, accepting the risk the design comment was avoiding (a done claim with a held lease) and mitigating it with the release immediately after.
2. Have the daemon emit the terminal tx as part of the release-with-finalization call, so it is server-side and cannot be lost to client death. This looks strongest: the daemon already knows finalized_by_worker=true and the tx content is derivable from the run record.
3. Keep the client-side tx but make the release non-fatal to the caller (defer harness teardown until the client disconnects or a grace period elapses).

ACCEPTANCE. A worker finalize whose harness is killed the instant the lease is released still produces its terminal tx; proven by a test that kills the finalizing client between release and tx, plus one live dispatch. dispatch-status must never again show a released run as [unreported] after a successful finalize.

CORRECTION [2026-07-29, TASK-37TAF]: this task's record carried "Old CLI + new daemon is compatible: absent terminal_tx defaults to None and the old client does its existing POST /tx" under do-not-re-litigate. DISPROVEN and closed: on acp-stdio the release kills the old client's process group before its POST /tx (the same argument this task's own finding 1 made for the other direction). TASK-37TAF (merged 2026-07-29) closed it by refusing finalized_by_worker releases with no terminal_tx at post_run_release. Both skew directions are now fail-closed: new CLI/old daemon by the client-side capability probe, old CLI/new daemon by the server-side payload guard. Also noted: this task reached DONE before 37TAF resolved, despite 37TAF's body requiring otherwise — the both-directions claim is only true as of 37TAF's merge.

* DONE TASK-WGXKD.1 terminal-tx emission must survive version skew and graceful daemon shutdown :dispatch:daemon:cli:defect:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-WGXKD.1
:PRIORITY: P0
:END:

Fix round for the TASK-WGXKD reviewer BLOCK SHIP (run-20260728T054156-cc1dc747e09c42898e9805950fac473f, merge 80dc4ec). Two HIGH findings, verbatim below.

** Finding 1 - HIGH correctness: the version-skew fallback is unreachable on the transport that motivated the task
manager.rs:1326-1412. The new client waits for /runs/:id/release to return and only then POSTs /tx when terminal_tx_id is absent. A pre-80dc4ec daemon ignores the unknown terminal_tx field, performs only release_with_finalization, and returns the old response shape. On acp-stdio that release calls reap_process_group (crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/subprocess_stream_json.rs:231-242) and signals the finalize CLI's own setsid group BEFORE the response or the fallback can execute.

So new CLI + old daemon reproduces the original defect exactly: durable commit, durable report, released lease, no terminal tx. The claimed version-skew safety is false for precisely the transport WGXKD existed to fix. This is a realistic upgrade / source-build window - the two halves ship in one runtime bundle but a user can run a freshly built CLI against a daemon that has not been restarted yet.

FIX DIRECTION (reviewer): add a pre-release capability handshake for atomic release+terminal-tx support. If the daemon lacks it, FAIL BEFORE RELEASING and tell the operator to restart/upgrade the daemon - do not rely on a post-release client fallback, because on subprocess transports there is no 'post-release' for the client. Add a version-skew regression that reproduces pre-80dc4ec daemon behaviour on acp-stdio and asserts either atomic reporting or refusal with the lease still held.

Note the failure mode of the fix itself: refusing to release leaves the lease held, which is the state the ORIGINAL ordering comment was trying to avoid. That is acceptable here because a held lease is visible and rescuable, whereas the lost tx is the invisible fourth state. Say so explicitly in the code comment so the next reader does not 'fix' it back.

** Finding 2 - HIGH correctness: the detached finalization task is not owned by graceful shutdown
api.rs:6561-6565. The detached task's only JoinHandle lives in the request future. When the caller disconnects - which is the normal case this whole fix exists for - that handle is dropped and the task continues untracked.

Controlled restart drains only work already enqueued in the writer (api.rs:9630-9665), while daemon shutdown stops the writer immediately after axum returns (crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/lib.rs:637-650). If a restart lands while the detached task is still in driver teardown or has not yet reached append_tx_request, the drain barrier can pass first, the writer and runtime shut down, and the terminal tx is lost.

This is a normal graceful-restart race, DISTINCT from the already-accepted daemon-crash gap. It is live on the manager's own machine: every launchctl kickstart of orgasmic.daemon during a runtime rebuild is exactly this window.

The existing disconnect test does not cover it - it widens the gap to three seconds via release_terminal_tx_delay but then waits for the tx before shutting down.

FIX DIRECTION (reviewer): register release/finalization tasks in daemon-owned lifecycle state, e.g. a task tracker or JoinSet held outside request futures. Graceful restart/shutdown must stop accepting new releases, await those tasks, THEN place the writer drain barrier and shut the writer down. Add a test that disconnects during release_terminal_tx_delay, initiates controlled restart before the append, and proves the terminal tx is durable before the old daemon exits.

** Reviewer conclusions that are NOT findings - do not re-litigate
- append_tx_request extraction is faithful: POST /tx delegates directly to it, so actor choice, destination, tx-id policy and project/home refresh are identical for both callers.
- Generation ordering is safe: the terminal tx carries the exact RUN_ID, mark_matching_dispatch_reported fails closed on a present-but-unmatched run id, and dispatch creation rejects overlapping open task records.
- The failed-append shape is visible: release removes the run before the terminal append, append failure is logged and returned, dispatch-status leaves the record [run-gone] [unreported] and --orphans-only includes it. That was the acceptance floor and it is met.
- Old CLI + new daemon is compatible: absent terminal_tx defaults to None and the old client does its existing POST /tx.
- No reachable restart double-emission was found. Caveat carried forward: writer request-id caching is in-memory only, so any FUTURE transport-error fallback would need persistent ledger-aware dedupe.

** Manager note
The reviewer asked in Open Questions whether the live acp-stdio trial passed. That trial is the TASK-6AYEJ.2 dispatch on the rebuilt runtime; its result will be recorded on TASK-WGXKD when it lands. It does not gate this fix round - both findings are code-level and hold regardless of the trial outcome.

* DONE TASK-WGXKD.2 release admission must be atomic with tracker closure; restart must actually await the drain :dispatch:daemon:cli:defect:race:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-WGXKD.2
:PRIORITY: P0
:END:

Fix round for the TASK-WGXKD.1 reviewer BLOCK SHIP (run-20260728T063208-1080f3a600dc40b6946754da476afca8, merge 1fbc3f7). Findings verbatim.

IMPORTANT CORROBORATION: finding 1 was found INDEPENDENTLY by a second reviewer in a separate worktree - it is finding 3 of the TASK-6AYEJ.2 review (run-20260728T063207-654ec2af0d5140ffbb091ed15de786d1), with the same file:line anchors and the same conclusion. Two independent derivations; treat it as confirmed, not speculative.

** Finding 1 - HIGH: release admission is not atomic with tracker closure
api.rs:217-240, 6672-6702, 9857-9861. post_run_release reads is_closed() and THEN awaits supervisor.snapshot() before calling spawn(). close() only flips an independent atomic flag, while spawn() increments active unconditionally and never rechecks the closed state. On the multi-thread runtime a release can read false, restart can then close the tracker and observe active == 0, and the release can register and run AFTER the release drain and potentially after the writer barrier. That recreates the exact graceful-shutdown loss this task exists to eliminate: the lease is released while its terminal tx lands after the barrier or dies with the service.

The added late-release assertion does not cover this straddling request - it sends the release only after the restart response, when is_closed() is already true. The endpoint test at dispatch_endpoint.rs:3734-3774 sleeps 500ms until it is inside the injected delay and only then requests restart, so it proves waiting for an ALREADY-REGISTERED task, not atomic close-versus-registration.

FIX DIRECTION: replace the separate is_closed() + spawn() sequence with one atomic admission operation (try_acquire / try_spawn) that checks closed and increments active under the same synchronization boundary, acquired BEFORE any await that restart can overtake. If closure won, drop the count and return 503. Add a barrier-controlled race test with a deterministic hook between handler admission and tracker registration, raced against controlled restart, proving the release is either tracked to completion or rejected.

** Finding 2 - HIGH: the real restart command abandons the drain after 5s, discards warnings, and stops the service anyway
daemon_lifecycle.rs:242, 847-868; api.rs:145-148, 9856-9877; main.rs:1795-1833. request_restart_drain() gives the HTTP request a 5-SECOND timeout, DROPS the send() result, returns Ok, and stop_inner() immediately invokes the OS service stop. The new API may legitimately wait 15 seconds. Driver teardown alone is budgeted 5s plus producer join 5s (supervisor.rs:4021-4051), and rmux can spend 2s on the SDK kill plus 2s on the CLI fallback (rmux.rs:83-87, 1514-1525). So a realistic teardown exceeds the lifecycle client's 5s fuse before the terminal tx append.

The endpoint warning is not actionable because the CLI never parses it. And the non-restart mirror in lib.rs is NOT a backstop for service shutdown: cmd_serve converts only Ctrl+C into RunningDaemon.shutdown, whereas LaunchAgent/systemd stop terminates the service.

MANAGER VERIFIED THIS DIRECTLY: crates/orgasmic-cli/src/main.rs:1830-1831 awaits tokio::signal::ctrl_c() and nothing else - there is no SIGTERM handler. Every launchctl kickstart -k of orgasmic.daemon, which is the manager's standard runtime-rebuild step and has run four times today, therefore SIGTERMs the daemon WITHOUT running the finalization drain at all. The graceful-shutdown fix is currently unreachable on the only shutdown path this machine actually uses.

The passing integration test uses a 3s delay and calls /daemon/restart directly, staying below the hidden 5s production boundary and never exercising service stop.

FIX DIRECTION: make the lifecycle restart request typed and authoritative - timeout GREATER than release-finalization plus writer-drain budgets, propagate request failures, parse RestartResponse, and do not stop the service after a drain timeout without a durable recovery plan. Include run ids / dispatch generations and copyable rescue commands in timeout output. Route SIGTERM and service-stop through RunningDaemon.shutdown so the library drain actually runs. Add an end-to-end lifecycle test with a delay beyond 5s and the real stop sequence.

** Finding 3 - MEDIUM: a panicked or aborted finalization decrements the count but its lost tx is invisible
api.rs:178-195, 230-239, 6702-6705. The drop guard correctly lets wait_idle() finish, but the tracker retains only a COUNT, not the JoinHandle or the completion outcome. The sole join-error log lives in the HTTP request future - and dropping that future is the NORMAL worker-finalize case this whole change documents. If the detached task panics after release and before append, the guard moves the count to zero, restart reports a clean drain, and no durable warning or rescue record identifies the lost tx. There is no panic/abort regression test. This is a live-daemon task failure, NOT the accepted whole-daemon crash gap.

FIX DIRECTION: give the tracker ownership of task OUTCOMES, not just a count. Catch and retain panic/abort results keyed by run id and intended terminal tx, surface them through restart warnings and dispatch recovery/status, and add panic/abort tests proving both count release and visible loss recovery.

** Reviewer conclusions that are settled - do not re-litigate
- The duplicated capability string has effective integration coverage: CLI finalize tests run against the current daemon and would fail if the constants drifted.
- Failing closed on transient probe errors is the CORRECT safety trade, because the retry remains pre-commit and the error includes the underlying transport/HTTP detail.
- scripts/install.sh can temporarily place a new CLI in front of an old daemon, but its final orgasmic status staleness check prints 'restart recommended'. orgasmic update performs the restart itself. No silent standard upgrade path was found beyond the defects above.
- The one-way close is consistent with the pre-existing one-way acquisition pause; not filed separately. Fixing finding 2 should make restart failure/timeout explicit and define whether the daemon reopens or stays quiesced.
- The TASK-6AYEJ.2 interaction leaves a USABLE path, not a dead end: dispatch-status prints TX_ID, tokened close remains available, and fresh recovery records run.created ORIGIN=recovery. Caveat: the WGXKD refusal text's 'run the same finalize command again' is optimistic - the operator may first need orgasmic recovery status / orgasmic run recover. Consider softening that text while you are here.

** Description
Hit live [2026-06-10] dispatching TASK-TGGAJ via =orgasmic manager dispatch=
(rmux + claude). The CLI HTTP client has a hardcoded 10s timeout
(=daemon_client.rs= =from_home=, ~line 44) while a real rmux+claude dispatch
takes longer server-side (session spawn + claude TUI startup + 10s
=input_ready_timeout= wait + brief paste). Failure cascade observed:

1. CLI times out ("error sending request"), reports failure, and removes the
   worktree it created — while the daemon proceeds and spawns a real claude
   whose cwd has just been deleted (run-20260610T183047). The worker is doomed
   but holds the (task, kind) supervisor lease.
2. The zombie lease then 409s every redispatch ("another dispatch is already
   active") while =GET /runs/:id= 404s and =POST /runs/:id/release= refuses
   ("active run ... not found" pattern) — no API path clears it; only a daemon
   restart does (observed twice: run-...T182512, run-...T183047).
3. The CLI's failure cleanup removes the worktree but NOT the branch, so the
   next attempt dies on "a branch named 'task-NNN-impl' already exists".

Workaround used today: dispatch directly via =curl= against
=/projects/:id/tasks/:task/dispatch= with a long timeout and a pre-created
worktree — which also skips the CLI-side lifecycle stage flips (had to apply
BACKLOG->IN_PROGRESS by hand).

UPDATE [2026-06-10 22:35]: operator commit =ab7bb93= addressed most of this —
Fix 2 (non-blocking acquire: drivers send Ready at spawn, paste moves off the
HTTP path; CLI dispatch POST gets a dedicated 30s timeout) kills the
timeout-vs-spawn race, Fix 3 adds =Supervisor::release_orphaned_lease= +
=POST /projects/:p/tasks/:t/lease/release= + =orgasmic manager lease-release=
(no more restart-to-clear). REMAINING SCOPE before dispatching this task:
verify under the new code, then fix only what's left — most likely the CLI
failure-cleanup still deleting the worktree while a daemon-side spawn may
have started, and never deleting the created branch (the "branch already
exists" retry papercut). Re-scope or close as covered if nothing reproduces.

UPDATE [2026-06-11 manager re-validation]: batch-1 ran two normal-path CLI
dispatches (TASK-RVEKT, TASK-CJWT3.1) plus both closes on the =981e3f3= binary —
all completed in ~1s, lifecycle auto-flips fired, no worktree deletion, no
zombie lease, no leftover branch (=--worktree-remove --branch-delete= both
honored). Caveat: spawns were fast, so the slow-spawn (>30s) window was never
entered — consistent-with-fixed, not proof. RE-SCOPED to the remainder: (a) a
forced-slow-spawn regression test for the CLI timeout path, (b) failure-path
cleanup ordering (worktree delete must not race a started daemon spawn;
branch must be deleted on failure cleanup). Consider folding (a) into
TASK-BRXGG's parallel-safety work — same test surface.

FENCING INVARIANT (round-3 critique, point 3b — adopted; UPGRADED per round-4
critique §5, conceded [2026-06-11]): the round-3 wording ("CLI consults the
daemon's authority, then deletes") is still check-then-act over HTTP — a
TOCTOU window survives between the daemon's answer and the CLI's delete. The
destructive act itself moves daemon-side: cleanup of anything a spawned
worker may own is EXECUTED by the daemon — kill the worker's process group,
=waitpid= for confirmed death, and only then the daemon deletes
worktree+branch (reuse the =reap_process_group= machinery). The CLI only
*requests* cleanup and reports the daemon's result. CLI-local deletion stays
legitimate only for resources the daemon provably never learned about (the
dispatch request never reached it).

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CLI dispatch HTTP timeout either raised well above worst-case rmux spawn
  (e.g. 120s+), made configurable, or the dispatch route made async
  (daemon returns run_id immediately, spawn completes in background).
- [ ] Worktree/branch cleanup for a possibly-spawned worker is executed
  daemon-side (PGID kill → waitpid → daemon deletes), per the fencing
  invariant above; the CLI only requests it and reports the result. CLI-local
  deletion happens only when the daemon provably never received the dispatch,
  and removes the created branch whenever it removes the worktree.
- [ ] Supervisor lease for a failed/dead spawn is always releasable: either
  auto-released when the spawn errors/session dies, or =POST /runs/:id/release=
  (or a new endpoint) can clear a lease whose run never registered.
- [ ] Regression tests for the timeout path in
  =crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs= (slow-daemon stub).
- [ ] Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-cli, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check, MSRV 1.78.

  /projects/:id/tasks/:task/dispatch/cleanup= executes release (driver

  sweep → wait) BEFORE =git worktree remove --force= + =git branch -D=;
  CLI requests it on timeout/transport failures and only deletes

* DONE TASK-WYSMM Mobile: selection-comment quote stuck on first word; extend-selection never updates the composer :ui:bug:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-WYSMM
:END:

On mobile browsers, long-press selects one word and touchend opens the inline comment composer quoting only that word. Dragging the native selection handles to extend the selection never updates the quote: handle drags do not dispatch pointerup/touchend to the page (only document.selectionchange fires), and ArtifactView captures the anchor exactly once on pointerup/touchend/keyup. Fix: keep the captured anchor in sync via a debounced document selectionchange listener while the composer is eligible, re-capturing when the selection is non-collapsed inside the artifact body and preserving the existing quote when the selection collapses (e.g. focusing the textarea).

TASK-FWBYB.1 hardened it (=DaemonLiveness= enum + exactly-one liveness signal when daemon not-Running). The check is real, validated end-to-end, and silent when daemon is fresh.

Open follow-up (cited in goal.org and TASK-FWBYB notes): users running their normal =orgasmic status= command don't see the staleness warning — only =orgasmic doctor= surfaces it. =orgasmic status= is the more common liveness check (one-line output: boot_id + uptime + projects + parse_errors + tx count). Surfacing the staleness Warn there means users notice "you're running a stale daemon binary" without needing to remember to run doctor.

Fix shape (small, ~30-100 LOC):

* DONE TASK-XCJYC Rename non-ACP transports and reserve acp-* for the real protocol :drivers:cli:naming:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-XCJYC
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Problem: orgasmic uses "acp" for transports that are not the Agent Client Protocol. ACP is a specific open standard from Zed Industries (released August 2025, JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio for local agents, HTTP/WebSocket for remote): it standardises the editor-to-agent boundary while MCP standardises tool access. It is adopted by JetBrains, Google, GitHub and 25+ agents, and Zed ships an ACP Registry containing Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and others.

What orgasmic labels `acp` is not that:
- `acp-stdio` + claude runs `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json` — Claude Code's own stream-json wire
- `acp-stdio` / `acp-ws` + codex runs `codex app-server` — Codex's own JSON-RPC app-server
- `cursor-acp` is a cursor-agent adapter

The source half-knows: `adapters/claude.rs` documents itself as "ACP-like stdio stream-json", and the `protocol_version` values are already honest (`claude-code-stream-json/1`, `codex-appserver/1`). Only the wrapper names lie. One genuine error remains at `adapters/claude.rs:364`, which reports `protocol_version: "acp/1"`.

Cost, in increasing order of severity:
1. It misleads readers into treating two unrelated native protocols as one protocol's two implementations. This happened twice in one manager session on 2026-07-25.
2. It hides that ACP-vs-MCP is a live architectural distinction, precisely the layering an operator asking for a worker "without MCP" is reasoning about.
3. It squats on the name. If orgasmic adds real ACP, the correct name is taken by something that is not it.

Decision (operator, 2026-07-25): modes name the wire only, since the harness field already determines the protocol.
- `("acp-stdio", H)` becomes `("stdio", H)`
- `("acp-ws", H)` becomes `("ws", H)`
- driver id `claude-acp` becomes `claude-stream-json`; `cursor-acp` becomes `cursor-agent`
- `acp-stdio` and `acp-ws` are reserved for real ACP and must not be reused for anything else

Scope: roughly 371 occurrences of `acp` across 12+ files, concentrated in `orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs`, the CLI and daemon dispatch tests, `orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs`, `orgasmic-daemon/src/config.rs`, and the drivers crate.

This is a cutover, not a find-and-replace. `--mode acp-stdio` is user-facing, the pair list is the `SUPPORTED` matrix authority per dec_WDR5K item 1, and the old names are persisted: 70 historical runs carry `transport: "acp-stdio"` and 1 carries `acp-ws`, plus worker ids such as `reviewer-codex-acp-stdio` throughout tx history.

Work:
1. Rename the mode pairs, driver ids, transport constants, and the `acp/1` protocol_version error.
2. Follow dec_WDR5K item 10's precedent for historical data: no alias table, old records render their historical strings as plain text. Confirm the recovery classifier and transcript finder still resolve pre-rename records, since `persisted_run_address_from_session` reads `transport` from old RunMeta.
3. Record the reservation so a future contributor cannot re-take `acp-*` for a non-ACP transport.
4. Add a glossary term distinguishing ACP, MCP, and orgasmic's transport modes.

Acceptance:
- no identifier, mode value, doc comment or protocol_version calls a non-ACP transport "acp"
- pre-rename session records still classify and still resolve to their native transcripts
- `acp-stdio` and `acp-ws` are unused and documented as reserved
** Amendment: cursor-acp keeps its name
MANAGER RULING [2026-08-03], after verifying the implementer's reasoning rather
than accepting it. The 2026-07-25 decision listed `cursor-acp` -> `cursor-agent`
as one of four renames. That line item is WITHDRAWN. `cursor-acp` keeps its name.

Two independently verified reasons:

1. *The rename is impossible as written.* `cursor-agent` is ALREADY a live
   legacy transport id — =legacy_driver!(CursorAgentDriver, "cursor-agent", ...)=
   with ="cursor-agent" => Some(Box::new(CursorAgentDriver))= in =driver_for=.
   Renaming onto it produces a duplicate key, and
   =registry_covers_every_transport= asserts =driver_for(t).transport() == t=,
   which two entries cannot both satisfy. One of the two cursor pairs would
   become unreachable by legacy id.

2. *The name is TRUE, so renaming it would delete information.* =cursor_acp.rs=
   really does speak the Agent Client Protocol — verified: =session/new=,
   =session/prompt=, =session/update=, =session/request_permission=. The
   acceptance criterion on this task is that no *NON-ACP* transport is called
   "acp". cursor-acp is ACP, so the criterion is already met, and this adapter
   is the one whose name tells a reader it speaks the standard.

This is consistent with the decision's own principle rather than an exception to
it: a MODE names the wire, and the HARNESS decides the protocol. So
=("stdio", "cursor-agent")= carrying ACP is exactly the intended shape.

The implementer declined to invent a third name the operator had not chosen, or
to delete the `cursor-agent` alias to free the string. That was the right call
on both counts and is recorded here so a future reader does not "finish" the
rename.
** Reviewer verdict and resolution
REVIEWER VERDICT [2026-08-03], reviewer-codex-tmux (gpt-5.6-sol/high), diff
=db40c97..d54fba5=: *REJECT* on one P1, now RESOLVED in =dd494ab=.

*The finding, and it was fair.* The cutover stripped the ACP umbrella from
identifiers, mode values and protocol_versions but left it in two comments,
which this task's acceptance criterion covers by name:
- =trait.rs:343,349= called the shared JSON-RPC session/turn hooks "ACP-like
  runtimes" IN THE SAME SENTENCE that contrasts Codex app-server's
  =thread/start= with real ACP's =session/new=. The comment knew they were
  different protocols; the umbrella made them read as two dialects of one.
- =ui/src/lib/runLabels.ts:27= called every non-PTY live surface the "ACP chat
  transcript", which covers claude stream-json and codex app-server.
Both predate the cutover, so this was a MISSED CRITERION, not a regression.
Fixed to "session-oriented JSON-RPC runtimes" and "structured chat transcript";
swept for other instances, none remain.

*The reviewer improved on the implementer's proof.* Residual Risk #1 declared
that historical resolution was argued from two tests rather than executed,
because the =cfg(test)= registry fence blocks the composition. The reviewer went
around the fence entirely and probed PRODUCTION: the real session for
=run-20260726T102724-...= records =transport: "acp-stdio"=, and =orgasmic run
native-transcript= resolved it to Codex rollout =019f9df7-...= with
=status: found=, =confidence: high= and filename correlation. That closes the
native-transcript half of the historical criterion with a LIVE ARTIFACT. No
local =acp-ws= record exists to probe, so that variant stays covered by source
inspection and focused tests.

Residual Risk #2 was judged LOWER than the implementer stated, verified:
=WsDriver::attach= returns =NotReattachable= directly and =StdioDriver::attach=
delegates to =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver::attach=, which does the same without
spawning.

*Two gaps in the review, stated so nobody reads it as broader than it was.*
1. The reservation guard's NEGATIVE probe was not run — the reviewer holds a
   strictly read-only contract and the brief asked it to mutate source. That was
   the MANAGER'S BRIEFING ERROR, not a reviewer failure. The guard's positive
   test passes and the implementer ran the negative probe itself; a read-only
   reviewer simply cannot be the one to repeat it. Future review briefs should
   not ask for source mutation.
2. No broad suite was re-run (host had two concurrent dispatches), so
   daemon-lib, drivers, core, cli_parity/dispatch and ui remain IMPLEMENTER
   CLAIMS rather than independent verification. The merge was proven
   byte-identical to the gated branch, which is what makes that acceptable.

* DONE TASK-XPYRR a task title cannot be corrected through any CLI surface, so a retracted claim outlives its correction
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-XPYRR
:PRIORITY: P1
:TAGS: cli,daemon,org-surface
:END:
** Description
A task heading's title cannot be changed through any CLI surface. `task update`
takes `--state`, `--priority`, `--reason` and `--property`, and rejects
`--title` with `unexpected argument`. `node body set` edits prose and named
sections, never the heading line. `node prop set` edits the drawer. Nothing
edits the title.

=== Why it matters, concretely

TASK-0RCRY was filed on 2026-07-28 with a diagnosis that was **retracted the
same day** (tx-20260728-orgasmic-3226): the claim that workers inherit the
daemon's `$TMUX`. The body was rewritten around the one surviving fact and now
opens with an explicit correction. **The title could not be rewritten**, so the
board still reads:

  "Workers inherit the daemon's $TMUX, so tmux tests talk to the rmux server
   and six gated tests never run"

The title is the most-read field on the board — it is what `dispatch-status`,
the task lists and every survey print. A retracted claim sitting in a heading
outlives the correction in the body, and the only reader guaranteed to see the
correction is one who opens the task.

The manager cannot fix this by hand: `.orgasmic` is daemon-owned and hand-edits
are forbidden. So the wrong title is currently unfixable by any sanctioned path.

=== Same class as TASK-JQARS

JQARS was about a documented command that did not exist. This is the inverse:
a field the product plainly owns, with no surface to write it. Both leave an
operator with a state they can observe and cannot change.

=== Ask

1. Add title editing to the task surface, through the daemon with the same OCC +
   structural guard as the other node writes. `task update --title` is the
   obvious shape given the flag already suggested by clap's own "a similar
   argument exists" tip.
2. Decide and record whether a title edit is allowed to change the org tags on
   the title line, or whether tags stay a separate concern. Do not let a title
   write silently drop tags — the heading line carries both.
3. Check the same question for the other node kinds that have titles (decision,
   architecture, glossary, goal). Report which already have a write path and
   which do not; fix only the ones in scope and file the rest.
4. Fix TASK-0RCRY's title as the acceptance demonstration, to:
   "No tmux call site passes -L/-S, so every probe and test session shares one
    server — on a dev box, the operator's own"

=== Acceptance

- `orgasmic task update <id> --title "..."` rewrites the heading, preserves the
  drawer, the body, all named sections and the org tags, and records a tx.
- Prove it by injection: a test that rewrites a title and asserts tags and body
  survive fails if the tag-preserving path is removed. Show it red, then green.
- A title containing org-significant characters (`*` at line start, `:tag:`
  shapes, trailing colons) either round-trips or is rejected with a reason — say
  which you chose and why. A silently corrupted heading is worse than a refusal.
- TASK-0RCRY reads correctly on the board afterwards.

=== Non-goals

- Do not add a general "edit any org line" escape hatch. The structural guard is
  the reason these surfaces are narrow.

* DONE TASK-XQ89W cascade-release babysitter when implementer run terminates (no orphans) :daemon:supervisor:babysitter:lifecycle:bug:polish:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID:               TASK-XQ89W
:PRIORITY:         P3
:WORKER:           implementer-codex-stdio
:IMPLEMENTS:
:PRODUCES:         crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs
:WRITE_SCOPE:      crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs
:READ_SCOPE:       crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/r#trait.rs
:TEST_CMD:         cargo test --workspace
:DEPENDS_ON:       TASK-KFGDS TASK-KFGDS.1
:END:

** Description
Deferred-MEDIUM finding from TASK-KFGDS reviewer pass: when the implementer run terminates, the spawned babysitter should also release. Currently =RunRecord= (=crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs:148-162=) stores a =babysitter_target: Option<String>= field that's set on BABYSITTER runs (pointing back at their parent implementer run_id) but NOT a companion =babysitter_run_id= on IMPLEMENTER runs. So when the implementer's =release()= fires (=supervisor.rs:814=), the supervisor doesn't know which babysitter run is its companion and the babysitter run continues writing to its .babysitter.jsonl indefinitely.

This was a known gap on the original cursor/subprocess-stream-json path too; TASK-KFGDS.1's babysitter spawn just extended the pattern to acp-stdio without fixing the cascade-release. With babysitters now spawning on every CLI dispatch (post-TASK-KFGDS.1), orphan babysitter runs accumulate on every clean implementer.done. Worth fixing.

Fix shape (small, ~30-60 LOC):
1. Add =babysitter_run_id: Option<String>= to =RunRecord= (set when supervisor auto-spawns the babysitter after implementer acquire).
2. In =Supervisor::release= when =rec.kind == RunKind::Implementer= AND =rec.babysitter_run_id.is_some()=, cascade-release the babysitter via the same release path.
3. Regression test: spawn implementer + auto-babysitter; release implementer; assert babysitter run is also released (= no longer in supervisor.runs).

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1 RunRecord companion field*: add =babysitter_run_id: Option<String>= to =RunRecord=. Set it at babysitter auto-spawn site (search for where =AcquireRequest.babysitter: Some(...)= triggers the babysitter spawn — that's where the new babysitter run gets its run_id; record it on the parent implementer's RunRecord).
- [ ] *F-2 cascade release*: extend =Supervisor::release= so that when an Implementer run releases AND has a non-null =babysitter_run_id=, it also calls release on the babysitter run (with a reason like ="cascade from implementer <run_id>"=). Order: release implementer first, then babysitter (avoid the babysitter writing a "lost parent" event mid-cascade). Idempotency: if the babysitter is already released (e.g., user manually released), don't error.
- [ ] *F-3 regression test*: in =supervisor.rs= tests, synthesize an implementer acquire with =babysitter: Some(BabysitterAutoSpawn { ... })=. Assert that AFTER spawn, =supervisor.runs= contains both runs AND the implementer's RunRecord has =babysitter_run_id == Some(<bs run id>)=. Then call =release()= on the implementer. Assert: (a) implementer is released, (b) babysitter is also released (gone from =supervisor.runs= OR has =terminal_outcome.is_some()=).
- [ ] All gates green: =cargo test --workspace=, =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings=, =cargo fmt --check=, =git diff --check=. MSRV 1.78.

** Notes
- *NOT* =:FIX_SUBTASK: t= — full IMPLEMENT → REVIEW → DONE lifecycle. Small scope but earns a proper reviewer pass.
- *Worker*: =implementer-codex-stdio= — continued dogfood; cargo test --workspace will likely exercise approval-grant again (5th in-row implementer dispatch).
- *Out-of-scope*: don't restructure RunKind / RunRecord beyond adding the field. Don't change the babysitter spawn LOGIC; just track the resulting run_id. Don't touch =acp_stdio.rs= or driver code.

** Evidence
(populated at cluster close)

Operator decision [2026-07-28]: decisions.org is enough. The architecture layer makes orgasmic too heavy and adds redundant bureaucracy. Deliverable: a written report (artifact or task Evidence block) covering the inventory, the coupling risks, a staged plan with per-stage effort estimate, and an explicit recommendation. Plus a decision draft for decisions.org if the recommendation is GO.

** Scope of what "architecture" means here
1. The =arch_XXXXX= node class and =.orgasmic/architecture.org= (177 headings, 26 top-level subsystems, IMPLEMENTED + TARGET ARCHITECTURE sections).
2. The =architector= worker kind / =architect= stage: =POST /architect=, =stage_spec("architect")=, =WorkerKind::Architector=, =DispatchEndpointKind::Architector= ("architector-watch-then-integrate"), the architector prompt spec, and =manager architecture= stage plumbing.

5. UI: =ArchitectureView.tsx= (273 lines), NodeModal arch node views, router/routes entries, =descriptor.ts=, capabilities.
6. Shipped instruction surfaces: =shipped/prompt-studio/context-packs/architecture.org=, =shipped/prompt-studio/prompt-specs/manager.org=, =shipped/entry/router.org=, =shipped/schema/tx.org=, =shipped/skills/orgasmic/SKILL.md=, =shipped/skills/orgasmic/references/recall-resume.md=, =shipped/project-scaffold/tasks/{goal,backlog}.org=.
7. The =// orgasmic:arch_NNNNN= source marker convention and its drift comparator.

** Measured inventory (manager scan 2026-07-28, non-target, non-node_modules)
- =architecture.org=: 177 org headings, 26 top-level =arch_= subsystems, ~2100+ lines.
- =arch_= identifier occurrences by file (source only): api.rs 21, index.rs 25, org.rs 31, id.rs 22, schema.rs 21, architecture_drift.rs 20, marker.rs 10, identity_lint.rs 8, session.rs 8, plus fixtures/tests (integration.rs 21, fixtures.rs 19, bootstrap_smoke.rs, id_mint.rs, identity_lint.rs).
- =architect= occurrences: api.rs 94, main.rs 29, manager.rs 26, dispatch.rs (test) 25, index.rs 24, NodeModal.tsx 22, integration.rs 21, ArchitectureView.tsx 15.
- Source files carrying an =orgasmic:= header marker that names an =arch_= id: 51. Of those, 21 marker lines are arch-ONLY (no =dec_=/=TASK-= companion) — those 21 files lose their entire back-edge if arch ids are dropped, while 30 degrade gracefully to their decision/task ids.
- State coupling: =.orgasmic/tasks/done.org= has 335 =arch_= references, tx logs 151 (2026-06: 58, 2026-07: 93), =decisions.org= 15, =tasks/goal.org= 6, =tasks/backlog.org= 2 (=:IMPLEMENTS: arch_RN73Z= on two live backlog tasks).

** Questions the exploration must answer with evidence
1. *Is the source-marker back-edge worth keeping without arch nodes?* The drift comparator is the only mechanical code↔model link in the product. If arch dies, does =// orgasmic:dec_XXXXX, TASK-XXXXX= keep enough value to retain a (renamed, simplified) drift check, or does drift die with it? Name the 21 arch-only marker files and say what each would carry instead.
2. *What happens to history?* tx records and done.org are append-only narrative. Excision must NOT rewrite them (dec on ID migration set the precedent that history keeps old ids and stays resolvable via git). Confirm that dangling =arch_= references in immutable surfaces do not trip the identity lint / malformed-ID lint, or specify the lint carve-out needed.
3. *What do the 15 decisions.org =arch_= references become?* Several decisions cite arch nodes as pairing context (dec on recovery cites arch_Z3Z3V/arch_A53QX; dec on graph-page excision says arch_M8JQT "sheds its claims at excision"). Do those decisions need amendment, or is a dangling-but-historical reference acceptable?
4. *What absorbs the content that is actually load-bearing?* Some arch nodes carry real constraints (INTERFACE/CONSTRAINTS claims, =:SOURCE_PATHS:=). Decide per top-level subsystem: fold into the owning decision, drop, or park in an archive file. Give a rough count of nodes in each bucket — do not do the folding.
5. *Live task fallout*: two backlog tasks carry =:IMPLEMENTS: arch_RN73Z=. Enumerate every open task with an arch edge and say what the drawer becomes.
6. *Does anything block on architecture at runtime?* Specifically: does dispatch, boot reconciliation, or the read model fail if =architecture.org= is absent, or is it already optional? Test it — this determines whether excision is subtractive or requires new fallbacks.
7. *Precedent*: the Graph page excision (dec_ZG9B9 / TASK-M6146) is the closest prior art for removing a whole surface. Read what that cost in practice and calibrate against it.

** Estimate format required
Break the removal into stages that can each land and gate independently, e.g.: (a) stop producing — retire the architector worker kind + architect stage + create verbs; (b) retire the drift comparator and the marker convention; (c) remove read model + CLI + UI surfaces; (d) retire the file and the node class from core schema/id/lint; (e) shipped instruction surface rewrite. For each stage give: files touched, LOC delta estimate, test suites affected, whether it is reversible, and a rough dispatch-round count. Flag which stages are cheap and independently valuable even if the operator later declines full excision.

** Non-goals
Do not remove anything. Do not edit architecture.org. Do not rewrite tx or done.org. No source changes beyond a throwaway experiment for question 6 (which must be reverted). The output is a report and a decision draft.

One-round fix of the 8 reviewer.finding tx entries from the TASK-ZEFEY pass (run-20260703T194200). Mandatory items 1-4; LOWs 5-8 are in scope and small.

1. HIGH validate_mdx (artifacts.rs:110-144): replace the flat byte-scan with top-level structural validation - the daemon validates only what it can see without a real MDX parser: top-level block tags must be registered (BLOCK_TYPES), balanced, and well-formed; everything INSIDE a registered block's body is opaque and never scanned for unknown tags (that is where generics like Vec<Item>, f::<String>(), and DSL content legitimately live). Unclosed or malformed top-level tags are rejected. Deep/nested validation defers to the TASK-T25XQ JS/MDX parser. MANAGER RULING: empty or zero-registered-block content is REJECTED (an artifact must contain at least one registered top-level block). Use the reviewer's probe strings as the unit-test corpus with expected outcomes per this policy: <Code>let v: Vec<Item> = f::<String>();</Code> accepted; <EntityRelationship>A<Order>B</EntityRelationship> accepted (body opaque); bare prose, empty string, and unclosed <RichText rejected.
2. MEDIUM canonical parsing (artifacts.rs:148-172, 347-365): route artifact.org and reviews.org reads through orgasmic_core OrgFile::parse; delete the duplicate inline parsers. On write (comment_org_block :253-275), escape or reject comment bodies whose lines begin with * so a body can never truncate the heading structure or inject org syntax.
3. MEDIUM writer discipline: move archive_current_mdx and directory creation onto the writer path (or fold into the submit writer.transaction).
4. MEDIUM atomicity: comment add and consume each become a single writer.transaction bundling file rewrite + tx append, matching submit.
5. LOW duplicate artifact.created on retry (api.rs:8828): fold creation intent into the atomic transaction or make it idempotent.
6. LOW headerless reviews.org branch (artifacts.rs:504-511) seeds the #+title header; GET /artifacts/:id?version=N distinguishes no-such-version (404 with explicit message) from no-such-artifact.
7. LOW escape :PROMPT:/:TITLE: to single-line on write (tx.org:206 already promises this).
8. LOW WS events carry the artifact's actual state, not hardcoded "submitted".

MANAGER RULING (reviewer open question): GET /artifacts/:id current-version comment list EXCLUDES consumed comments by default; add include_consumed=true query param (archived-version views in TASK-EDQPG will use it). Adjust the round-trip test accordingly.

Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon and -p orgasmic-cli (redirect to files); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; fmt on touched files. New unit tests for the validator corpus, leading-* escaping round-trip, and atomicity (no partial state after simulated failure where testable).

** Description
Implement the schema and daemon changes that the 2026-05-23 UI grilling session locked in. Five model additions, one model realign, one new tx type, one new projection, one new slot. All landed in a single sprint task so the new UI sessions (3 onwards) can build against the new model without serialization tricks.

The five model additions:
1. *Task lifecycle realign* (dec_MKC0A). Collapse per-kind state machines to a single 6-stage lifecycle on the task heading: BACKLOG / EXPLORE / PLAN / IMPLEMENT / REVIEW / SHIP / DONE plus BLOCKED / CANCELLED. Update =shipped/schema/state-machine.org=, =crates/orgasmic-core/src/schema.rs::TaskState=, =crates/orgasmic-core/src/org.rs::TODO_KEYWORDS=. Migrate the existing 45 sprint headings to the new keywords (most map directly: =DONE=→=DONE=; =READY=→=BACKLOG= or =IMPLEMENT= depending on task; =analyzing/implementing/testing/fixing/merging=→folded into =IMPLEMENT= stage).
2. *Run sub-state* (dec_RECYG). Per-kind sub-states (=analyzing=, =implementing=, =testing=, =fixing=, =merging=, =planning=, =drafted=, =findings_recorded=, =reviewing=, =approved=, =requested_changes=) move off the task heading and onto the run record as a string field with three namespaces: =agent.<verb>=, =human.<verb>=, =ci.<verb>=. Add a =RunState= field on =RunSummary= and serialize through =DriverEvent= lifecycle.
3. *Subtasks* (dec_JW11K). Add =:PARENT_TASK:= property to =TaskHeading=. ID format =TASK-NNN.M=. Daemon's materialized index rolls up =subtasks: BTreeMap<TaskId, Vec<TaskId>>= from back-edges; index rejects orphan subtasks at boot/refresh. Subtask creation via =POST /tasks/:id/subtasks=. UI never directly mutates the org file.
4. *Comments + activity projection* (dec_A4V2N). New tx type =comment= per =shipped/schema/tx.org=: properties TX_ID, TIME, TYPE=comment, ACTOR, PROJECT, TASK, RUN_ID (optional), ARTIFACTS (optional), IN_REPLY_TO (optional), BODY (escaped markdown). New endpoint =POST /tasks/:id/comments= (writer routes through =POST /tx= internally). New projection in =index.rs=: =activity_index: BTreeMap<TaskId, Vec<TxEntry>>=; rebuilt on boot, incrementally updated on each =comment= or =manager.action= tx append. New endpoint =GET /tasks/:id/activity= returns chronologically-merged comments + state-transition tx + run lifecycle events from the JSONL session.
5. *Ownership lock model* (dec_CX17K, dec_JW9TJ). Add =:STAGE_AGENT_BACKLOG:= through =:STAGE_AGENT_DONE:= properties to =shipped/project-scaffold/project.org= and parse them in =ProjectFile= view. On a stage transition (whether DnD-via-tx or supervisor-driven), the daemon consults the stage-agent map and auto-spawns a run if a template is configured (empty = human-only). Supervisor reports =owner= on the run record: =human= when no active run, =agent.<kind>= when active. Add =POST /runs/:id/release= endpoint that cancels the active run and returns ownership to =human= (used by the UI's "Release agent" affordance).
6. *Activity slot for agent prompt compiler* (dec_A4V2N). Register =task.activity= slot namespace in =shipped/schema/slots.org=; extend =crates/orgasmic-core/src/slots.rs::is_dynamic_skill_slot= to recognize it; loader fills from the same =activity_index= projection. Existing agent templates can opt in with ={{task.activity}}=; not required for v0.0.1 dogfood.

** Notes
This is a substantial single-task refactor. It is filed as one task rather than a Round of N because the schema/projection/endpoint changes are mutually-dependent: you cannot land =comment= tx type without the writer accepting it; cannot land the activity index without the comment tx type; cannot land subtasks without the index roll-up. Splitting would force ordering serialization without the benefit of parallel execution.

Verification command after each landing:
=cargo test --workspace && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check && git diff --check=.

- *Session 3*: Tasks page (list + kanban + DnD + ClickUp-style modal + subtasks + activity rail) — depends on subtasks model, comment tx, activity projection.
- *Session 4*: Manager popover (peek/workbench/focus + xterm.js bridge) + bell + LED + gear + theme + TanStack Router migration — depends on the new tx topology only loosely.
- *Session 5*: Decisions + Architecture + Glossary + ADR + Snapshots + Activity + cross-domain Graph — depends on existing graph endpoints; no new model needs.

* DONE TASK-YGB1R Replace workflow tier adjectives with derivable escalating triggers :workflow:runtime:process:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-YGB1R
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Problem: `shipped/workflows/default.org` classifies work with bare adjectives — "trivial", "ordinary", "risky". Those are subjective enough that an agent already in execution momentum resolves them in whichever direction keeps it moving. On TASK-KWSTJ a P0 daemon-recovery change touching ~900 lines across orgasmic-core, orgasmic-daemon, orgasmic-cli and the UI read as manager-direct without the classification ever being contested.

Replace the adjectives with triggers a reader cannot argue with, while keeping the three-tier shape.

Work:
1. Define concrete escalating triggers, at minimum: task priority (P0/P1 is never trivial); blast-radius paths (daemon recovery, supervisor, boot, auth, dispatch lease, writer durability); breadth (crate count / file count / net line count over a stated threshold); and presence of a `depends_on` chain or an umbrella parent.
2. Any trigger firing means the work is at least `ordinary`; two or more, or a safety/auth path, means `risky`.
3. Keep the tiers as guidance for *how much process*, not a hard gate — the point is to remove the judgement call about which tier applies, not to remove judgement about how to work.
4. Where a trigger is derivable from the task heading itself (priority, tags, depends_on), surface it: an agent reading `orgasmic task get` should see the floor tier without recomputing it.
5. Reconcile with the manager-implementer clause in `shipped/entry/router.org` so router and workflow do not drift.

Non-goal: an exhaustive rubric. Four or five unambiguous triggers beat twenty debatable ones, and long prose dilutes the instruction it is meant to strengthen.

Acceptance:
- two agents reading the same task heading reach the same floor tier
- the P0/multi-crate/recovery-path shape that produced this task classifies as at least `ordinary` with no interpretation
- the fast path for genuinely small work stays fast

** Description

Every codex acp-stdio dispatch leaves last.txt as the bare marker "codex
turn completed" while the worker's full markdown report sits unread in the
session JSONL (e.g. dispatch-TASK-SMFHY-implementer-20260612T171049.jsonl:
304 assistant text_chunks containing the complete Changed/Gates report;
last.txt = 21 bytes).

Verified root cause, two layers:
1. ADAPTER: =emit_turn_completion= (orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/
   codex.rs:646-665) maps =turn/completed= to
   =RunComplete { summary: Some("codex turn <status>") }= — a status
   marker fabricated from the status field, never the turn's output.
   ="thread closed"= (codex.rs:596-602) has the same defect.
2. DAEMON: =dispatch_last_summary_from_session= (orgasmic-daemon/src/
   api.rs:4032-4101) prefers ANY non-empty run_complete summary over the
   assembled assistant text — the placeholder always shadows the real
   report.

Contrast: subprocess-stream-json distills accumulated assistant text at
exit (=SubprocessExitSummary::distill=), which is why cursor dispatches
produce real last.txt summaries; rmux distills the terminal tail.

Preferred fix shape (minimal): the codex adapter emits =summary: None=
for generic status markers (completed / thread closed) so the daemon's
existing =or(assistant_summary)= fallback assembles the report; carry a
real summary only when the protocol provides actual content. Keep
RunFail's error path as is. Add an adapter unit test (turn/completed with
no content → None) and a daemon-side test that a session with assistant
chunks + marker-only run_complete yields the assistant report in
last.txt.
** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A codex acp dispatch whose session carries assistant text yields a
  last.txt containing the worker's final report, not a status marker.
- [ ] turn/completed and thread/closed with no real content emit
  =RunComplete { summary: None }=; statuses with genuine protocol content
  may carry it. RunFail error mapping unchanged.
- [ ] Adapter unit test: turn/completed (no content) maps to summary None.
- [ ] Daemon test: session with assistant chunks + marker-only
  run_complete writes the assembled assistant report to last.txt.
- [ ] Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers -p orgasmic-daemon;
  cargo fmt --check.
** Evidence
Fixed manager-direct [2026-06-13] (operator-directed: dev-process fix while the ZD72S+BRXGG dispatch ran). Both root-cause layers addressed exactly as scoped:
1. ADAPTER: emit_turn_completion non-failed arm and thread/closed now emit RunComplete { summary: None } — no fabricated markers; RunFail mapping untouched (codex.rs).
2. DAEMON: dispatch_last_summary_from_session demotes legacy pre-fix markers (is_generic_completion_marker: "codex turn <status>" single-token, "thread closed") to last-resort fallback so old sessions also resolve to the assembled assistant report (api.rs).
Tests: adapters::codex turn_completed_without_content_emits_summary_none, thread_closed_emits_summary_none, turn_failed_still_maps_to_run_fail; api::tests dispatch_last_summary_prefers_assistant_report_over_generic_completion_marker, dispatch_last_summary_uses_marker_when_nothing_else_exists, generic_completion_marker_detection_is_narrow — all green.
Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers -p orgasmic-daemon — failure set identical to the pre-change baseline (hermes roundtrip + post_projects + PID trio + nested_worktree, all owned by in-flight TASK-ZD72S; live_rmux render test is a load-flake, passes isolated). fmt clean; drivers clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; daemon clippy dead-code debt verified IDENTICAL on clean main (ZD72S territory).
LIVE NOTE: production daemon still runs the old binary; the fix reaches real last.txt files at the next rebuild+restart (scheduled with the ZD72S integration — that run's own report still needs the session-jsonl workaround, the last time).

* DONE TASK-YN5FJ Review cannot precede merge: the overlap guard plus an unverified --merge-sha structurally push unreviewed code to main :cli:manager:process:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-YN5FJ
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-cli/**,crates/orgasmic-daemon/**
:END:

** Description
Today the tool structurally PRESSURES a manager to merge unreviewed code to
main, and then cannot tell whether they did. Both halves are verified in source
[2026-08-03], reproduced live on the TASK-XCJYC close.

*The forcing chain, in three facts:*

1. =build_dispatch_plan= (=manager.rs:2320=) refuses any dispatch while an open
   dispatch overlaps the same task. Its own comment names the case:
   "dispatching the reviewer before closing the implementer". So a reviewer
   cannot start until the implementer generation is CLOSED.
2. =dispatch-close --status done= on an implementer REQUIRES =--merge-sha=
   (=manager.rs:801-806=), so closing asserts a merge already happened.
3. Therefore: review requires close, close requires a merge -> the merge
   precedes the review. Structurally, not by anyone's choice.

*And the assertion is unverified.* =merge_sha= is
=args.merge_sha.map(sanitize_tx_value).filter(|s| !s.is_empty())=
(=manager.rs:796-800=), where =sanitize_tx_value= (=:5279=) only strips newlines
and trims. Nothing calls git. Nothing checks the sha exists, is a merge commit,
contains the worker's commit, or is on any particular branch. It is recorded as
tx property =MERGE_SHA= and never read back as evidence.

So orgasmic does not require merging to MAIN — it requires ASSERTING a merge.
That is the worst of both worlds: pressure to merge early, and no ability to
tell whether the merge happened, where it landed, or whether anyone reviewed it.

** What to change, in priority order

*1. Let a reviewer dispatch against a reported-but-open implementer generation.*
This is the minimal fix and it removes the forcing entirely. The overlap guard
exists to stop two workers colliding on one branch and worktree; a reviewer
reading a branch is not that collision. Permit a DIFFERENT =--kind= on a task
whose open dispatch is already =reported=. With this alone, review can precede
the close, so it can precede the merge.

*2. Make =--merge-sha= evidence instead of an assertion.* Verify it resolves
(=git rev-parse --verify=), that it is a merge commit, and that it contains the
recorded =--worker-commit=. Then the useful rule becomes expressible: REFUSE a
close whose merge lands on the repo's default branch unless a reviewer verdict
tx exists for that generation. That is what turns "no unreviewed code on main"
from a convention into something the tool can enforce.

*3. Consider a close status that does not claim a merge* (=--status handed-off=
or similar), so an implementer generation can close cleanly while its branch
waits for review. Lower priority if 1 lands, since 1 removes the need.

** The operator's hypothesis: is =.orgasmic/= on main the cause?
NO for this defect — the two guards above are, and they are independent of
where state lives. But the instinct points at a real second-order problem worth
recording:

The daemon writes =.orgasmic/= live at the REPO ROOT CHECKOUT, so state and code
are pinned to the same branch. A protected-main workflow (integrate on a branch,
fast-forward main only on APPROVE) is therefore awkward: every dispatch tx and
task transition would have to land on the integration branch too, and main would
lag its own state. Option 4 below is a change today with ZERO code
(=--merge-sha= is unverified, so merging to an integration branch already
satisfies the close) — but this coupling is what makes it uncomfortable rather
than obvious.

There is also a KNOWN DEFECT in the same family, already recorded: a dispatched
reviewer's worktree carries a FROZEN SNAPSHOT of =.orgasmic/= and cannot see the
live daemon's uncommitted writes, which has produced false negatives on
state-touching review. Any redesign of where state lives should fix that too,
rather than treating it separately.

*4. Integration branch* — workers merge to =integration=, review happens there,
main is fast-forwarded only on APPROVE. Works today without code changes.
Evaluate against 1+2 rather than instead of them: 1+2 fix the mechanism, 4 is a
policy that still depends on a manager following it.

** Acceptance
- A reviewer can be dispatched for a task whose implementer has reported but
  whose generation is not yet closed.
- A close recording a merge sha that does not resolve, is not a merge commit, or
  does not contain the worker commit, is refused by name.
- A close whose merge lands on the default branch without a reviewer verdict for
  that generation is refused by name — and the refusal states the remedy.
- The unverified-string behaviour is covered by a regression test, since it is
  what made the current state invisible.
** Manager review and verdict
MANAGER REVIEW [2026-08-03], performed personally at the operator's request
rather than by a dispatched reviewer. Diff =2bdf627..task-yn5fj-impl=, merged as
=6ead5c5=. Verdict: *APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS*.

=== What I verified rather than accepted
- *The overlap relaxation is correctly narrow.* It refuses when
  =!open.reported || open.kind == args.kind=, so an UNREPORTED generation and a
  SAME-KIND second dispatch both still collide. Only reported + different kind
  is admitted. That is exactly the handoff and nothing wider.
- *The architector guard was left byte-identical*, as the brief required for the
  concurrent TASK-RQ270.1 merge. The only architector mention added is including
  =architector.done= in the merge-verification =matches!=, and verification runs
  only when a sha is present — so stage A deleting that guard cannot strand the
  path. The merge was in fact clean.
- *Merge evidence is real*: resolves, >= 2 parents, contains the resolved
  =--worker-commit=. Default-branch detection reads the registered board
  =BRANCH=, tries local then =origin/<branch>=, and uses
  =git merge-base --is-ancestor=.
- Gates re-run by me on the merge: fmt clean, clippy =--workspace
  --all-targets -D warnings= clean, =cli --test dispatch= 57/0, =cli_parity= 3/0.

=== FINDING P1 — CONFIRMED: the refusal's stated remedy does not resolve the refusal
The default-branch gate requires a =reviewer.done= whose =VERDICT= property is
non-empty. But =VERDICT= has no flag. It is settable ONLY through the generic
=--property VERDICT=...=, where it previously served one narrow purpose —
=reviewer_done_stage= reads it to decide whether the task goes to done or back
to in_progress — and it is OPTIONAL there (=.unwrap_or(false)=).

The refusal prints: "Dispatch and close a reviewer for that reported generation,
or re-run with =--no-review-required --reason <why>=". A manager who follows the
first branch literally will dispatch a reviewer, close it, retry, and be refused
AGAIN with the same message, because their close carried no =VERDICT=.

*This is confirmed against production, not reasoned.* The =reviewer.done= this
manager wrote for TASK-XCJYC one hour before the review —
=tx-20260803-orgasmic-4401= — carries =REASON=, =REVIEWED_DIFF=, =CLOSED_TX=,
=MODEL=, =EFFORT= and lifecycle properties, and NO =VERDICT=. It is a complete,
ordinary, correctly-formed reviewer close that the new gate would reject. Every
historical reviewer close on this project is in the same shape.

*Fix direction*: promote the verdict to a first-class =--verdict= flag on
reviewer closes rather than leaving it an undocumented incantation, and name it
in the refusal text. A typed flag also addresses the implementer's own residual
risk that "any non-empty VERDICT, including a negative one, satisfies the rule".
Filed as TASK-YN5FJ.1.

=== Second-order, deliberately NOT blocking
Historical reviewer dispatches carry no =REVIEWS_TX=, so a pre-existing
generation can never satisfy the gate. That is acceptable: the feature is new,
=--no-review-required --reason= records the exception honestly, and back-filling
a ledger would be worse than the gap.

=== Not live yet
These paths run from the INSTALLED runtime (=05e1813=). The gate takes effect
only after a deliberate runtime reinstall, which is why merging with a known
P1 in the refusal text is safe: nothing can hit it before that reinstall, and
TASK-YN5FJ.1 should land first.

* DONE TASK-YN5FJ.1 fix-subtask: the review gate's refusal names a remedy that does not satisfy it — promote VERDICT to a real flag :cli:manager:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-YN5FJ.1
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-cli/**
:END:

** Description
From the TASK-YN5FJ manager review, section "Manager review and verdict".
CONFIRMED against production, not reasoned.

The default-branch gate requires a =reviewer.done= carrying a non-empty
=VERDICT=. =VERDICT= has NO FLAG — it is settable only through the generic
=--property VERDICT=...=, and it was previously optional, read by
=reviewer_done_stage= only to choose the task's next stage (=.unwrap_or(false)=).

So the refusal text — "Dispatch and close a reviewer for that reported
generation, or re-run with --no-review-required --reason <why>" — names a first
branch that DOES NOT WORK. Follow it exactly and you are refused again with the
same message.

*Production evidence.* =tx-20260803-orgasmic-4401=, the =reviewer.done= this
manager wrote for TASK-XCJYC, carries =REASON=, =REVIEWED_DIFF=, =CLOSED_TX=,
=MODEL=, =EFFORT= and lifecycle properties and NO =VERDICT=. It is an ordinary,
correctly-formed reviewer close that the new gate rejects. Every historical
reviewer close is the same shape.

** Fix
1. Add a first-class =--verdict= flag to =dispatch-close= for reviewer closes,
   so the value the gate depends on is a documented part of the surface rather
   than an incantation through =--property=. Keep accepting the existing
   =--property VERDICT= spelling so nothing already written breaks.
2. Consider a typed value set (approve / approve-with-follow-ups / reject)
   rather than free text. This also answers the implementer's own declared
   residual risk that any non-empty verdict — including a negative one —
   currently satisfies "a verdict exists". Decide deliberately whether a REJECT
   should unlock a default-branch merge; there is a real argument either way
   (a REJECT the manager then resolved is exactly what happened on TASK-XCJYC),
   so state the reasoning rather than picking silently.
3. Name the verdict requirement IN the refusal text, so the remedy is
   self-contained.

** Ordering
Land this BEFORE any runtime reinstall. The gate is not live until the runtime
is rebuilt, so there is no live breakage today — but the first reinstall after
TASK-YN5FJ without this fix hands the operator a refusal they cannot clear
except by =--no-review-required=, which defeats the feature.

** Acceptance
- A reviewer close can record its verdict through a documented flag.
- Following the refusal's stated remedy actually clears the refusal — pin this
  with a test that walks the full loop: refuse, follow the remedy verbatim,
  succeed.
- Existing =--property VERDICT= closes still work.
** Evidence
Landed =bb2fb24= (merge) / =036b1d9= (worker commit) on main, base =739e3b8=.

Implementer: =implementer-claude-tmux= — driver tmux, harness claude, model claude-opus-5, effort high. Run =run-20260805T124037-ad04be2d00694da9929573ba9c7865c1=, started_tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4429=.

Manager rulings implemented as decided, with the reasoning carried in code comments rather than only in this record:
- RULING 1 — every verdict clears the gate, =reject= included. The gate asks whether an independent review happened, not whether it approved; blocking on a reject would force =--no-review-required=, stamping a bypass on a dispatch that WAS reviewed. A bad verdict already has its consequence in =reviewer_done_stage=.
- RULING 2 — =--verdict= takes a typed set (=approve= / =approve-with-follow-ups= / =reject=) that is a strict superset of the legacy free-text vocabulary; =clean= / =ship= / =has-issues= stay reachable through =--property VERDICT== unchanged.
- RULING 3 — passing both spellings is a hard error naming both, rather than last-wins.
