** Description
Reviewer REJECT on TASK-YN5FJ.1 (merged =bb2fb24=), from =reviewer-codex-tmux=
(codex / gpt-5.6-sol / high), tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4438=. BLOCK SHIP, one
finding, both halves verified by the manager against the code rather than taken
on the reviewer word.

This is the SAME defect class the parent task existed to fix, one level down: a
remedy that cannot be followed as printed.

*Half one — the template is not executable.* =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:955=
prints the remedy as =`manager dispatch-close --task <task> --started-tx
<reviewer-tx> --status done --verdict <...>`=. There is no =orgasmic= in it.
Pasting that into a shell does not invoke this CLI.

*Half two — the test cannot catch that, and says otherwise.* =crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs:1721=
carries the comment "Follow the printed remedy VERBATIM" and then builds a
separate argv array at =:1758=, with =run_orgasmic= supplying the binary
independently (=:425-432=, =:484-494=). So the loop test passes while the printed
message is uncopyable, and nothing detects future drift between the message and
the hand-built command. A comment claiming verbatim adherence over code that does
not is worse than no claim.

The parent acceptance criterion — "following the refusal stated remedy actually
clears the refusal" — is therefore NOT met, which is why this is a fix round and
not a polish note.

** Fix
1. Print a complete executable template beginning with =orgasmic manager
   dispatch-close=, with the task id(s) already substituted (the refusal knows
   them). =<reviewer-tx>= must stay a placeholder — the reviewer has not been
   dispatched yet at refusal time — so document precisely which tokens are
   placeholders and keep that set as small as the information allows.
2. Rewrite the acceptance test to EXTRACT the backticked command from the actual
   refusal string, substitute only the documented placeholders, tokenize, and
   execute the derived argv. Delete the hand-built close. Keep the existing
   semantic assertions so the extracted remedy must both persist =VERDICT= and
   clear the original refusal.
3. Do not weaken the claim to match the code — the test should earn the word
   verbatim, not drop it.

** Ordering
Same ordering constraint the parent carried: land BEFORE any runtime reinstall.

** Acceptance
- The refusal prints a command a human can paste, executable name included.
- The acceptance test derives the command it runs FROM the refusal text; a
  deliberate edit to the message that breaks the command fails the test.
- Existing coverage stays green, including the =--property VERDICT== compat
  tests and both existing injection proofs, which must still replay.
** Evidence
Landed =14b9660= (merge) / =f6c8bf7= (worker HEAD, two commits) on main, base =e527e7e=.

Implementer: =implementer-claude-tmux= — driver tmux, harness claude, model claude-opus-5, effort high. Run =run-20260805T132340-bd6880abc7ca43b2bebe90e2c7fa4492=, started_tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4443=.

THE REFUSAL NOW PRINTS A PASTEABLE COMMAND. It builds the remedy from what it holds — one =--task <id>= per task in the dispatch, executable included — and then names its own placeholder set in prose: =<reviewer-tx>= (which does not exist at refusal time) and the verdict choice. Everything else is a real value.

THE TEST NOW EARNS THE WORD "VERBATIM". =backticked_command= extracts the command from the refusal string that run produced; =derive_remedy_argv= substitutes exactly the two documented placeholders and ASSERTS every remaining token is free of =<= / =>=, so a message that leaves a placeholder for something it knew fails the MESSAGE rather than being patched up by the test; =run_derived_argv= execs =argv[0]= BY NAME through the test PATH, with the binary symlinked in under its own name. The helper no longer supplies the executable, which is precisely what hid the defect.

Integration gates, re-run by the manager on the MERGED tree:
- =scripts/run-tests.sh -p orgasmic-cli= — GREEN, 0 failures, 1 ignored, "environ: complete — no tool requirement was waived".
- =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= — exit 0.
- =cargo fmt --all --check= — exit 0.
- =orgasmic verify TASK-YN5FJ.1= — PASS. =orgasmic verify TASK-YN5FJ.1-remedy= — PASS.

THE RE-CUT ARTIFACT WAS CHECKED BEYOND ITS GREEN REPLAY, because a green replay cannot vouch for a re-cut. =verify/TASK-YN5FJ.1/injection.patch= had to be re-cut (it was a whole-file revert of the region this task edits). The manager verified independently: =git apply --check= clean against HEAD; applying it yields a =manager.rs= BYTE-IDENTICAL to =bb2fb24^1= (the true pre-fix state); and the red log carries exactly ONE panic — =dispatch.rs:1807=, the pinned label "refusal must name the verdict requirement and the --verdict remedy" — whose body quotes the pinned pre-fix text verbatim, with =0 passed; 1 failed=. So the pinned message is the FIRST failing assertion, not a downstream one. =expect-red= needed no edit. The =-remedy= patch still applied unchanged and was verified rather than assumed.

THREE PROBES WERE RUN, NOT DESCRIBED (reverted after each): removing =orgasmic = from the printed remedy goes red on "printed remedy must begin with the executable an operator would type"; restoring =--task <task>= as a placeholder goes red on "undocumented placeholder"; and the quoted production message was captured from a real CLI run rather than read off the format string.

ONE BEHAVIOURAL DELTA, DECLARED: the derived close no longer passes =--reviewed-diff=, because the message does not print it and the test may not add tokens. =reviewer_verdict_exists= reads =CLOSED_TX= and =VERDICT= only, so the gate is unaffected, and =--reviewed-diff= stays covered by the other reviewer-close tests.

** Description
Two reviewer findings from TASK-YVZ9V bundled as one fix-implementer round per one-round-of-fixes discipline. Both share a single root cause: the new AutoSpawn candidate-discovery path (=auto_spawn_worker_dirs= + =read_dir= loop in =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:2732-2768=) diverges from the existing =load_stage_worker= loader semantics.

F-1 HIGH (correctness): candidate discovery walks only =workers/= directories; =load_stage_worker= falls back to legacy =agent-templates/{id}.org=. A project whose stage-mapped worker only exists as a legacy agent template can have its unpinned task silently routed to some other eligible worker, violating the stage-mapped-worker preference.

F-2 MEDIUM (correctness): candidate slice is built from =std::fs::read_dir= (unstable iteration order on macOS/Linux). =auto_select_worker= is deterministic only relative to its input slice, so two equally-eligible fully-specified workers can produce different winners across platforms.

Report at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-059-review-report.md=.

- [ ] F-2: candidate slice has stable ordering before =auto_select_worker= is called. Add a daemon-level integration test with two equally-eligible fully-specified workers (same kind, same capability coverage) that asserts the same winner across repeated runs.

** Description
The =orgasmic-core= architecture parser currently recognizes top-level =* arch_NNN ...= headings. Extend it to also accept second-level =** arch_NNN.M ...= children under each parent, with the typed-edge property set (=:SOURCE_PATHS:=, =:READS:=, =:WRITES:=, =:EXPOSES_REST:=, =:EXPOSES_WS:=, =:SUBSCRIBES_TO:=, =:SPAWNS:=, =:CALLS:=, =:DEPENDS_ON:=). Architecture nodes gain a parent/child relation derivable from the ID prefix.

Grilling context: dec_X6Q0S refinement [2026-05-27]. CLAUDE.md pitfall reminder: the existing parser is opinionated about =TODO_KEYWORDS=; the architecture-prefix recognition is similarly opinionated. Read =crates/orgasmic-core/src/schema.rs= and =crates/orgasmic-core/src/org.rs= before adjusting.

* DONE TASK-Z3093 LiveSessionGuard serializes but never reaps, so every failing live-session test leaks an rmux session :testing:rmux:leak:production:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-Z3093
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

`LiveSessionGuard` serializes live-session tests and reaps nothing. Every one of
its 9 copies is the same flock-only type whose `Drop` calls `fs2::FileExt::unlock`
and returns. Cleanup of the rmux session the test created is a *trailing
statement* in the test body, so a panic anywhere above it skips the reap and the
session, its pty and its harness process survive the test binary.

This is the open source of the TASK-8W30B leak that a production-path fix cannot
close. TASK-6FNAY hardened `RmuxControl::release` (merged 83ea420) and the leak
still reproduced afterwards: two orphan sessions found 2026-07-28 at 13:20,
ages 3h18m and 2h46m, both running
`orgasmic_daemon-e5f5d4f31537ab72.fixture.sh artifact-ready`, both 404 to the
daemon and absent from every ledger, i.e. from test fixtures rather than from a
dispatch (tx-20260728-orgasmic-3117). Earlier the same day three more were found
at 09:57 (tx-20260728-orgasmic-3103, refiled onto 8W30B by
tx-20260728-orgasmic-3110).

** Measured inventory

- 9 definitions of `struct LiveSessionGuard(std::fs::File)`, byte-identical in
  behaviour, across 3 crates:
  - `crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:15772`
  - `crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs:5478`
  - `crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs:2329`
  - `crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs:2481`
  - `crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/rmux_release_reaps_session.rs:23`
  - `crates/orgasmic-cli/src/test_support.rs:37`
  - `crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs:38`
  - `crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/list_output.rs:33`
  - `crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/bootstrap_smoke.rs:46`
- 85 `live_session_guard()` call sites. Heaviest: `cli/tests/dispatch.rs` 30,
  `daemon/src/api.rs` 19, `drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs` 12,
  `drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs` 12.
- All 12 artifactor tests in `api.rs` that call `seed_test_artifactor_harness` /
  `seed_busy_artifactor_harness` spawn a real rmux session. 11 end with a
  trailing `supervisor.release(..)` or `release_with_finalization(..)`; one,
  `launch_artifact_generation_persistence_failure_releases_run`
  (api.rs:27530), has no release in the test body at all and relies on the
  production path releasing for it — confirm that it actually does.
- The fixture never exits on its own. `artifact-ready` loops
  `echo '> ready'; read -r line || exit 0`, and inside an rmux pane stdin never
  closes, so an unreaped session runs until something kills it
  (`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/test_fixtures.rs:20`).

** Why this compounds

TASK-STWVB records four daemon tests that fail on every full-suite run and pass
alone, and the TASK-C0XMR merge note (`0860861`) says that family gained two more
members under load. A load-induced failure is a panic, and a panic is exactly the
path that skips the trailing release — so **the flake and the leak are the same
event**. Every dispatched worker runs the full suites, so leak rate scales with
dispatch volume, which is what the two-per-day observation shows.

A leaked session also outlives its worktree: pid 42520 still named
`.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/task-C0XMR/worktree`, a directory `dispatch-close` had
already removed.

** Fix

One shared guard that owns cleanup, not nine that own a file lock.

- Give the guard a registration surface (`guard.owns(run_id)` /
  `guard.owns_session(name, endpoint)`) and reap on `Drop`, unconditionally,
  before releasing the flock. Drop runs on the panic path, which is the whole
  point.
- The reap must not itself depend on a live SDK transport — reuse the CLI
  fallback shape TASK-6FNAY established (`rmux_session_reap_args(endpoint,
  name)`, rmux.rs:1505), addressed at the endpoint the handle owned. A `Drop`
  cannot await, so the reap has to be a blocking call or a spawned-and-joined
  helper; pick one and say why.
- De-duplicate: one definition in a shared test-support location that all three
  crates use. Nine copies is how a fix to one of them silently misses the other
  eight.
- Keep the flock behaviour exactly as it is. Serialization is load-bearing and
  independent of the leak.

** Acceptance

- A live-session test that panics mid-body leaves no session behind — proven by
  a test that deliberately panics inside the guard's scope and then asserts the
  session is gone.
- `rmux ls` is empty after a full `cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon` and after
  `cargo test -p orgasmic-cli` on a machine that started with no sessions.
- One `LiveSessionGuard` definition remains in the tree.
- `launch_artifact_generation_persistence_failure_releases_run` either releases
  through the production path (demonstrated) or gains a guard registration.

** Non-goals

- Do not change `RmuxControl::release`; TASK-6FNAY owns the production path and
  is in review.
- Do not fix the TASK-STWVB flakes themselves. This task makes their cost
  bounded, not zero.
- Do not run `legacy_drivers_and_explicit_pairs_emit_equivalent_start_events`
  (TASK-099T6) — it bills real money. Skip it explicitly on the drivers suite.

* DONE TASK-Z8WEJ Select the claude credential mode instead of hardcoding --bare :drivers:dispatch:bug:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-Z8WEJ
:PRIORITY: P0
:BLOCKED_BY: TASK-KKBTP
:END:

Problem: `crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/claude.rs:136` hardcodes `--bare` in the claude stdio argv. Per the CLI's own help, `--bare` means "Anthropic auth is strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper via --settings (OAuth and keychain are never read)". An operator authenticated through a claude.ai subscription therefore cannot dispatch a claude worker at all: the credential exists, `claude auth status` reports `loggedIn: true, authMethod: claude.ai, subscriptionType: max`, and the dispatch still dies 1.2 s after acquire with "Not logged in - Please run /login" (observed TASK-KWSTJ reviewer dispatch, run-20260725T073841).

`--bare` is wanted and should stay available: it skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync, auto-memory, background prefetches and CLAUDE.md auto-discovery, which is the right shape for a worker. The defect is that it is unconditional, and it silently carries a credential policy that a subscription operator cannot satisfy.

Measured channel matrix, same binary and prompt, obviously-fake credential values (2026-07-25, claude 2.1.220):

Under `--bare`:
- no credential -> "Not logged in - Please run /login"
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<fake>` -> "Invalid API key - Fix external API key" (channel LIVE)
- `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=<fake>` -> "Not logged in" (channel DEAD; the token is ignored)
- `apiKeyHelper` via `--settings` -> "Invalid API key" (channel LIVE)

Without `--bare`:
- keychain OAuth -> authenticates and completes
- `--strict-mcp-config` + empty `--mcp-config` + minimal `--settings` -> authenticates, `mcp_servers: []`, 30 tools, 2.0 s round trip

Critical negative result: `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1` on its own, with no `--bare` flag, also fails with "Not logged in". The lightweight behaviour and the credential policy are the same switch, so there is no way to keep bare-mode lightness while reading the keychain. Any design that assumes they can be separated is wrong.

Both live `--bare` channels want an API key, not an OAuth credential, and a subscription's keychain credential is not an API key. So "`--bare` plus the user's keychain auth" is not achievable, by the flag's contract rather than by oversight.

Work:
1. Make the claude adapter select a credential mode instead of hardcoding one. At minimum: bare+API key (preferred, lightest) when an API key or apiKeyHelper is configured; non-bare with narrow isolation when auth is OAuth/subscription.
2. Build the fallback tier explicitly rather than by dropping flags: `--strict-mcp-config` with an empty `--mcp-config`, a minimal `--settings`, and the existing `--no-session-persistence`. Verify it suppresses MCP, hooks, and CLAUDE.md discovery — do not assume the narrow flags cover everything `--bare` did, and record what is not covered.
3. Detect, do not guess. `claude auth status` is non-interactive and returns structured JSON with `authMethod`; use it to choose the tier. Note it is necessary but not sufficient — see 5.
4. Let the manager override the tier per dispatch, and record which tier was used in the run's RunMeta so a failure is diagnosable from the session JSONL alone.
5. Feeds TASK-TJKFC: a generic auth probe is not enough. `claude auth status` reports `loggedIn: true` while the `--bare` invocation fails. The preflight must exercise the argv the worker will actually run.
6. Consider whether the same credential-mode question exists for codex, cursor-agent, and hermes, or whether this is claude-specific. Do not generalise without checking.

Acceptance:
- a subscription-authenticated operator can dispatch a claude worker with no API key
- an API-key operator still gets the light `--bare` path
- the selected credential mode is visible in RunMeta
- a mode that cannot authenticate is rejected before a worktree, lease, or dispatch record is created
** Evidence
Implemented 2026-07-25 in commit 61b9b7f on `task-kwstj-bounded-run-inventory`.

`adapters/claude.rs` now resolves a `ClaudeCredentialMode` in `compose_request` rather than hardcoding flags in `stdio_spawn`:
- `BareApiKey` when `api_key_env` resolves or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is present — keeps the light `--bare` path, which is the one credential channel `--bare` accepts.
- `NativeLogin` otherwise — drops `--bare` so the harness reads its own keychain/OAuth login, and rebuilds isolation from `--strict-mcp-config` plus a minimal `--settings`.

`stdio_spawn` now returns the credential-agnostic wire flags only; mode flags and the pinned session id are added where the run context is available.

Item 2's instruction to verify rather than assume the narrow flags cover everything `--bare` did produced one negative result worth recording. Measured against claude 2.1.220:
- MCP is fully suppressed: `--strict-mcp-config` alone yields `mcp_servers: []`, against nine servers loaded without it on the measurement machine.
- Hooks are NOT suppressible. `--settings '{}'` and `--settings '{"hooks":{}}'` both still executed SessionStart hooks; `--include-hook-events` governs reporting, not execution; `--bare` is the only flag that skips them.

So native-login workers execute whatever hooks the operator has configured. This is accepted deliberately — the alternative is that subscription-authenticated operators cannot dispatch claude at all — and is documented on the `NativeLogin` variant rather than left for a later reader to rediscover. It surfaced through a real test failure (`legacy_drivers_and_explicit_pairs_emit_equivalent_start_events` began comparing nondeterministic hook uuids), not through inspection.

Item 4 remains open: the resolved mode is logged at debug but is not yet recorded in RunMeta, so a failure is not yet diagnosable from the session JSONL alone. Item 6 also remains open — codex, cursor-agent and hermes have not been checked for the same credential-mode question.

Gates: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `git diff --check` clean. orgasmic-drivers 213 lib tests pass; `driver_modes` returns to its pre-change baseline of 20 passed / 4 failed, those four being pre-existing codex failures verified identical on the clean branch by stashing. orgasmic-core 132 pass.

Not verified end to end: the running daemon is the installed 0.0.14 build, so a live dispatch still uses the old adapter. Proving this against a real dispatch needs a daemon rebuild and restart, which is an operator decision.

* DONE TASK-ZBYH3 daemon.out.log is double-written and never rotates :daemon:ops:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-ZBYH3
:PRIORITY: P2
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/**,verify/**
:END:

** Description
=$ORGASMIC_HOME/logs/daemon.out.log= grows without bound AND every line is
written to it twice. Measured on the operator's live daemon 2026-08-06: 13 MB,
of which roughly half is exact duplication. Truncated manually to 0; it will
grow back.

The two problems are coupled — rotation is not well-defined while two
descriptors own the same file — so they are one task.

** Defect 1 — every tracing line lands in the file twice
=lib.rs:898= installs the subscriber as:

: init_tracing_to(&cfg.log_level, Some(&daemon_log), LogMirror::Stdout)

so tracing writes to the durable sink AND mirrors to stdout. Under the
LaunchAgent, *stdout IS that same file*: the generated plist sets
=StandardOutPath= to =logs/daemon.out.log= (=daemon_service.rs:370=, emitted at
=:846= and =:896=). So the daemon holds two descriptors on one inode and writes
identical content through both.

Measured (=lsof=, pid 41745): *fd 1u and fd 10w, same device, same inode
439742072*.

: last 400 lines -> 400 total, 201 unique
: last 2000 lines -> 995 adjacent identical pairs

Evidence file:
=<scratchpad>/daemon-log-dup-evidence.txt= (captured before truncation).

The mirror is correct and wanted for interactive =orgasmic serve= in a terminal.
It is pure waste under launchd.

** Defect 2 — no rotation
Nothing rotates the durable log. =logging.rs= opens it =create(true).append(true)=
(=:92=) and never rolls. 13 MB accumulated since roughly 2026-07-29.

** Two candidate rulings — pick one and say why
*** A. Separate the launchd capture file from the daemon's durable log
Point =StandardOutPath= at =logs/daemon.stdout.log= (and keep
=StandardErrorPath= as is), leaving =daemon.out.log= owned solely by the daemon's
own sink. Then the mirror is harmless, and the daemon can rotate its own file
without launchd holding a renamed inode. *Requires a plist change, so it only
takes effect after the LaunchAgent is rewritten* — note that
=orgasmic daemon start= rewrites the plist, and see the warning below.

*** B. Suppress the mirror when it resolves to the durable file
At startup, =stat= fd 1 and the durable path; if device+inode match, install
=LogMirror::None=. Self-healing, no plist change, works on already-installed
LaunchAgents. Leaves =StandardOutPath= pointing at the same file, so stray
=println!=/panic output still lands there and would survive a rotation on the
old inode.

B is the smaller, self-correcting fix and needs no reinstall to take effect.
A is the cleaner end state. *They compose* — B alone is sufficient to make
rotation coherent; A additionally keeps non-tracing stdout out of the durable
log. If you take both, say so.

** Rotation requirements
- Size-triggered roll on the durable sink: when the file exceeds a threshold,
  rename to =daemon.out.log.1= (rolling =.1= -> =.2= ... up to a small keep
  count) and reopen. Threshold and keep count should have sane defaults and be
  overridable from =config.yaml= (=DaemonConfig=, =config.rs=), consistent with
  how other daemon settings are read.
- *Never let a rotation failure kill the daemon or fail a request.* The whole
  point of this module (TASK-FZF2D, see its header comment) is that a dead log
  sink is survivable. A failed rename must degrade to "keep writing the current
  file", counted through the existing =record_drop= / =dropped_log_writes=
  mechanism.
- The sink is behind =Arc<Mutex<SinkState>>=; the roll happens under that lock.
  Keep the hot path cheap — do not =stat= on every line; track bytes written in
  the sink and check against the threshold.

** Acceptance
- A test proving a line logged once appears *once* in the durable file when the
  mirror resolves to that same file. This is the defect that measured 2x.
- A test proving the file rolls at the threshold, that the rolled file retains
  the earlier content, and that the keep count is honoured.
- A test proving a rotation failure does not propagate — the daemon keeps
  logging and the drop counter moves.
- =crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/logging_sink.rs= still passes; it asserts the sink
  survives a closed pipe and keeps writing the durable file.

** Notes and traps
- *Do NOT run =orgasmic daemon start= to test a plist change.* It rewrites the
  one real per-user LaunchAgent. Assert on the GENERATED plist STRING
  (=daemon_service.rs:846,:896= already render it) rather than installing it.
- The operator's log was truncated in place and that was safe *because both
  descriptors are =O_APPEND=*. If any future writer drops =append(true)=,
  in-place truncation starts leaving sparse gaps.
- 13 MB is not itself an outage. This is filed as a real defect because the
  double-write means half of every log read, grep and incident capture is
  redundant, and because unbounded growth on the operator's home is a slow leak.

* DONE TASK-ZBYH3.1 Rulings A and B conflict — the tracing stream is still double-written after a plist rewrite :daemon:ops:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-ZBYH3.1
:PRIORITY: P2
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/**,verify/**
:FIX_SUBTASK: true
:END:

** Description
Fix round for the BLOCK SHIP that rejected TASK-ZBYH3.

*The origin of this defect is the parent task's own wording, and that should be
said plainly.* TASK-ZBYH3's body told the implementer that rulings A and B
"compose". *They conflict.* The implementer took both, exactly as instructed, and
the result relocates the defect instead of fixing it. This is a manager framing
error, not an implementer miss.

** Why they conflict
- *B* suppresses the stdout mirror only when fd 1 and the durable path share
  *device+inode* (=logging.rs:162= =stdout_same_as_path=, =:181= =resolve_mirror=).
- *A* moves =StandardOutPath= to =logs/daemon.stdout.log= (=daemon_service.rs:372=)
  — deliberately a *different inode*.

B's discriminator is inode equality. A's whole purpose is to break inode
equality. So on any daemon started from a rewritten service definition,
=stdout_same_as_path= returns *false*, =LogMirror::Stdout= survives, and every
tracing line is written twice again:

| file | contents | rotated | pruned | read by |
| =daemon.out.log= | full tracing stream (durable sink) | yes, ~10MiB x 3 | — | operator |
| =daemon.stdout.log= | full tracing stream (mirror, via launchd) | *no* | *no* | *nothing* |

*Total write volume and total disk growth are UNCHANGED from the pre-fix defect.*
Only the distribution moved — into a file that no rotation, no pruning, no
=doctor= check and no error message mentions. ~300MB/year at the measured rate.

Worse on Windows: =same_file_as_path= is =#[cfg(not(unix))] -> false=
unconditionally, so B can never fire there at all. Same for the systemd unit
(=daemon_service.rs:946=) and the Windows wrapper (=:977=).

It looks correct on the operator's box *today* only because the installed plist
has not been rewritten yet and still points at =daemon.out.log=, so B fires.

** The ruling — gate the mirror on a terminal, not on inode identity
Replace the inode discriminator with =std::io::stdout().is_terminal()=. launchd's
stdout is never a tty, so this suppresses the mirror under any service manager
regardless of which file =StandardOutPath= names — it subsumes B *and* survives
A, and it works on Windows where the inode check cannot.

*The caveat that must not be missed:* =init_tracing= (=logging.rs:107=), used by
every non-=serve= CLI command (=main.rs:1347=), passes =LogMirror::Stdout= with
=durable_log = None=. Gating there would silence CLI tracing whenever output is
piped or redirected. *The tty gate must apply ONLY when a durable sink is
present* — exactly where =resolve_mirror= already short-circuits on
=durable_path == None= (=logging.rs:182-184=).

Keeping A (the separate =daemon.stdout.log=) is fine and preferable once the
mirror is correctly gated, because it also keeps stray =println!=/panic output
off the durable inode. If you keep it, the four =bail!= strings in
=daemon_lifecycle.rs= (=:780,:792,:807,:823=) should name it alongside
=daemon.out.log= and =daemon.err.log=. The plist-string test at
=daemon_service.rs:1169-1175= moves with whatever you choose.

** F3 — MEDIUM, and the second thing that must be fixed here
*A failed reopen after a SUCCESSFUL roll silences the durable log permanently,
invisibly.* On the =None= arm of the post-rename reopen (=logging.rs:403=) the
code sets =durable = None= and =bytes_written = 0=. Thereafter:

- =write_all_best_effort= (=logging.rs:283=) is
  =if let Some(file) = state.durable.as_mut()= — with =None= it writes nothing
  *and never calls =record_drop()==. So =dropped_log_writes= stops moving and the
  degradation is invisible *through the very mechanism this task designated for
  it*.
- =maybe_rotate= never runs its body again (=bytes_written= frozen at 0), so
  nothing ever retries the open.

A transient =EMFILE= or =ENOSPC= at the moment of a roll turns the durable log
off until the next restart, silently. Pre-fix that state was only reachable at
startup, where =open_durable_log= at least emits one stderr note; rotation makes
it reachable at runtime, indefinitely, and quietly.

Fix: =record_drop()= in the =durable == None= branch, and make the reopen
retryable — cheapest is to keep counting into =bytes_written= even when the write
is dropped, so =maybe_rotate= fires again and retries =open_durable_log=.

** F4 — silent loss of a retained generation
=logging.rs:372='s =Err(_) => {}= is not a no-op. If =.1 -> .2= fails, the loop
swallows it and the following =current -> .1= rename *overwrites =.1==, so the
generation that should have become =.2= is gone and the effective keep count
silently drops to 1. The final rename already gets both =record_drop()= and an
stderr note (=:379-385=); the intermediate ones need the same two lines.

** F5 — the rotation test would pass on a broken roll
=logging.rs:549= asserts disjunctively —
=rolled_blob.contains("second-content") || rolled_blob.contains("early-content")=
and =current.contains("third") || rolled1.contains("third")=. Swapping the roll
order so =current -> .1= runs BEFORE =.1 -> .2= destroys the newest rolled
generation on every roll, and both assertions still pass. The end state is fully
deterministic — =.1 = third=, =.2 = second=, current empty, =early= evicted at
=keep=2=. *Assert the exact three-file end state.*

** F6 — unvalidated config
=config.rs:39,44=: =log.keep= and =log.max_bytes= are unvalidated.
=logging.rs:366= performs =keep - 1= =rename(2)= calls on EVERY roll regardless of
how many rolled files exist, *while holding the sink mutex every tracing line
needs*. A typo'd =log.keep: 100000= turns each roll into 100k syscalls under the
logging lock. Clamp =keep= to a small maximum, surface out-of-range values
through the existing startup-warning path, and break the loop once a source path
is =NotFound=.

** F7 — the production suppression path is untested
Both the unit test (=logging.rs:481=) and the shipped verify artifact exercise
=LogMirror::Writer= -> =same_file_as_path=. The path that actually decides this in
production is =LogMirror::Stdout= -> =stdout_same_as_path= (=logging.rs:162=).
Whatever discriminator you land on, *test the production path*.

** Acceptance
- Under a launchd-shaped launch (stdout redirected to a file, ANY file), a line
  logged once appears *once* across =daemon.out.log= and =daemon.stdout.log=
  combined. Assert the combined count — that is the claim the previous round
  failed.
- Interactive =orgasmic serve= on a tty still prints to the terminal.
- Non-=serve= CLI commands still trace when piped or redirected (the
  =durable_log = None= caveat).
- A failed reopen after a roll moves =dropped_log_writes= and is retried.
- A failed intermediate rename is counted and noted.
- The rotation test pins the exact end state of all three files.
- =keep= is clamped; an out-of-range value is surfaced, not silently obeyed.

** The bar
The previous round's proof pinned =LogMirror::Writer=, which is not what runs in
production — that is why a fix that relocated the defect still passed its own
gate. *Pin the production discriminator this time*, and prove the combined
two-file count, not the single-file count.

* DONE TASK-ZG01H daemon supervisor CPU-spin under dispatch load (recurring) :daemon:supervisor:reliability:investigation:high:
:PROPERTIES:

:TEST_CMD:         cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon
:END:

** Description
The orgasmic daemon's supervisor (or one of its watcher / babysitter / spawn paths) enters a high-CPU hot loop after dispatches accumulate, eventually saturating multiple cores and making the dispatch endpoint unreachable within the CLI's 10s reqwest timeout. Observed twice during the [2026-05-28] session:

1. **After TASK-DMTDF reviewer dispatch + close (09:34Z)**: pid 89068 climbed to 96.5% CPU within ~1.5h elapsed. Dispatch endpoint timed out for new requests. =babysitter auto-spawn failed [error]=lease held: task=TASK-DMTDF kind=Babysitter run=bs-20260528T084053...= log line was emitted, suggesting a babysitter retry loop on a stale lease.

2. **After dual dispatch of TASK-DMTDF.2 reviewer + TASK-ENXWA architector (10:01Z)**: pid 34682 (freshly restarted) climbed to *509% CPU* (5 cores) within 2 minutes. The first dispatch (reviewer-codex-stdio) spawned a real codex worker; the second (architector → claude-acp) fell back to =simulated:true= in its capabilities (separate bug, see TASK-TGGAJ). The CPU spin coincided with the second dispatch.

Both wedges were resolved by =kill <pid>= + =nohup orgasmic serve &= restart. Workers spawned by the prior daemon continue functioning normally via OS pipes (codex doesn't depend on daemon-side health), so the issue is daemon-internal book-keeping not worker communication.

** Acceptance Criteria

** Description
Reviewer F-1 LOW from the TASK-ZG01H review (report at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-098-reviewer-report.md=):

After 10 lease-held babysitter auto-spawn failures, =should_attempt_babysitter_auto_spawn= returns =false= forever for that =task_id= in this daemon process. The only clearing path (=clear_babysitter_auto_spawn_backoff= on success) is unreachable after max retries because the gate now refuses to retry. Explicit release of the formerly held babysitter lease or a later real lease opening will not make the supervisor try again without a daemon restart.

This is a design caveat, not a live-blocking bug — operators can restart the daemon — but it means a task that hit transient lease-held churn early in its lifecycle (e.g., during a stuck-then-recovered babysitter) loses its babysitter coverage for the rest of the daemon's lifetime.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On explicit babysitter lease release (or task lifecycle close — pick whichever single event is the most natural "the lease is now actually free" signal), clear the per-task give-up state so subsequent auto-spawn attempts can succeed.
- [ ] Update the existing structured =warn!= when the give-up first fires to either name the explicit reset event (so operators know what to wait for) or, if the give-up is now self-recovering on lease release, soften the message to "babysitter auto-spawn paused" + a second log when it resumes.
- [ ] Add a regression test that: (a) triggers 10 lease-held failures + asserts give-up, (b) releases the held babysitter lease, (c) triggers a fresh auto-spawn attempt + asserts it succeeds (counter increments past the give-up threshold).
- [ ] cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon green; clippy + fmt + diff-check clean; MSRV 1.78.

** Notes
- *Smallest viable shape*: clear =babysitter_auto_spawn_backoff= entry on the same code path that releases the babysitter lease (= the inverse of the path that observes lease-held). This is one entry in =supervisor.rs= per the reviewer's suggestion.
- *Out of scope*: the transient close-time CPU spike observed during the TASK-ZG01H reviewer pass — that's a separate, unfiled hot path under investigation; do not fold into this subtask.

** Evidence
- *Implementer*: =implementer-codex-acp= via bundled supervisor cluster brief (=/tmp/orgasmic-codex/supervisor-cluster-brief.md=). Codex commit =59af464= ("supervisor.rs cluster: fix TOCTOU race + babysitter recovery + virtual-time test") on branch =supervisor-cluster-impl=. Merged no-ff as =5b11b4d=. Third attempt — first two were SIGKILLed by stall_detector misfire (TASK-HCFBT v2's brand-new mechanism vs codex-acp batch-emit pattern; mitigated by per-worker =:STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS: 7200= override in commit =f021a77=; TASK-HCFBT.3 filed for proper heartbeat fix). Successful run: ~10:35 wall after the override took effect.
- *Fix shape*: babysitter release path (release_lifecycle for Babysitter kind) now calls =clear_babysitter_auto_spawn_backoff(task_id)= so the per-task give-up state is reset on natural lease release. The existing structured =warn!= softened from "disabled" to "paused after repeated lease-held failures; resumes after babysitter lease release". A second =tracing::info!= fires on resume (=babysitter auto-spawn resumed after backoff reset=).
- *Regression test*: codex confirmed the test path (TASK-ZG01H.1's AC asked for: 10 lease-held failures → assert give-up; release lease; fresh attempt succeeds). Test included in the +267 LOC supervisor.rs change.
- *Gates on merged main =5b11b4d=*: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon ✓ (125 pass — 3 new vs prior 122) | cargo test --workspace ✓ (424 pass — 3 new vs prior 421) | clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings ✓ | fmt ✓ | diff-check ✓ | MSRV 1.78.
- *Bundled with*: TASK-HCFBT.1 (TOCTOU revalidation, MEDIUM) and TASK-HCFBT.2 (virtual-time integration test, LOW) — all three in commit =59af464=. Cargo.toml gained =[dev-dependencies] tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["test-util"] }= for the virtual-time test.

** Description
Worker templates are already hot-reloaded: =spawn_worker_run= reads the worker
=.org= fresh from disk on every dispatch (=load_stage_worker= →
=content::load_worker= → =load_worker_path=, no cache), and =collect_worker_paths=
globs both =shipped/workers/= and =~/.orgasmic/user/workers/= each call. So a user
editing a template's model / provider / driver / effort / persona sees it applied
on the next spawn with no daemon restart — good.

The weakness is *feedback timing*. An invalid edit (unknown model id, unsupported
driver/harness pair, malformed property drawer, missing linked skill) does not
surface until the user actually dispatches, at which point the spawn fails late
with a =WorkerLoad= / parse error. For users who experiment with their own worker
templates frequently, this is a slow, surprising loop.

Add save-time validation so a broken template is flagged before dispatch:
- A dry-run / validate endpoint that loads a worker by id (or accepts inline org
  source), runs the same parse + schema + =driver_for_mode_harness= +
  linked-skill resolution that =spawn_worker_run= uses, and returns structured
  ok/errors WITHOUT acquiring a run.
- Surface it in the worker/template editor UI (inline error on save/edit).
- Optionally extend the existing doctor lint to sweep =workers/*.org= and report
  unresolvable driver/harness, model, or skill references.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [X] A validate endpoint resolves a worker (by id and/or inline source) and returns the same failure classes =spawn_worker_run= would hit (parse error, schema error, unsupported driver/harness, missing skill) as structured results, without spawning a run or holding a lease.
- [X] The worker/template editor surfaces validation errors at save/edit time through the Settings worker pipeline/status surface backed by =GET /workers/validate=.
- [X] Doctor lint (or the validate path) reports unresolvable driver/harness, model, or linked-skill references across =workers/*.org=; this landed as the validate-path sweep endpoint.
- [X] Tests cover a valid template plus each failure class.

- [2026-06-13 Sat] Validation reuses worker parsing/schema, linked-skill resolution, =driver_for_mode_harness=, and driver config validation. Diagnostics cover =parse_error=, =schema_error=, =unsupported_driver_harness=, =missing_skill=, =driver_config=, read/not-found errors.
- [2026-06-13 Sat] Settings worker pipeline now consumes =/workers/validate= and marks invalid workers inline, with expandable diagnostic messages for broken templates.

** Description
Live evidence from both batch-1 dispatches [2026-06-11]:

1. *Release lag*: TASK-CJWT3.1 session JSONL shows =run_complete= ("rmux
   end-of-turn marker observed") at 10:59:40Z but the lifecycle release only
   at 11:09:41Z — exactly the 600s stall window later. TASK-RVEKT shows the
   same pattern. For rmux runs, =run_complete= does not trigger supervisor
   release; the stall detector reaps the lease 10 minutes after the worker
   already finished. Consequence: leases (and redispatch) blocked ~10min per
   run, and the UI shows a live working badge for a worker that has exited.
2. *Mislabeled release reason*: the release event records
   =outcome: completed, reason: stall_timeout_exceeded= — a completed run
   must not carry a stall reason; recovery/telemetry consumers will
   misclassify it.
3. *last.txt content*: both =task-NNN-last.txt= files contain only the
   32-byte marker summary ("rmux end-of-turn marker observed") instead of
   the worker's final message; the real summary is only inside a 15-24MB
   stdout.log. tmux/codex paths write the worker summary — rmux should too
   (TASK-RF3J1.5 family).

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =run_complete= on an rmux run triggers supervisor release promptly
  (test: release event within seconds of run_complete in the session JSONL,
  not after the stall window).
- [ ] Release events for completed runs carry a completion reason, never
  =stall_timeout_exceeded=.
- [ ] =last.txt= for rmux dispatches contains the worker's final summary
  (tail of the worker's last message), not the marker-observation string.
- [ ] Existing stall-detector behavior preserved for genuinely stalled runs
  (regression test).

** Description
Replaces the seven remaining UI placeholders that survived UI Session 4 and lands the routing substrate that the polish-phase 2 endgame depends on. Today =GraphView=, =OrgView=, and =SettingsView= are the only entry points for Decisions, Architecture, Glossary, ADR, Snapshots, Activity, and stage-agent configuration. Per dec_PA23Y, dec_TQZTE, dec_E394G there should be six first-class pages with list rows + back-stack modal + (where applicable) per-page react-flow graph, in addition to the cross-domain Graph that already shipped in Session 4. Per dec_JSX48 the routing substrate becomes TanStack Router with path-for-nav + query-for-modals. =OrgView= ships a CodeMirror-with-org-mode editor (replacing the bare textarea). =SettingsView= grows a stage-agent map editor over the =STAGE_AGENT_*= property group on =project.org=.

This is a large but architecturally well-scoped session: every surface has a clear list-rows + modal-with-back-stack pattern, an existing fetcher (=fetchDecisions/Architecture/Glossary/Adrs/Snapshots= already in =ui/src/lib/api.ts=), and a decided UX (dec_PA23Y..046). The new abstraction is =NodeListView=/=NodeGraphView=/=NodeModal= parameterised by node-kind per dec_PA23Y's user note.

** Description
Addresses reviewer findings F-1 (high), F-2 (medium), F-3 (medium), and F-8 (high) from =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-047-review-report.md=. The TanStack Router migration shipped the path-based routes but the per-page filter state, the modal drawer-stack, and the manager-size query param did not adopt TanStack's =useSearch= / =navigate= contract — instead they kept legacy =useQueryState= writes, =window.history.pushState= calls, or component-local =useState=. This breaks the dec_JSX48 "path + query hybrid, browser-back follows previous filter" contract and prevents deep-linking from reflecting the actual session state.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1 fix.* =NodeModal= drawer-stack management goes through TanStack Router's =useSearch= + =navigate({ search })= instead of =window.location.search= + =window.history.pushState= / =replaceState=. Chip-click inside a modal body pushes a new id onto =?drawer_stack=...= via =navigate=; clicking Back / closing modal pops via =navigate=; browser back/forward respects the stack (TanStack tracks history per its router instance).
- [ ] *F-2 fix.* Esc on a stacked modal pops *one frame* via the same router seam — only deletes the whole stack when the stack is already empty (closing the bottom frame returns to the underlying route). Match the dec_JSX48 user-note browser-back contract: "close modal → previous page → previous filter".
- [ ] *F-3 fix.* =NodeModal= header renders a breadcrumb of opened nodes (e.g., =dec_GRDFB > arch_R3EPE > arch_R3EPE details=). Clicking any crumb pops the stack down to that depth. Single Back icon remains for the one-step pop. The breadcrumb hides on viewports below =sm= (mobile sheet has limited header space) and falls back to "Back" + count.
- [ ] *F-8 fix.* Migrate the search-state holdouts to TanStack:
  - =DecisionsView= filter bar (topic filter, free-text query) reads from =useSearch()= and writes via =navigate({ search })=. Drop the =useQueryState= calls. Same shape for =ArchitectureView= (free-text per TASK-ZYPJC.4) and =ActivityView= (Type / Actor / Date / Task filters; date-range needs a JSON-safe shape).
  - =ManagerPopover= consumes =?manager=peek|workbench|focus= from =useSearch=. The =sessionStorage= persistence stays as a fallback for "last size when no query param", but the URL is authoritative on initial render. Writing the URL on size change is OK — debounce if needed to avoid history spam during drag.
  - Update the route's =validateSearch= schema so type-safe accessors exist.
- [ ] *Manager popover regression check.* Cmd+\` toggle and Esc collapse must still work; drag handles must not race the URL writes (debounce or write only on settle).
- [ ] *No new deps.* TanStack Router is already installed; no =@tanstack/react-router-zod= or similar add-on. Use TanStack's built-in =validateSearch= (function form).
- [ ] =cd ui && npm run build= passes (tsc --noEmit + vite build).
- [ ] =git diff --check= clean.

** Description
Addresses reviewer findings F-4 (medium perf), F-11 (medium design), F-13 (medium design). =NodeModal= currently runs all per-kind fetchers (decisions / architecture / glossary / ADR / three orgFile reads) on every page even when the modal is closed — wasteful network + auth-noise; glossary IDs leak through to modal header chrome and the mobile Sheet description even though dec_E394G requires the canonical name as the primary key in UI; ADR promote/demote actions live only in the row kebab menu and the source decision in the row renders as a passive badge instead of a clickable chip linking into the source decision modal.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-4 fix.* Detail loaders inside =NodeModal= are gated on =open=. When the modal is closed (no =?<kind>= path segment + no top-of-stack id), no fetchers run. When opening from a list page, the matching list response is reused if it already contains the needed fields — only fetch a detail endpoint (=GET /architecture/:id= / =GET /glossary/:id= / =GET /adr/:id=) when the body needs fields that the list summary lacks.
- [ ] *F-11 fix.* Glossary modal hides the raw =:ID:= everywhere user-facing: header shows canonical name only; mobile Sheet description shows canonical name; the back-stack chip uses canonical name. The id stays in the URL =?drawer_stack=glossary-NNN= but is not rendered as a code span anywhere in the UI.
- [ ] *F-13 fix part 1.* ADR row's "Generated from dec_NNN" is a clickable chip that pushes =dec_NNN= onto the drawer stack (opens the source decision modal). Keep the kebab menu for Promote/Demote at the row level.
- [ ] *F-13 fix part 2.* ADR modal header carries Promote + Demote buttons (mirror the row kebab actions). Disabled states: Promote disabled when status is already =accepted=; Demote disabled when status is already =proposed= or =deprecated=. Both fire the existing =postAdrPromote= / =postAdrPromote= helpers with sonner toast feedback.
- [ ] =cd ui && npm run build= passes.
- [ ] =git diff --check= clean.

** Evidence
- [2026-05-23 Sat 18:26] Shipped in bundled fix-implementer commit =8c26232= (merged =6862918=). =NodeModal.tsx= now gates detail loaders on =open= (no fetchers run when stack is empty + nodeId is null); list-page payloads are reused as seed data for the modal body (no re-fetch when the list already carries the needed fields); glossary modal chrome shows canonical name in the header + mobile Sheet description (id stays in URL only); ADR row source-decision is a clickable chip that pushes the source decision id onto the drawer stack via the router seam; ADR modal header carries Promote + Demote buttons with disabled-state logic (Promote disabled at =accepted=; Demote disabled at =proposed= / =deprecated=).
- Verification: =cd ui && npm run build= clean. No network burst on page load.
- Reviewer F-4 (medium perf), F-11 (medium design), F-13 (medium design) closed.

** Description
Addresses reviewer findings F-5 (medium bug), F-6 (medium design), F-7 (medium design). =NodeGraph= secondary edges from architecture nodes try to draw =decision -> architecture= edges even though the graph node set only contains architecture ids — those edges reference missing source nodes and React Flow throws missing-node warnings. The per-page graph only implements double-click to open a modal; dec_PA23Y also requires single-click 1-hop highlight, Enter on the focused node, and a right-click context menu. The dec_NZ9PS mobile matrix is only partially applied: the graph subview remains an inline fixed-height canvas instead of opening as a full-screen Sheet below =md=, and list-row chips/actions stay visible below =sm= instead of degrading.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-5 fix.* =NodeGraph= for architecture only emits secondary =:DECIDES:= back-edges when both endpoints exist in the rendered node set. Currently the source is a decision id not in the architecture node set — change the secondary edge to architecture → motivating-decision id only when that decision id is also in the node set (which it never is in the architecture-only subview); for the architecture subview, surface the motivating decision as a row chip in the side panel instead of a graph edge. No React Flow missing-node warnings.
- [ ] *F-6 fix.* Per-page graph interactions:
  - Single click on a node → 1-hop highlight (TASK-EBWZ9.3 cross-domain Graph pattern). Re-uses the same opacity-25% / opacity-100% logic.
  - Enter key on focused node → opens the modal (the existing double-click behaviour).
  - Right-click on a node → ContextMenu (radix) with "Open modal" + "Open in cross-domain Graph" entries. The latter navigates to =/projects/$projectId/graph= with =?focus=$nodeId= so the cross-domain graph can fitView on that node (cross-domain GraphView accepts =?focus= if it's wired; if not, just navigate without the param — flag in evidence).
- [ ] *F-7 fix part 1.* Below =md=, the per-page graph subview opens as a full-screen Sheet (slides up from bottom) instead of rendering inline. The List/Graph toggle on mobile becomes a button that opens the Sheet. Mirrors TASK-EBWZ9.5's mobile Sheet pattern for the cross-domain graph detail.
- [ ] *F-7 fix part 2.* Below =sm=, list-row chips that are not load-bearing (=kind=, =priority=, ADR badge for non-promoted decisions, snapshot label) hide. =useIsMobile()= hook already exists; reuse it. Row IDs + titles + status pills + Restore/Action buttons stay visible.
- [ ] =cd ui && npm run build= passes; no React Flow missing-node warnings in console.
- [ ] =git diff --check= clean.

** Evidence

New =ui/src/components/ui/context-menu.tsx= +265 (local shadcn/radix ContextMenu primitive).

** Description
Addresses reviewer findings F-9 (medium design), F-10 (low a11y), F-12 (high a11y — nested interactive controls invalid HTML), F-14 (medium bug — no distinct loading state), F-15 (low design — Decisions sort + pill rendering). One coupled pass over =NodeListView= + per-page Views.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-12 fix (high).* =NodeListView= row primitive supports non-nested row actions: split the row into a clickable row body (no =<button>= wrap) + an absolutely-positioned trailing action zone (kebab / chips) that uses =stopPropagation= AND is wired with =onPointerDown=stopPropagation= so the row's click handler doesn't fire. Row body is a =<button>= or =<div role="button" tabIndex={0}>= but the action zone is outside the button element. Validate via DOM inspection: no =<button>= inside =<button>=.
- [ ] *F-9 fix.* Add the missing filter/search bars:
  - =GlossaryView=: free-text search over canonical name + definition. URL-backed (=?q=...=).
  - =AdrView=: status multi-select (proposed / accepted / superseded / deprecated) + free-text search over title. URL-backed.
  - =ArchitectureView=: free-text search over title + interface line. URL-backed.

- [ ] *F-10 fix.* Filter chips on every page (Decisions, Architecture, Activity) carry =aria-controls= pointing at the id of the region they filter (list container, feed container, or graph canvas).
- [ ] *F-14 fix.* Distinct loading state: while =useResource= is pending, render a Skeleton block (shadcn primitive — count ~6 rows) inside =NodeListView= instead of falling through to the empty-state message. Empty-state message renders only when =loading === false && items.length === 0=. Same logic for SnapshotsView and ActivityView.
- [ ] *F-15 fix.* =DecisionsView=:

  - Decision list uses topic/glossary chips only; obsolete chosen-label/status chips are not rendered.
  - Status pill rendered only when status is not =decided= (=question / proposed / superseded= surface; =decided= is the default and visually quiet).

* DONE TASK-ZYWZD node body set silently drops nested headings: a write verb that lost 92 percent of a body and reported success :cli:daemon:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-ZYWZD
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Filed 2026-07-28. `orgasmic node body set` replaces only the free prose between
the property drawer and the first nested heading. A body containing `**`
sub-headings is silently truncated at the first one — TASK-ATAXN was filed with
300 of its 3959 characters and nobody was told. The read side compounds it:
nested `**` sections are NOT returned in the JSON `description` field, so the
loss is invisible through the same surface that caused it. A write verb that
can drop 92% of its payload and report success is the single worst surface in
the CLI.

=== The principle (shared with TASK-HQ970, defect 2)

A writer must not commit what it cannot read back. TASK-HQ970 states it for
`tx record` (re-parse before reporting success); this task applies the same
round-trip guarantee to the node body surface. If the fix grows shared
machinery (compose -> re-parse -> diff-against-intent -> refuse on loss), use
it for both.

=== Work

1. WRITE: `node body set` must either persist the full submitted body
   (including nested `**` headings, correctly re-depthed under the task
   heading) or REFUSE, naming exactly what would be lost ("body contains 3
   nested headings starting at '** The gap'; this verb replaces prose only —
   use ... or restructure with ==="). Never a silent partial write. Same audit
   for `node body append` and any sibling that composes org content.
2. READ: `task get` / `node` reads must expose the full body, or explicitly
   mark elision ("+ 3 nested sections not shown") — never present a truncated
   body as complete. Pick and record one; full exposure preferred.
3. Post-write verification: after composing the new file content, re-parse and
   assert the submitted body round-trips before the write is committed
   (mirrors HQ970's acceptance "a write that would not round-trip is rejected
   rather than committed").

=== Acceptance

- Setting a body containing `** Section` either persists it fully (verified by
  reading the raw org node) or errors naming the offending heading — proven
  both ways in tests.
- The ATAXN shape is the regression fixture: a ~4000-char body with three `**`
  sections survives set + get with zero loss, or is refused up front.
- No silent partial write remains on any `node body` verb (enumerate them in
  the report).
- Injection proof per project standard: restore the truncating behavior, show
  the round-trip test red with output, restore the fix, green.

=== Non-goals

- Do not implement TASK-HQ970 (tx record validation) here; share machinery if
  natural, cross-reference regardless.
- Do not redesign the org body/section model; make the existing surface honest
  about it.

Related: TASK-HQ970 (same round-trip principle on tx record), TASK-XPYRR
(title, the other unwritable field), the recorded gotcha "`node body set`
replaces prose only, so `**` headings in a body are lost".

* CANCELLED TASK-79VKP.6 Bound dispatch build caches without cross-worktree false greens :framework:worktree:build:performance:
:PROPERTIES:
:DEPENDS_ON: TASK-3X5AQ TASK-GRCWC
:ID: TASK-79VKP.6
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

** Description
The TASK-K9WWM final test worker created a separate 1.7 GiB worktree cache and spent 50.71 seconds compiling before one exact assertion test; the warm manager target ran all three exact tests in 7 seconds. TASK-3X5AQ proves that sharing CARGO_TARGET_DIR across checkouts can silently execute another checkout binary, and TASK-GRCWC guards destructive pruning. The remaining build-cache duplication has no implementation owner.

Measure and choose a sound cache strategy that keeps checkout-specific fingerprints and final binaries isolated. Candidate mechanisms must be proved rather than assumed: compiler-object caches such as sccache, immutable dependency seeding followed by private fingerprints, filesystem cloning or hardlinks with copy-on-write validation, bounded worktree slots for disk only, or explicit no-reuse with automatic quota pruning. Never share a mutable Cargo target directory across different checkout paths.

** Acceptance
- Baseline disk, cold build, warm build, and concurrent-build costs are recorded for manager plus at least two worktrees.
- The selected design cannot make an edited worktree report Fresh or run a binary built from another checkout; reproduce the TASK-3X5AQ negative control.
- Cache storage is bounded and attributable per project, and cleanup observes TASK-GRCWC safety.
- A TASK-K9WWM-shaped one-file test correction materially reduces duplicate compile time and disk without weakening test identity.

** Description
Follow-up to TASK-EBVHJ. The =ConnectGate= "Advanced →" button calls =goView('settings')=, but =pathForView= (=AppShell.tsx= ~136) falls back to =/board= whenever =projectId= is null, and Settings is only project-scoped (=/projects/$projectId/settings=). So for the exact target user — a fresh tunnel visitor with no project selected — "Advanced →" lands on =/board= instead of Settings, where they can't adjust baseUrl/profiles before connecting.

Pick the smallest coherent fix:
1. Add a global, project-independent Settings route (e.g. =/settings=) the gate can always reach (the connection/profile section needs no project); OR
2. If a global route is too invasive pre-MVP, hide/disable "Advanced →" in =ConnectGate= when there is no active project (so the button never dead-ends), and surface profile/baseUrl editing inline in the gate instead.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] From a projectless origin, the visitor can reach connection/profile settings (baseUrl + token) without first selecting a project — OR the dead-end affordance is removed and equivalent control lives in the gate.
- [X] No regression to TASK-EBVHJ's blocking token flow; =npm --prefix ui run build= + =tsc --noEmit= green.

** Evidence
Chose option 1 (global route — cleaner than hiding the affordance, and =SettingsView= already handles =projectId: null= by disabling the project-config section). Implemented directly by the manager (trivial ~16-line scope), landed on main in =cbe7c6e=: new root-level =globalSettingsRoute= (path =settings=) → =<SettingsView projectId={null}/>= in =ui/src/app/router.tsx= (added to =routeTree=); =pathForView= in =AppShell.tsx= now returns =/settings= for =goView('settings')= when =projectId= is null (else the existing =/projects/$projectId/settings=). So "Advanced →" and the header settings button both reach Settings projectless. Gates: =tsc --noEmit= + =npm run build= green. Browser click-through unverified this session (no browser-automation tool).

*Reverted (cancelled).* On operator review (screenshot), the =ConnectGate= "Advanced →" button was removed entirely (=9d688fe=): it was added scope beyond the original ask AND subtly broken — =ConnectGate= is a blocking Radix modal, so navigating to settings left the overlay on top, blocking the page it opened; and a tunnel visitor's =baseUrl= defaults to same-origin, so only the token is needed. With the button gone, this task's premise (make its target reachable) no longer applies, so the global =/settings= route + =pathForView= branch were reverted in the same commit. The modal is now just token input + Connect. Net effect of TASK-K3Y04 on the tree: nil.

** Description
Closes TASK-M5JTN reviewer F-2: Item 1's path (c) (accumulate all system "thinking delta" chunks into the summary) produces noisy last.txt on live cursor-agent implementer dispatches (composer-2.5-fast emits 500+ raw thinking chunks with no terminal event). Path (a) — driver synthesizes a =DriverEvent::RunComplete { summary }= on clean subprocess exit when no terminal was emitted — is the correct long-term fix. The reviewer confirmed feasibility: =cursor.rs= already has =terminal_emitted=, =emit_run_complete_once=, =translate_result=; =subprocess_stream_json.rs= currently emits nothing on successful exit when =!terminal_emitted()= (lines 276-286).

After path (a) ships, the system-text fallback in =dispatch_last_summary_from_session= becomes redundant for cursor-agent dispatches (the synthetic =run_complete= will win precedence). Decision: keep the system fallback in place as a defense-in-depth for other drivers that might exhibit the same emission pattern, OR remove it once path (a) is verified comprehensive — defer that judgment to this implementer.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] In =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/subprocess_stream_json.rs= (or =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/cursor.rs=, depending on architectural fit), synthesize a =DriverEvent::RunComplete { summary }= when: (a) subprocess exits with status 0, (b) no terminal session marker (=RunComplete=, =Lifecycle::Release=) has been emitted, and (c) some content was accumulated during the run. * CANCELLED TASK-Q07Y5 WGXKD.2 fix round: bound writer shutdown and derive ExitTimeOut from the real budget :dispatch:daemon:cli:fix:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-Q07Y5
:PRIORITY: P0
:END:

Fix round for the reviewer BLOCK SHIP on TASK-WGXKD.2 (merged `6a518f3`).
Reviewer: reviewer-codex-rmux (rmux / codex / gpt-5.6-sol / high),
run-20260728T103240, reported tx-20260728-orgasmic-3136, closed
tx-20260728-orgasmic-3137.

The merged change is NOT reverted. Its central claim held under review: `try_admit`
checks `closed` and inserts the admission under the same `watch::Sender` write
lock, `post_run_release` acquires it before its first await, the admission moves
into the detached task so cancellation retains ownership through `Drop`, and no
sole handle is taken before a cancellable await. `daemon restart` does parse the
real `/daemon/restart` response with a 40s client ceiling, SIGTERM and Ctrl+C both
route through `RunningDaemon.shutdown`, and the macOS plist is rewritten on every
service start (`start_macos_launch_agent` writes it before bootstrap), not only on
install. All independent gates exited 0 at `ca3f9df`.

What follows is what the round claimed and did not establish.

** 1. HIGH — `ExitTimeOut 60` is not larger than the worst-case shutdown, because
   half of that shutdown has no budget at all

`crates/orgasmic-cli/src/daemon_service.rs:707-727`,
`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/lib.rs:665-688`,
`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/writer.rs:513-522`.

After SIGTERM, `RunningDaemon` waits up to 20s for release finalizations and then
calls `WriterHandle::shutdown().await`. That call queues behind prior writer
commands and awaits its reply **with no timeout**. `RESTART_WRITER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT`
bounds only the pre-stop marker, not `WriterHandle::shutdown`.

Concrete failure: a terminal-tx append is still blocked in writer I/O or fsync
when the 20s release drain expires; shutdown then waits behind that append, and
launchd sends SIGKILL at 60s while the append is still non-durable. That
recreates the released-but-unreported loss the whole WGXKD family exists to
prevent.

The comment at daemon_service.rs:707 reasons "drain (20s) + writer shutdown < 60",
but the second term is unbounded, so the inequality is unprovable rather than
generous. The budget test added in this round checks 40 > 20 + 5 and 35 > 20 — it
never proves the plist timeout covers writer shutdown.

**This is live on the operator's machine right now.** The plist was rewritten with
`ExitTimeOut 60` on 2026-07-28 (tx-20260728-orgasmic-3118); the window is wider
than it was, and still not closed.

Required: give writer shutdown an explicit finite budget and a durable timeout
outcome, then **derive** the service-manager timeout from release drain + writer
shutdown + margin rather than hard-coding 60. If the derived number differs from
60, the plist must carry the derived one, and a test must assert the plist value
is the derived value — not a literal.

** 2. LOW — the production lifecycle composition still has no end-to-end regression

`crates/orgasmic-cli/src/daemon_lifecycle.rs:1498-1563`,
`crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/daemon_lifecycle.rs:99-181`.

The >5s test uses a stand-in HTTP server and stops after parsing its response; the
SIGTERM test has no in-flight release. Both pass even if the real `daemon restart`
sequence parses the drain response and then has launchd cut off the old daemon
during writer shutdown — which is exactly finding 1.

Required: drive the actual lifecycle restart path with a release lasting beyond
five seconds, including service stop and replacement bind. Testing the HTTP wait
and the SIGTERM routing in isolation is what let finding 1 through.

** Acceptance

- `WriterHandle::shutdown` has a finite budget and a defined outcome on timeout;
  the outcome is durable or recoverable, not silent.
- The macOS `ExitTimeOut` is derived from the drain and writer budgets, and a test
  asserts the rendered plist carries the derived value.
- A SIGTERM test holds a terminal-tx append in flight through the release timeout
  and proves either durability before exit, or a durable run-specific recovery
  record written before the watchdog can kill the daemon.
- An end-to-end restart regression covers service stop and replacement bind with a
  release that outlasts five seconds.

** Non-goals

- Do not revert `6a518f3`. Its atomic-admission fix is sound and reviewed.
- Reviewer finding 2 (old CLI → new daemon terminal-tx race) is **out of scope**
  and filed separately. It is pre-existing from TASK-WGXKD.1 and the reviewer
  states it does not block this round.

* CANCELLED TASK-RRVX0 TASK-35TK4 fix: eliminate CLI lock-probe acquisition race :fix:daemon:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-RRVX0
:PRIORITY: high
:READ_SCOPE: .orgasmic/gotchas.org,crates/orgasmic-daemon,crates/orgasmic-cli
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon && cargo test -p orgasmic-cli
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon,crates/orgasmic-cli
:END:

** Description
Claude Opus review of b18808c..bd3d7bd returned SHIP but identified one medium new regression: the CLI lock-state probe briefly acquires daemon.lock exclusively, while daemon startup makes a single nonblocking exclusive-lock attempt. A microsecond overlap can make a legitimate booting daemon misclassify the CLI probe as an unhealthy incumbent and exit.

** Acceptance Criteria
- Daemon lock acquisition tolerates the CLI probe transient without weakening single-instance exclusion or spawning work before lock ownership.
- Retry behavior is tightly bounded (roughly 100-150 ms total), handles only WouldBlock, and preserves immediate propagation of other filesystem/lock errors.
- Deterministic regression forces the overlap and proves the daemon eventually acquires after the probe releases; a continuously held incumbent still fails closed.
- Preserve Rust 1.87 compatibility by calling fs2::FileExt methods explicitly.
- Run focused lock/autostart/double-serve tests, cargo fmt --all --check, cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon, cargo test -p orgasmic-cli, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; classify known baseline watcher/bootstrap flakes separately.
** Notes
The two originally assigned Codex gpt-5.6-terra/high attempts were interrupted by shared daemon restarts and produced no edits. A concurrently dispatched equivalent fix completed under TASK-870YX: commit 4c0a151, merged to main as e4b6b7b. Manager independently reran the focused daemon-lock, CLI boot-owner, and double-serve regressions; all passed. This duplicate record is cancelled as superseded, not left as an unfixed defect.

* CANCELLED TASK-TH906 manager dispatch --effort is silently dropped for every non-claude harness, and the ledger records it as fact anyway
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-TH906
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

** Description
=orgasmic manager dispatch --harness codex --effort high= records =:EFFORT: high=
on the =manager.dispatch_started= tx and =:EFFORT_OVERRIDE: high= on the
=run.created= tx, *and never passes the value to the harness.*

=crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs:989-994= pushes =--effort= only inside
the =if is_claude= block. The non-claude branch at =:1004-1011= pushes =--model=
and nothing else:

: if matches!(harness, "codex" | "cursor-agent" | "hermes") {
:     if let Some(model) = cfg.model.as_ref() { … push "--model" … }
: }

=modes/rmux.rs:1817-1828= has the identical shape — model for everyone, effort
for claude only.

*And =--effort= is not even the right flag for codex.* =codex --help=
(codex-cli 0.144.5) exposes =-m/--model= and =-c/--config <key=value>=; there is
no =--effort=. Reasoning effort is =-c model_reasoning_effort="high"=. So the
push would not have worked had it been reached.

** Measured, not inferred
Dispatch =tx-20260808-orgasmic-5485= (TASK-2QK4P.1.1.1 reviewer, codex, tmux) was
given =--model gpt-5.6-sol --effort high=. Both tx entries record =high=. The
worker's own pane footer read:

: gpt-5.6-sol xhigh · ~/.orgasmic/worktrees/orgasmic/task-2qk4p.1.1.1-review

=~/.codex/config.toml= on this machine carries =model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"=,
which is what the run actually used. *The flag was dropped and the ledger asserts
otherwise.*

** Why this is P1
1. *The ledger is the product's evidence surface.* An effort recorded but not
   applied makes every dispatch comparison across efforts meaningless, and there
   is no way to tell after the fact which runs honoured the flag.
2. *The manager protocol echoes driver/harness/model/effort after each dispatch.*
   That echo is read by the operator as a statement of what ran. It was false
   here and the manager had no way to know.
3. It is silent. No warning, no refusal, no =unsupported=.

** Acceptance
1. Either PASS the effort to every harness that accepts one — for codex that is
   =-c model_reasoning_effort=<value>=, not =--effort= — or REFUSE the dispatch
   by name when the harness cannot take it. Do not record a value that was not
   applied.
2. If a harness genuinely has no effort control, =dispatch= must say so at
   dispatch time and the tx must not carry =EFFORT=/=EFFORT_OVERRIDE=.
3. Same treatment for =--model= on any harness that ignores it, and the same
   audit for the =rmux= path, which has the identical claude-only gate.
4. A regression per supported harness asserting the launch argv actually carries
   the requested effort, or that the dispatch was refused. =tmux.rs:3238-3255=
   already does this for claude; it has no codex counterpart, which is why the
   gap survived.
5. Check whether =cursor-agent= and =hermes= have effort controls too — they are
   in the same =matches!= arm.

** Notes
Observed on runtime =ed0ebbc=, codex-cli 0.144.5, 2026-08-08.
